## 2026-09-10 — html2pdf retry helper (production incident: Ryan Yeaton 59334 membership receipt 403)

**BACKEND ONLY — `vfo-admin-api` **`v823`** — deployed 2026-09-10, edge PR #226 (`ea6a814` on main), tag `backend-good-2026-09-10-v823`, **smoke 5/5 vs `v823`** (Jake). One new file, seventeen edited; no frontend change of any kind, so no `npm run build`, no `npm run deploy` and deliberately NO `live-N` tag.** Gates at ship: `deno check --no-lock` **0 errors**; **action count unmoved at 494** (6 + 488, the hub's anchored greps) — no action added, renamed or removed; **no migration, no DDL, no policy, no DB function, no `email_templates` row, no cron change**, so the **security advisor was NOT re-run** (the hub's rule, not an omission: this branch touches no table, no policy and no function); `boldsign-webhook` **untouched**; `router/dispatch.ts`, `middleware/*` and every HTTP chain call untouched. `git diff --stat`: **17 files changed, 62 insertions(+), 191 deletions(-)** plus the new `utils/html2pdf.ts`.

### What broke

`membership-sweep-daily` (jobid 16, **12:00 UTC**) charged **four** members inside **one second** on 2026-09-10. Each successful charge chains `automation_MEMBERSHIP_invoicereceipt`, and that handler renders **two** PDFs through `https://api.html2pdf.app/v1/generate` — so the burst put **eight renders through the service in about four seconds**. One of them was refused: **`membership invoice/receipt: receipt PDF generation FAILED — status 403`** at **12:00:08.787Z**, on **Ryan Yeaton — member 59334, plan 61, `member_payment_schedule` row 381, $792, card**.

**The key was valid.** The other three members' invoice *and* receipt renders succeeded on the same credential seconds either side, and 24 hours of logs contain **exactly one** PDF 403. This was a **rate/concurrency refusal returned as 403**, not an auth failure.

**The damage is entirely about where in the handler it landed.** `actions/membership/invoice-receipt.ts` reserves its accounting numbers first, renders second, drafts third, files the vault PDFs fourth and stamps the ledger row last. `renderPdf` had **no retry**, so the 403 became a 500 from the render step — **after** `allocateDocNumber` had reserved **`INV-59334-0001` / `REC-59334-0001`** (`document_numbers` rows **496 / 497**) and **before** the Gmail draft, before the two vault PDFs, and before `invoice_number` / `receipt_number` / `docs_emailed_at` were written to row 381. The result: money taken, numbers spent, ledger row blank, no documents, no email — **and nothing that would ever retry it.** Stripe already had its 200 two chain hops upstream (#327's redelivery only fires when *we* time out, never on a prompt 500) and the sweep re-drafts nothing. **#282's reservation guard could not catch it either** — that guard fires when the reservation *fails*; here it succeeded and the render after it died.

### Repair (done by hand, 2026-09-10)

Two steps, in this order, because the order is the whole point:

1. **The reserved numbers were written onto row 381 first**, `docs_emailed_at` left **NULL**. The handler reads `primary.invoice_number || null` / `primary.receipt_number || null` before allocating, so a row carrying the numbers makes a re-run **reuse** them — a blank row would have minted `-0002` and orphaned `-0001` permanently. `docs_emailed_at` had to stay unset because it is the handler's own "already sent" early return.
2. **The action was re-fired through the cron job's own stored command** — a `DO $$` block that reads `command` from `cron.job` for **jobid 16**, `replace()`s the JSON body with this row's arguments and `EXECUTE`s the resulting `net.http_post`, so **the service-role key never left the database**. Same manoeuvre as the **2026-09-02** entry below (re-drafting deleted tax-revshare sweep emails by NULLing the once-only stamp and executing jobid 5's stored command).

**Result at 14:40:53Z:** the Gmail draft and both vault PDFs landed, and the `-0001` numbers were kept.

### The code change

**New `supabase/functions/vfo-admin-api/utils/html2pdf.ts`** — `renderHtmlToPdf(html: string, label: string, extra?: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<ArrayBuffer | null>`. It POSTs `{ apiKey: Deno.env.get("HTML2PDF_API_KEY"), html, output: "pdf", ...extra }` and makes **3 attempts**, waiting **1500 ms then 3000 ms with ±20% jitter** — the jitter is load-bearing, because the failure mode is a *simultaneous* burst and un-jittered retries would re-collide. It retries **403 / 429 / 5xx** and thrown fetch errors, logs **every** failed attempt as `html2pdf <label>: attempt N/3 FAILED — status S`, and returns `null` after the last. **Other 4xx do not retry** (400 bad HTML, 401 bad key, 404, 413 too large — they answer identically every time).

**All 20 direct call sites across 17 action files were migrated to it**, and the `ArrayBuffer | null` return contract was chosen precisely so that **each caller's existing failure handling is unchanged** — its log line, its `throw`, its `return json(..., 500)`, its bell. The sites: `accountant/invoice-receipt`, `accountant/send-agreement`, `advisor/invoice-receipt`, `advisor/send-agreement`, `agreements/pdf-draft`, `membership/invoice-receipt`, `msm/pip-invoice-receipt` (×2), `onboarding/agreement-send`, `onboarding/bg-receipt`, `onboarding/license-invoice-receipt`, `pipeline/contract-invoice-receipt` (×2), `pipeline/contract-send-agreement`, `specialist-revenue/invoice-receipt`, `tax/final-retainer-receipt`, `tax/implementation-receipt`, `tax/invoice-receipt` (×2), `tax/send-agreement`. **Five of them pass `{ format: "Letter", margin: 0 }` through `extra`** — the four agreement senders (`accountant`, `advisor`, `onboarding` specialist, `pipeline` MAP 1) plus `tax/send-agreement`; every other site was already the plain `output: "pdf"` body. The seven handlers that pre-check the var themselves (`"HTML2PDF_API_KEY not configured"`) **kept that guard** — the helper reads the env itself, but removing a caller's own 500 would have been a behaviour change. `utils/html-templates.ts` and `utils/membership-html-templates.ts` matched the URL grep only in **comments** and needed no change.

**Post-migration proof:** `grep -rn "api.html2pdf.app" --include=*.ts .` returns `utils/html2pdf.ts` and the two comment lines only — no handler names the endpoint any more.

### What is NOT proven

**The retry arm has never fired in production.** No live 403 has been retried; the helper's retry path is **code-only** until the next sweep burst collides. Gotcha **#483** carries the incident, the repair recipe and the rule.

## 2026-09-09 (3rd branch) — Looking at a payment page is not failing to make one: the `canceled` widening gets a booking gate (hotfix)

**BACKEND ONLY — `vfo-admin-api` **`v822`**, a one-predicate hotfix to `router/webhooks.ts`. No frontend change of any kind, so no `npm run build`, no `npm run deploy` and deliberately NO `live-N` tag.** One file, one hunk. **Action count unmoved at 494** — no action added, renamed or removed. `deno check` **0**; **smoke 5/5 vs `v822`** (Jake). Route pages unmoved at **34**; crons unmoved at **17**; `send_mode=true` unmoved at **31**; `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **`v40`**. **No migration, no DDL, no policy, no DB function, no `email_templates` row, no cron change — so the security advisor was NOT re-run, which is the hub's rule and not an omission: this branch touches no table, no policy and no function.** Gates: `deno check` **0 errors** / action count **493** / **smoke to be recorded against `v822`**.

### What broke

The 2026-09-08 branch (`v815` → `v817`, gotcha **#475**) widened the `payment_intent.payment_failed` block so it also runs for **`payment_intent.canceled`** on MAP 1 / TAX metadata shapes. The reason was sound: when an ACH micro-deposit verification is never completed, Stripe cancels the PaymentIntent after ~10 business days and emits `canceled`, **not** `payment_failed`, and without the widening the row would sit at `'processing'` forever with no bell and no client email.

**What was not costed is that Stripe mints the PaymentIntent when a Checkout page is OPENED, not when the payer submits.** A client who clicks a durable `/pay` or `/tax-pay` link, selects *"US bank account"*, looks at the form and closes the tab leaves a live PI behind carrying our full metadata. That session expires unpaid **24 hours** later and emits **`checkout.session.expired`** followed by **`payment_intent.canceled` with `cancellation_reason: 'automatic'`** — byte-for-byte the shape of the micro-deposit expiry the widening was written for. **`cancellation_reason` cannot distinguish them; both are `automatic`.**

The generic first-payment branch then acted, because its only guard was `target.currentStatus !== "succeeded"` — a test that asks *"is this row unpaid?"*, which is true of every row nobody has ever touched.

**Pat Hurst — client 123, `client_tax_plans` 87, retainer $6,750, `fee_process_version 2026-08-25`** — opened his durable `/tax-pay` link and chose ACH **twice on 2026-09-08 (19:08Z and 21:09Z)** without submitting. The expiries arrived on **2026-09-09 at 13:58Z (×2, redelivered) and 15:59Z**, each pair `checkout.session.expired` + `payment_intent.canceled (automatic)`. Each one flipped **`retainer_status` NULL → `'failed'`** and raised `FAILURE_first_payment_declined` — **notification 1898**, *"… canceled (automatic)"*. `actions/tax/stripe-checkout.ts` (~line 62) treats **any truthy `retainer_status` outside the recovery states** as *"Payment already completed"*, so **his link went dead**: the single surface he had to pay through, closed by the act of looking at it.

**Census across the estate: exactly one client hit** — one `retainer_status='failed'` row and **zero** `pay1_status='failed'` rows. **The exposure window is exactly one day**: before `v815`-`v817` this event was ignored for TAX / MAP 1 altogether.

### Remediation (already done, by hand)

`client_tax_plans` 87's `retainer_status` was reset to **NULL** by SQL at **~18:30Z on 2026-09-09**, guarded on **`retainer_payment_intent_id IS NULL`** so the write could not possibly clobber a row that had a real booking behind it — the same evidence the code fix now gates on, used as the safety on the repair:

```sql
update client_tax_plans set retainer_status = null
 where id = 87 and retainer_payment_intent_id is null;
```

His link works again. **Nothing was re-sent and no client contact was needed** — the link is durable, so restoring the column restored the page.

### The fix (`v822`)

In the generic first-payment branch of `router/webhooks.ts`:

```ts
const cancelWithoutBooking = event.type === "payment_intent.canceled" && target?.currentStatus !== "processing";
```

When true the branch **logs and ignores** (`… not booked, abandoned Checkout page — ignored`); otherwise it behaves exactly as before. **A canceled PaymentIntent is a failed payment only when the row was booked `'processing'` against it** — `'processing'` is written by `checkout.session.completed` at submit time and means the debit is in flight, which is precisely the micro-deposit case the widening exists to serve. The row's own booking is the evidence a payment was submitted; **the event is not**.

**`payment_intent.payment_failed` behaviour is unchanged** — that event only exists once a charge was actually attempted, so it needs no booking test. **The three late-ACH arms were never exposed**: MAP 1 P2-4, Tax implementation and Tax final retainer already required `=== "processing"`. The generic first-payment arm was the only one without a booking test, because until the 2026-09-08 widening it had only ever seen `payment_failed`.

Gotcha **#482** (*a canceled PaymentIntent is not a failed payment unless the row was booked against it*), which also narrows **#475** point (4) in place. `flows/stripe-webhook.md` gains the `'processing'` gate under Branch C, and `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md`'s *First payment declined* trigger cell was corrected — it still named `payment_intent.payment_failed` alone.

## 2026-09-09 (2nd branch) — Five misc portal edits and one sub-fix: an account id stops meaning a payable account, a charge date stops being editable as one, and a seven-character rename breaks three slides

**BACKEND SHIPPED — `vfo-admin-api` **`v819` → `v820`** (all five items) **→ `v821`** (the deck-template pointer alone, `actions/tax/generate-presentation.ts`). The FRONTEND is NOT YET PUBLISHED at the time of writing (`npm run deploy` owed), so there is no `live-N` tag yet.** Fourteen edge files (two new: `utils/connect-payout-readiness.ts`, `actions/gc/update-subscription-date.ts`), two new build scripts under `scripts/roi-presentation/`, and four react files (`AdminPortal.jsx`, `MembersPanel.jsx`, `MemberOverviewPanel.jsx`, `GCMarketplaceViews.jsx`). **Action count 493 → 494** — one action ADDED (`gc_update_subscription_date`), none renamed or removed. Route pages unmoved at **34**; crons unmoved at **17**; `send_mode=true` unmoved at **31**; `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **`v40`**. **No migration, no DDL, no policy, no DB function, no `email_templates` row, no cron change — so the security advisor was deliberately NOT re-run.** Gates against the shipping version: `deno check` **0 errors** / action count **494** (6 + 488) / `npm run build` **exit 0, 34 route pages** / **smoke 5/5 vs `v820`**, run by Jake. **`v821` was not smoke-gated, and that is a rule not an omission:** its only delta from `v820` is one handler file and its `TEMPLATE_OBJECT` constant, which the hub's gate table classes as an isolated single-handler change.

Five unrelated asks in one chat. Three of them turn out to be the same shape — **a stored value being read as something it is not**: an account id read as a payable account, a charge date read as a start date, a fixed-width text box read as text.

---

### 1 — An account id is not a payable account (`v820`, edge): the #159 closure for Tax and MAP 1

`actions/tax/revshare.ts` and `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts` both branched their member leg on a bare `!member.stripe_account_id`. **That test has been wrong since Express accounts entered the system.** The admin's *"Set Up Payment Details"* button creates the account the instant it is clicked, so `stripe_account_id` is populated the moment somebody ASKS a member to onboard — long before the member can receive anything. The transfer then went out to a half-built account, Stripe refused it (*"your destination account needs … capabilities enabled: transfers"*), and both engines booked that as a generic transfer **`Failed`** with an action-required bell, re-raised every night, describing a state no admin could act on. It fired for real on **2026-09-03 at 02:30:03Z** — Lisa Sheeran (member 20027), plan 91's `$2,443.75` retainer leg — and sat there for six days.

**The new branch order, identical in both engines:** the member-standing hold branch (unchanged) → **`!stripe_account_id || (STRIPE_KEY && !payable)`** → the `!STRIPE_KEY` env-var `Failed` branch (now reachable only when an account id exists, i.e. exactly the rows it always served) → the transfer. `payable` comes from the new **`utils/connect-payout-readiness.ts`**:

- **`connectTransfersActive(acctId, key)`** — `GET /v1/accounts/{id}`, true **only** when `capabilities.transfers === 'active'`; false on no id, no key, a network error or any non-active answer, and **it never throws**, because a probe failure must not take down a payout run. A Stripe outage therefore parks a leg for one night and self-heals.
- **`connectSetupLinkSent(member)`** — `!!members.connect_setup_email_sent_at`, the stamp `actions/members/stripe-connect-request.ts` writes when the payout-setup email goes out.

`utils/specialist-revenue-payout.ts` had carried the identical probe **inline since 2026-08-24**; it now imports the shared one. That extraction is behaviour-identical and is the **#453** rule applied — the second copy of a check is the one that goes stale.

**The money and the bell are gated separately, and that is the interesting half.** Both arms park the leg at **`AWAITING_CONNECT`** (*"Awaiting Connect Setup"*), which is non-terminal and already picked up by both nightly sweeps — Tax's `isRetry` lists it, MAP 1's `resolved` test is a positive allowlist that excludes it — so the share pays itself on the first tick after the member finishes onboarding, with no human in the loop (**#303**: never route a conditional payout to a terminal value). The **bell** follows the ASK instead: its whole instruction is *"click Set Up Payment Details"*, so once `connect_setup_email_sent_at` is stamped there is nothing left to ask and the engine **stays silent** — and `clearJakeFailure()`s **both** the held title and the older `Revenue share transfer FAILED — <client>` title, retiring the noise an earlier run minted. Where no link has been sent the bell is raised as before, its MESSAGE branching on which case it is (*"has not finished onboarding"* vs *"no Stripe payout account"*) while its **TITLE is untouched**, because the title is the clear contract (**#365/#411**).

**PIP was deliberately left out, and not for want of time.** `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts` writes `pip_rev_share_status='Pending'` on failure, and the 02:00 sweep's PIP pass releases **HELD** statuses only — `Pending` is excluded by design. Parking a PIP leg non-terminally would therefore **strand** it, and its failure bell is the only thing chasing it. A user-informed decision, recorded so nobody "finishes the job" later without changing the sweep first.

**VERIFIED LIVE.** After the `v820` deploy, the `tax-revshare-sweep-daily` cron's **own stored command** was executed in a `DO` block at ~18:0xZ on 2026-09-09. Plan **91** (Michael Lorente, client 131; member Lisa Sheeran 20027, `acct_1UBEcMRyIBJ7Ds0T`, un-onboarded, `connect_setup_email_sent_at` 2026-09-02) moved `retainer_rev_paid` from **`Failed`** to **`Awaiting Connect Setup`**, bells **1729** and **1784** flipped `read=true`, **zero** new bells were raised for client 131, and Jake confirmed both gone from his bell. **The `$2,443.75` is still owed** and pays on the first sweep after Lisa completes onboarding.

**Not exercised:** the **MAP 1 arm** (only the Tax engine fired), the *"account exists but is not payable AND no link has been sent"* message variant, a Stripe outage during the probe, and the env-var-missing `Failed` branch. **New gotcha #479.**

### 2 — Two bells for one person about one file (`v820`, edge)

An ICG (vault-assess group) planner dropping a PDF into a client's vault while the assess form is still outstanding sent the assigned PF **two** bells about the same file: the action-required *"Tax Assessment PDF added for «client»"* (do something) and the dismissible *"«planner» dropped a document in «client»'s vault"* FYI beside it.

`utils/assess-vault-stamp.ts maybeStampAssessVaultUpload` now returns **`Promise<boolean>`** — true **iff** it actually raised that bell, false on every early return and on a throw — and `actions/vault/gen-upload-url.ts` + `actions/vault/tax-admin-upload-url.ts` pass that answer into `notifyPlannerVaultDrop` as a new sixth parameter **`suppressPf`** (default **false**), which nulls the assigned PF for that one FYI. **Tracy is never suppressed** — she does not receive the action-required bell, so hers stays the only signal that a file landed. Every other case is byte-identical: a later ICG drop, a drop once the form is in, any non-ICG planner, any member drop through `notifyMemberVaultDrop`.

The structural point is that **"have I already told this person?" is a question only the earlier notifier can answer**, so it returns the fact rather than having the second consumer re-derive three conditions it would eventually disagree about. It required **reordering the two minters** — the stamp now runs BEFORE the notify, where `flows/notifications.md` correctly said it used to run after. They are independent and each carries its own try/catch, so the swap changes nothing else, but the ordering is now load-bearing and is commented as such at both call sites. **Code-only: no ICG drop has happened since the deploy. New gotcha #481.**

### 3 — Engagement level: private to admins, and it stops looking unsaved (`v820`, both repos)

Three separate faults on one field.

- **`actions/data/load-data.ts`** returned `engagement_level` to every logged-in caller. It is an internal rating **of** the member, in the whitelisted `members` blob the whole portal receives, so it now reads `isAdmin ? value : null` — the same treatment and the same reason as `notes` beside it (**#445**, the additive-whitelist half). Both of its readers are admin surfaces.
- **It looked unsaved after a tab switch, and the DB write had always landed.** `AdminPortal` fetches `allMembers` **once**; `MemberOverviewPanel` held the new value in optimistic local state, which died on unmount, so switching tabs and coming back re-rendered the stale fetched row. The panel now takes an **`onPatchMember`** prop and calls it after a successful `member_save_engagement`; `AdminPortal.patchMember(memberNumber, patch)` patches that one row inside `allMembers`. (Two members already carried `highly_engaged` from earlier, which is how the symptom was reproducible at all.)
- **The rating is now visible where people look at a member.** `MemberOverviewPanel` exports `ENGAGEMENT` + `engagementMeta`, and `MembersPanel` renders an engagement **pill** (dot colour + label from that shared list) on the profile hero's meta line after the status dot — **admin surface only**, which the `load_data` change now guarantees rather than merely arranges.

**Plus a navigation fix that is really a state-provenance fix.** `MembersPanel` exports **`MEMBER_PROFILE_ORIGIN_KEY`** (`'adminMemberProfileOrigin'`, sessionStorage). `AdminPortal.openMemberProfile(m, feature, origin = null)` writes the key when an origin is passed and **clears** it otherwise, and **only the Member Overview list passes one** (`'member_overview'`); a directory row click clears it, so it can never go stale. A new `onBackToOrigin` prop is threaded `AdminPortal` → `MembersPanel` → `Advisors`/`Accountants`/`StrategicMembersPanel` → `MemberDirectoryView`, and *"← Back to list"* reads **and clears** the key, calling `onBackToOrigin('member_overview')` — which `AdminPortal.backToProfileOrigin` turns into `setActiveTab('member_overview')` plus a `navClickCount` bump. With no key it behaves exactly as before.

**Verified by Jake on the dev server against `v820`:** the value persists across a tab switch, the pill renders on the admin profile (Test Member 59524, set `highly_engaged` by SQL for the test), the pill is **absent from a member login**, and Back-to-list returns to Member Overview from there while staying in Advisors when opened from Advisors. **Note for the next reader:** 59524 is member_type *'VFO Reconciliation (Free)'*, which `MemberOverviewPanel`'s `EXCLUDED_TYPES` hides on purpose — that is why it does not appear in the overview list itself.

### 4 — The ROI deck: v7 renamed a header, and the rename broke three slides (`v820` then `v821`, edge + bucket)

**Two template versions in one day, and the second exists because the first shipped a rendering bug no assertion in the package can see.**

**v7** (`scripts/roi-presentation/make_v7.py`, base = the live v6, sha `1d8995d2…`, 27,614,765 B) did exactly one thing: *"Your investment in VFO Specialists:"* → *"Your investment in VFO **Tax** Specialists:"* on slides 24/28/29, one `<a:t>` run each, with the sibling *"Your investment in VFO Services:"* deliberately untouched and asserted absent-of-change three times. Uploaded (`c3306a89…`, 27,614,772 B, round-trip verified) and shipped in `v820`. **Jake's first real deck showed the longer header WRAPPING onto a second line and OVERLAPPING the *"Plan Investment:"* row, on all three slides.** Shape 1528's box was fixed-width. **A wording change on a fixed-width box is a geometry change** — and nothing in the pipeline renders anything, so the token guard, the shape counts and the sum identities all passed.

**v8** (`make_v8.py`, base = v7) fixes it and takes one more liberty while it is in there:

1. **Shape 1528 is wider and cannot wrap.** `cx 4363200 → 5155530` EMU — a **measured** bound, not a rendered one (Inter is not installed locally) — **and** its `bodyPr` goes `wrap="square"` → `wrap="none"` with `<a:spAutoFit/>` replaced by `<a:noAutofit/>`. The autofit swap is the part worth remembering: autofit lets an editor opening the deck re-fit the box's `cy`, and `cy` is what the handler's Y-threshold constants are measured against. The sibling shape 1517 already carried `noAutofit`, which is the tell that this is the house pattern.
2. **Label and value are ONE text box per fee row.** Each value shape was merged into its label shape and deleted — **1527 into 1526** (*"Total Fee: ${{PLANNING_FEE}}"*; on slide 29 the literal *"Total Fee: $0"*, still no `PLANNING_FEE_Y2`), **1531 into 1530**, **1533 into 1532**, **1536 into 1535** (slides 24/28 only). Appended runs reuse the label run's `rPr`, the label's `pPr` is kept, and the merged `cx` is widened. **No `off`/`y`/`cy` changes anywhere.**

`make_v8.py` asserts an **identical token multiset** (31 distinct / 51 sites), 570 entries / 29 slides / 27 notes parts unchanged, and that **exactly** slides 24/28/29 differ. v8 sha `59409a2c…`, 27,614,588 B, uploaded and round-trip verified, live in **`v821`** (`TEMPLATE_OBJECT = "ROI-template-master-v8.pptx"`).

**The handler moved with it, and one of the constants would have 500'd every single-year deck.** `dropFeeRow3()` now expects **ONE** shape carrying both `{{FEE_ROW3_*}}` tokens instead of two carrying one each. And because four value shapes left slide 24's **left column**, `dropInvestYearsHeader()`'s expectations fell: **`SHIFT_EXPECTED_2PAY` 12 → 9** and **`SHIFT_EXPECTED_3PAY` 14 → 10**. `FEE_ROW_SHIFT_EMU`, `FEE_BELOW_MIN_Y` and `FEE_BELOW_EXPECTED` were **re-measured** off the v8 bytes and are unchanged (v8 moved no `y`, no `cy`) — re-measured, not assumed. A scratchpad simulation port passed all four modes (2- and 3-payment × single- and two-year), and a **negative control** — the v8 constants against the v7 master — fails loudly in all three surgery modes, which is what makes the pass meaningful.

**Both versions took the VERSIONED path (#342), and v7 is the case worth citing:** a pure wording edit is not automatically a hot swap, because these three slides CARRY tokens and the hot-swap rule stops there. Upload first, deploy second, both times. The bucket now holds **TWELVE** objects (v1–v8 plus four dated backups); **v6 and v7 both stay as rollbacks**.

**Verified:** Jake regenerated a real plan's deck against `v821` and confirmed slide 24 — header on one line, fee rows inline. **NOT confirmed:** the two-year appendix slides 25/26 rendering, and any 3-payment (three-row) deck against v8. **New gotcha #480.**

### 5 — A recurring service's start date, and the second deduction that nearly happened (`v820`, both repos)

New action **`gc_update_subscription_date`** (`actions/gc/update-subscription-date.ts`, `router/dispatch.ts` `AUTH_HANDLERS`, `constants/role-gates.ts` `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`) — **deliberately NOT in `MEMBER_SCOPED_ACTIONS`**, because it is addressed by `subscription_id` and reads the owning member off the row, so there is no `member_number` for that list to rewrite and the admin-only gate is the whole boundary (**#455**). Body `{subscription_id, start_date}`.

**The semantics are the entire feature, and they are Jake's "Option B" after a real near-miss.** `gc_redeem` deducts a recurring service's credits **synchronously** and sets `next_charge_date` one interval out, so a subscriber is **already paid for the period they are sitting in**. An earlier draft offered a *"next charge date"* field; typing `09/17/2026` into a **yearly** subscription redeemed `2026-09-09` would have **taken another 10 credits eight days later** and re-anchored the year from the wrong date. Jake caught it before clicking Save, and afterwards nothing would have — a second deduction on a subscription is indistinguishable from a legitimate renewal.

So `start_date` means **day 1 of the current period**, and the handler stores `next_charge_date = addInterval(start_date, gc_services.billing_interval)` using the **same `utils/gc-recurring.ts addInterval`** the redeem path and the nightly sweep use, so a month-end clamp cannot differ between the writer and the reader. **No credits move.** It refuses a date that is not real, a `cancelled` subscription, a service that is no longer recurring, and a `start_date` whose computed renewal is **before today UTC** (it would charge on the very next sweep); the UPDATE carries an optimistic **`.eq("next_charge_date", <the value just read>)`** and returns **409** on a race with the sweep.

**The UI, in `GCMarketplaceViews.jsx`** (the shared member/admin view — every change is `adminMode`-only except one layout wrap): a **borderless "Edit date" link** beside Cancel on the *"Subscribed — renews «date»"* row. An outlined button shipped first and crushed the service name onto two lines; Jake rejected it, and the row containers gained `flexWrap` and a proper flex basis so long names wrap instead of squashing. The dialog *"Reschedule recurring service"* reads *"Set the date «service» starts. It currently starts «renewal − one interval»."* with a date input and a live line *"Renews «start + interval», then every month|year. **No additional credits are taken.**"* — red, Save disabled, when the computed renewal is already past. The success banner is *"«service» now starts «d» and renews «the SERVER-derived renewal». No additional credits were taken."* `addIntervalLocal` / `subIntervalLocal` mirror the backend's clamping and say so in a comment.

**Verified by Jake on the dev server against `v820`** on two **yearly** subscriptions on Test Member 59524: List Building (sub 6) start `09/17/2026` → renews `2027-09-17`; Constant Contact (sub 7) → renews `2027-09-26`; pill updated, banner wording confirmed. **Not exercised:** a **monthly** reschedule; all four refusals (the past-renewal one is UI-greyed, so curl-only); and the member-login case, where the link simply does not render. **New gotcha #478.**

## 2026-09-09 — A $0.00 implementation fee is a legitimate answer: the tax fee amendment stops requiring that a payment still exist

**BACKEND SHIPPED — `vfo-admin-api` **`v819`**, deployed 2026-09-09 ~13:39Z. The FRONTEND is NOT YET PUBLISHED at the time of writing (`npm run deploy` owed), so there is no `live-N` tag yet.** Four files: `actions/tax/amend-fee.ts`, `actions/tax/implement-final-decision.ts` and `utils/tax-plan-steps.ts` in the edge repo, `src/components/admin/tax/TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` (a 47-line diff) in the react repo. **No migration, no DDL, no `email_templates` row, no cron change, no new action — the count is unmoved at 493** (6 + 487); route pages unmoved at **34**; crons unmoved at **17**; no new table, policy or DB function, so **the security advisor was deliberately NOT re-run**; `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **`v40`**. Gates against the shipping version: `deno check` **0 errors** / action count **493** / `npm run build` **exit 0, 34 route pages** / **smoke 5/5 vs `v819`**, run by Jake after the deploy.

### The change

The tax fee amendment's implementation-only arm — every shape except the two 3-payment Tax 4 arms — accepted a new total only if it was **strictly more** than the retainer already paid (*"Total must be more than the retainer already paid"*). That refused a real business shape: a client whose retainer already covers the whole amended fee owes **nothing further**. The floor is now `< 0` rather than `<= 0`, `$0.00` exactly stores on `implementation_amount`, and the refusal re-words to *"Total cannot be less than the retainer already paid"*. `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx`'s `amendFeePreview` mirrors the floor and adds an orange preview note when the split lands on zero. **The 3-payment Tax 4 arms keep their own floors untouched — a `$0.00` FINAL RETAINER is still refused**, because that installment is a payment the client has yet to make.

### The frontend half — one file, and one of its four edits is load-bearing

`TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` carries the mirrored floor and message, the orange preview note, **and two changes that are not cosmetic**:

- **The charge cascade collapses to ONE done row.** A new `implFeeDue` const (`amendToCents(implementation_amount) > 0`, the FE mirror of the backend's `implAmt > 0`) swaps the three-row *charged / receipt / revenue share* cascade for a single done row, **"No implementation fee due — retainer covers the full fee"**, dated from `implementation_final_decision_at`. Without it the tab shows three rows stuck on *Not completed* forever, the exact shape the backend's step-machine gate exists to prevent.
- **`tax5bAipcDone` gained an arm, and Tax 6 does not unlock without it:** `!(amendToCents(implementation_amount) > 0) && (implFinal === 'Proceed' || implFinal === 'Confirmed')`. The AI PC Admin cascade had always completed on the revenue-share email being sent; at `$0` that email never exists, so the bullet stayed hollow and the phase never closed. This is the FE-only twin of the step-machine gate — **the same missing "there is no payment" case, in a predicate no cross-repo check covers.**
- **Nine client-click DATES are now rendered** — `post_review_client_decision_at` on the 4 Tax 4 rows (Continue now / Proceed / both Refund rows) and `implementation_final_decision_at` on the 5 Tax 5b rows (Proceed now / Yes proceed / Decline / No / the new no-fee row). **Both columns have existed since 2026-08-28 and had never been displayed anywhere**; the rows read *"Client clicked …"* with no date at all until now.

### The three consumers that had to be re-walked

The old floor was silently guaranteeing "a payment exists" to code well outside the handler — see **new gotcha #477**.

- **`implement-final-decision.ts`** — the client's Proceed click at Client decision 2 now returns early at `$0` with `no_fee_due: true`: the decision is recorded, **no acknowledgement email is drafted** (its copy quotes the figure, so it would have said *"$0.00"* is now being processed), and **the charge chain is skipped**. The `TAX_impl_client_proceed` bell still fires, with the message *"No implementation fee is due — the fee was amended so the retainer already paid covers the whole engagement. Nothing was charged."* Without this the chain would have hit `charge-implementation.ts`'s own `implAmount <= 0` guard and surfaced a **400 as a FAILED CHARGE** on a plan where nothing was owed — the #468 shape of reporting intent instead of outcome. That guard stays as a belt.
- **`utils/tax-plan-steps.ts`** — the three Tax 5 auto steps *Implementation charged* / *Implementation receipt* / *Implementation revenue share* are now `applicable: implReach && implAmt > 0`. At `$0` there is no charge to fire, no receipt to number and no payout leg to sweep, so leaving them applicable would have stranded the Implementation phase as **permanently incomplete** on Client Overview. They are overview-only `System` steps with **no frontend mirror** (`TaxAutomationPanel.jsx`'s timeline cards read plan columns directly and carry no applicability logic).
- **The consumers that were already right** gate on `> 0` themselves and needed nothing: `actions/payments/normalize.ts` emits no implementation row, so `payments_cancel_remaining` skips it and `card-update-shared.ts` drops the plan from the card-update list.

Client decision 1 and Client decision 2 emails needed no change either — neither body quotes the implementation figure; the only amendment-bearing text is `[AMENDMENT_PARAGRAPH]`, which quotes the new **total**.

### Accepted non-behaviours

- **No corrected invoice is ever issued** — a fresh invoice only issues at the next payment and there is none. Same reasoning as the existing decline case.
- **The internal rev-share badge line prints *"Balance outstanding: $0.00"***, which is **true**, and is left alone.
- **`utils/tax-invoice-html.ts` and `send-agreement.ts` would print a `$0.00` implementation row** if either were re-run after such an amendment. Both are unreachable in the ordinary flow, so neither was given a zero branch.
- **Decline at Client decision 2 on such a plan charges and refunds nothing** — VFO holds the whole retainer; any partial refund (`$2,250` in Lana's case) is a **hand Stripe refund**, **by decision (Jake, 2026-09-09)**. Nothing was built for it.
- **A Refund click at Client decision 1 still refunds the FULL retainer** (`$4,500` for Lana), exactly as on every other plan — the amendment does not change that path.

### What motivated it — and why it became a RULE change

Two production plans: **Petrus Phoa client 111 plan 71** (legacy, in its Tax 5b amendment window) and **Lana Hurdle client 159 plan 107** (revised 2-payment, in its Tax 4 window, her `$4,500` ACH retainer still `processing` since 2026-09-08). Either could have been fixed by hand with a single `UPDATE`. **Jake chose the rule change**, because "the retainer already covers the whole fee" is a legitimate business answer and a hand-patched row would have hit the same three unguarded consumers the moment the client clicked Proceed.

### Verified live — fixture plan 186 on Test Client 62 (sandbox), wiped after

Lana-shaped: `$9,000` total, `$4,500` retainer paid, 2-payment. In order: the Tax 4 refusal at **`$4,499`** carrying the new message; the amend to **`$4,500`** → `implementation_amount` **0**, shares re-scaled `3,000` → `1,500 ×3`, `fee_amended_at_tax4` stamped, `client_tax_fee_amendments` audit row **17** with `created_by` `jlatham`, step row *"Completed - Amended"*; **Client decision 1** sent and its green click recorded (bells 1899/1900, *"Complete Client decision 2"*, to the planner and the team member); **Tax 5b "Keep"** (*"Completed - Kept"*); then the single *"Send implementation decision email"* button — **which sends decision `'Undecided'`, and is the only implementation-decision send the tab offers** — followed by the client clicking **"Yes - Proceed"** on the email. That click wrote `implementation_final_decision='Proceed'` and **nothing else**: `implementation_charge_status` NULL, **no PaymentIntent, no checkout token, no receipt**, bells 1905/1906 carrying the new no-fee message, and **NO `"$0.00"` Proceeding draft in Gmail** (Jake checked the mailbox). Client Overview's next action moved to **"Tax 6"** with the three implementation rows gone; the tax tab showed the single done row, **AI PC Admin green and Tax 6 unlocked**; and the newly-wired dates rendered 09/09 on *Client confirmed Continue*, *Client clicked Yes (proceed)* and the no-fee row.

**Cleanup:** plan 186, its 16 `client_tax_progress` rows, audit row 17 and one allocated specialist were all deleted — client 62 holds **zero** plans again. **Bells 1899–1906 were deliberately left** (12 unread on client 62), per the standing rule that a live sweep re-mints bells anyway.

**One fixture artefact, NOT a defect:** the retainer revenue share on plan 186 refused with *"Receipt number not found for retainer"* — the fixture never took a real payment, so it carries no `retainer_receipt_number`. `retainer_rev_paid` was hand-set to `'N/A — No Share Due'` to move the overview along. **This is exactly the path Lana's real amendment will exercise for the first time.**

### PRODUCTION DATA CHANGE — Petrus Phoa plan 71, through the portal, not by SQL

Amended at **Tax 5b on 2026-09-09 14:17Z by Jake, on the ordinary path** (the same green button any admin would use, against `v819`): total **`29,000` → `14,500`**, implementation **`14,500` → `0`**, shares **`9,666.66` / `9,666.66` / `9,666.68` → `4,833.33` / `4,833.33` / `4,833.34`**, `client_tax_fee_amendments` audit row **18**, step row *"Completed - Amended"*. His retainer share was already paid on the **legacy** system, and the re-scaled legs leave that payout **cent-identical** — no money moved and none is owed. **His implementation decision email has NOT been sent yet** — the team sends it, and his real Yes click will be the first genuine `$0` Proceed through `implement-final-decision.ts`.

Note that this **discharges nothing** on the 2026-09-03 planner-widening entry: Petrus was amended by Jake as an **admin**, so *"the first REAL planner amendment"* is still owed there.

### Owed

1. **Lana Hurdle plan 107 is the real one.** When her `$4,500` ACH retainer reaches `succeeded`, the team amends her to `$4,500` at Tax 4 — the **first real Tax 4 amend-to-`$0`** and the **first real retainer revenue share on re-scaled shares**, which the fixture could not fire.
2. **Petrus's decision email + his Yes click** — the first real `$0` Proceed through the new early return.
3. **The `Confirmed` value of that branch is UI-unreachable** (the tab only ever sends `'Undecided'`); it is code-identical to the `Proceed` arm and stays code-only.
4. **Decline at `$0`** — charges and refunds nothing — has never been clicked.
5. **Of the 9 newly-dated rows, only 3 were eyeballed** (Continue now, Yes proceed, the no-fee row). Refund / Decline / Proceed-now / No are code-only.
6. **Pre-existing, flagged and NOT fixed by this branch:** the tab's *"Revenue share verified, member paid, member emailed"* row treats only a `$0` `member_share` as N/A, while the backend's `REV_DONE` also accepts `'N/A — No Share Due'` — so a hand-set N/A reads done on Client Overview and not-done on the tab; and the *"Email sent - awaiting client decision"* chip on the Implementation decision row never changes after the client clicks.
7. **User-side:** today's two sandbox Gmail drafts for Test Client (Client decision 1, the implementation decision email). The test specialist allocation is already deleted.

## 2026-09-08 (3rd branch) — The deposit gets priced by the partnership that pays it, and both onboarding pipelines stop drafting

**A short follow-up to the same day's advisor + accountant onboarding rework (v811 → v814 + `live-185`; its entry is the *2026-09-04 / 2026-09-08* one below), from Jake testing it. `vfo-admin-api` v817 → **v818**, the frontend re-published, one data migration. No new action (493), no DDL, no cron, no new table, policy or DB function; `boldsign-webhook` untouched at `v40`. Gates: `deno check` **0** / action count **493** (6 + 487) / build **exit 0, 34 pages** / advisor **GREEN at the exact baseline** — a confirmation, since the only migration is an `UPDATE` on `email_templates`. **Smoke is owed against `v818`; 5/5 was last run against `v814`.**

### The accountant's Stage 1 order was wrong, and the reason is the cap

Accountant Stage 1 now runs Team Member → Meeting Reminder Setup → Preliminary Meeting → **Direct or Advisor Partnership → CC Connected Advisor → Deposit** → Preliminary Meeting Decision. The advisor order is untouched.

The reorder is not cosmetic. **The deposit's maximum depends on the partnership:** a **Direct** accountant (`'No accountant partnership'`) may be asked for up to **$4,000**, an **Advisor**-partnership accountant (`'Accountant Partnership'`) for at most **$2,000**, because that accountant already pays a $2,000 baseline; the minimum stays $500 on both, and the advisor pipeline stays $500–$4,000. With the Deposit above the Partnership row, the admin was being asked to price the deposit before the system knew what to cap it at.

So the ordering and the gating are the same fact seen twice. The Partnership row is **locked until the meeting outcome is set** (*"Complete the Preliminary Meeting step first"*, or *"Preliminary meeting was a no-show"*), the Deposit row is **locked until the partnership is picked** (*"Select Direct or Advisor Partnership first"*), the hint under the amount reads *"Minimum $500, maximum $2,000"* / *"$4,000"* and the Send button gates on that number. Per **#403** each lock is backed by a handler refusal: `deposit-email.ts` 400s a NULL partnership as well as an over-cap amount. And because the cap must not move under a link that has already been priced against it, the partnership select is **disabled once `deposit_email_sent_at` is set** (tooltip *"A deposit link has already been sent"*) with `save-partnership.ts` 400ing the same change — the same shape as the existing refusal to move the meeting outcome off `Completed - Send Deposit` after a link goes out.

### Both onboarding pipelines stop landing in Drafts

Migration `20260908150000_onboarding_reminders_deposit_send_mode.sql` flipped **14** `email_templates` rows to `send_mode=true` — per pipeline the four stall reminders (`_undecided_reminder`, `_signing_reminder`, `_payment_reminder`, `_deposit_reminder`) and the three deposit emails (`_deposit_payment_link`, `_deposit_received`, `_deposit_refund`). The six meeting-reminder rows were already `true` from 09-04, so **all twenty rows of both pipelines now auto-send** and the system-wide census goes **17 → 31** (**#325**).

**No code changed.** Every sender on these paths already runs through `gmailDraftFetch` / `deliverRaw`, which dispatch on the flag alone; the pipeline's `pipeline_sandbox_config` toggle still reroutes to `jlatham@` upstream of delivery. What the flip did require was the **#428** pass over the UI copy, because draft-era wording invites a confused second click and a duplicate *real* send: the refund confirm dialog in **both** onboarding components now says *"send the refund email"* / *"emails the advisor|accountant"* where it said *"draft"* / *"drafts"*.

**PRODUCTION CONSEQUENCE, and it is the point of the entry.** From the next daily sweeps — **05:00 UTC advisor, 06:00 UTC accountant** — the undecided / signing / payment / deposit stall reminders **real-send to prospects** instead of waiting in Drafts, and so do the deposit link, received and refund emails. These stall reminders are produced by a **cron**, so they are the first mail in this system that reaches an outside person with no human anywhere in the loop. One row is already inoculated: **William Winter (accountant 28)** carries `payment_reminder_sent_at` stamped 2026-09-05 — a draft addressed to `jlatham@` from the 09-04 → 09-08 sandbox window — so the ladder considers him reminded and sends nothing.

### Verified live, and what was not

On accountant row **31 "Test Cap"** (created and deleted the same evening): the Partnership row locked until the outcome was set and then unlocked; **Advisor** produced the *"maximum $2,000"* hint, **$2,500 was refused by the button and $2,000 accepted**; the deposit email **auto-sent**, with the function log reading `send_mode: auto-sent ACCOUNTANT_ONBOARDING/ACCOUNTANT_deposit_payment_link` — **the first real send of that template**; and the Partnership select was disabled afterwards.

Not exercised: the **Direct $4,000** hint; **all three backend 400s** (over-cap, NULL partnership, partnership-change-after-link), each of which the UI's own locks make unreachable — they exist for the API caller that skips the UI; and the **deposit-received, refund and stall-reminder** real sends. The ACCOUNTANT sandbox toggle was ON for part of the test (Jake flipped it) and is `false` again; nothing else in this branch sent anything. Two empty live Stripe customers created for deleted test rows — `cus_VDzJ6oBNUDPVz2` and `cus_VDweR9Qz933DAM` — are Jake's to delete in the dashboard; neither carries a charge.

**New gotcha #476** came out of the doc pass rather than the feature: every file in both working trees is **CRLF**, so a `\n`-anchored multi-line `perl`/`sed` rewrite matches nothing and still exits 0, leaving an empty `git diff` that reads exactly like "already applied".

## 2026-09-08 (2nd branch) — The bank sign-in wall comes down on `/pay` and `/tax-pay`, and "the client paid" stops being said about a payment that has not happened

**Edge repo only for CODE. `vfo-admin-api` v814 → **v815** (the feature) → **v816** (the Stripe-page wording, on all five builders that show the manual option) → **v817** (the re-worded "client paid" bells). The react repo carries **DOCS ONLY** — there is no frontend code change on this branch, so there was no `npm run build`, no `npm run deploy`, and deliberately **NO `live-N` tag**. TWO migrations, both applied via MCP and both committed as files. `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **v40**. Action count unmoved at **493**; route pages unmoved at 34; pg_cron unmoved at 17; `send_mode=true` unmoved at 17. **No new table, no policy, no DB function, no new action, no cron change.**

### What was asked, and the one thing that was refused

Jake asked for the `/pay` and `/tax-pay` Stripe pages to stop forcing clients through bank sign-in. The block is one parameter: `payment_method_options[us_bank_account][verification_method]='instant'` restricts Stripe's hosted page to the **Financial Connections bank-login flow with no manual account/routing fallback**, so every bank Financial Connections does not support — and every payer who hits MFA trouble or bails at the final authorize click — is locked out with no other way through. That is the diagnosis **#298** already made on SpecRev in July, after Dan Zimanski produced six expired sessions in fourteen days. **This branch is the first time that widening leaves SpecRev.**

The unpin itself is one deleted line per builder. Everything else in this entry is what the deleted line costs.

**One thing was proposed and REJECTED.** A frontend interstitial on `/pay` and `/tax-pay` — a "are you sure? manual entry is slow" step before the redirect — was offered and **Jake explicitly turned it down**. The Stripe page is the only warning surface, by decision. That constraint is what makes `custom_text[submit][message]` load-bearing rather than decorative: it is not one warning among several, it is the whole mitigation. Stripe's own *"Enter bank details manually (may take 1-2 business days)"* link text belongs to Stripe and **cannot be edited or hidden**, and the fallback must stay available, so a single bolded sentence above the submit button is all there is.

**The wording took three passes and is Jake's, verbatim:** *"**PLEASE DO NOT enter your bank details manually unless signing in to your bank above does not work.** Manual entry puts your payment on hold for several days while Stripe verifies small test deposits, and Stripe cancels the payment if they are not confirmed."* It lives once, in the new `constants/ach-checkout-note.ts`. **`custom_text` renders `**bold**` markdown** — confirmed live on the hosted page, which is why the first sentence lands as a sentence and not as literal asterisks. v816 exists because the note initially went on `/pay` and `/tax-pay` only; on review, **all five builders that now show the manual option** got it — the two SpecRev builders and the licence continuation branch had been unpinned since July with no warning at all. The two **recurring** builders **prepend** it to their existing *"No charge today…"* sentence with a blank line between, rather than replacing it: that sentence still has to be said, and the note goes first.

### `checkout.session.completed` stops meaning "paid"

On the manual-entry path Stripe fires it **at SUBMIT**, with the PaymentIntent parked in `requires_action`, micro-deposits pending and **no debit attempted**. The MAP 1 and Tax branches were already fetching that PaymentIntent to read `payment_method` — and throwing `status` away. That is precisely the shape **#370** caught on the one-time SpecRev path in August. **If you expose the fallback, you must read the PI's own status; the session's arrival is not evidence of a payment.**

**The sub-state is a nullable SIDE-COLUMN, not a new status value, and that is the branch's main design decision.** `pay1_status` / `retainer_status` / `final_retainer_status` keep saying `'processing'` for the whole wait; the three new columns (`pay1_bank_verification_pending_at`, `retainer_bank_verification_pending_at`, `final_retainer_bank_verification_pending_at`, migration `20260908120000`) carry the rest. This is the deliberate **opposite** of the SpecRev choice, whose fourth value `awaiting_verification` immediately stranded its own settle path because one guard read `=== 'processing'` (**#371**). A side-column is invisible to code that does not read it, so the settle branches, the late-ACH failure branches, the charge sweep, the open-installment resolver, the refund guards and every frontend status map needed **zero** changes. No backfill: NULL correctly means "not awaiting verification", which is true of every row that existed.

Each `checkout.session.completed` pass writes the column explicitly — `now()` when pending, an explicit **NULL** otherwise — so the column is never left stale from a previous attempt. On the pending path it also raises a dismissible FYI (`MAP1_ach_bank_verification_pending` / `TAX_ach_bank_verification_pending`, Jake + Tracy, `dedupe:"unread"`) saying no money has moved and that Stripe cancels after about ten days. Notification rules **207 → 209**; areas *MAP 1* 17 → **18** and *Tax* 39 → **40**, both written up in `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md` and both rows re-derived live rather than the whole page regenerated.

### Saying the true thing to the client

`CONTRACT_confirmationemail|ach` and `TAX_confirmationemail|ach` both say *"we have received your payment"*. On this path that is **false** — nothing has been debited. Four new `|ach_verify` rows (plain + member-paying twin each, `to_list`/`cc_list`/`bcc_list` copied **verbatim** from the rows they twin so the audience is identical, `send_mode=false`) are selected off the stamp, and they deliberately carry neither `[CARD_FEE_TEXT]` (never a card) nor `[PROCESSING_TIME]` (the "2-4 business days" sentence is exactly the promise that does not hold yet). They do carry `[RETAINER_LABEL]`, so a 3-payment plan still reads *"initial retainer"*. Migration `20260908120100`, applied by **`execute_sql`** rather than `apply_migration` — `apply_migration` can return `{"success": true}` and insert nothing into `email_templates` (**#373**), so the rows were SELECTed back afterwards.

**v817 exists because the bells were still lying after the emails stopped.** `MAP1_client_paid`, `TAX_retainer_paid` and `TAX_retainer_paid_schedule_meeting` all announced a payment. They now re-word on the pending path — *"«Client» submitted bank details (verification pending)"*, *"no money has moved yet"*, *"invoice & receipt follow once the funds settle"* — same rule keys, same recipients, same links. Reporting the INTENT as the OUTCOME is **#468** for the third session running.

One trap on the Tax side: `automation_TAX_confirmationemail` selects its columns by name, so `retainer_bank_verification_pending_at` had to join the explicit `.select(...)` **in the same edit**, or the predicate would have been silently, permanently false with the legacy branch as its symptom (**#448**).

### The event the expiry actually emits

When the client never verifies, Stripe cancels after ~10 business days and emits **`payment_intent.canceled` — NOT `payment_intent.payment_failed`** — and a dashboard Cancel does the same. That event was consumed for **SpecRev only**, so without this a MAP 1 or Tax row would have sat at `'processing'` **forever**, with no bell and no client email. The whole `payment_failed` block now also runs for `canceled` when `metadata.pipeline === 'TAX'` or `metadata.payment_number` is set, with `failReason` reading `cancellation_reason`. A new `payment_intent.processing` block clears the stamp when the bank verifies and the debit starts moving; `payment_intent.succeeded` belt-clears it on all three settle paths.

**A gap the implementing agent caught in its own review, and it is the most interesting thing on the branch.** A P1 PaymentIntent carries `metadata.payment_number = '1'`, and `isOffSession` is `!!md.payment_number || …` — written when only the nightly sweep stamped that field. The client-driven `/pay` page started stamping it too, back in v773. So a **cancelled Holistic P1 was being classified as an off-session installment and resolved to nothing at all**. `isFirstInstallmentCancel` (`canceled` **and** `payment_number === '1'`) removes it from `isOffSession` for that event only; a P1 **bounce** is still deliberately left to `checkout.session.async_payment_failed`, which fires the same bell title and dedupes. **A metadata field that two different producers set no longer means what its original consumer assumed.**

### Verified live — test client 62, sandbox, fixtures wiped afterwards

**Tax plan 185** (retainer $3,500, `fee_process_version` 2026-08-25): manual entry → `retainer_status='processing'`, `retainer_bank_verification_pending_at` **20:41:28Z**, `retainer_payment_intent_id` `pi_3UDVp5Rv8yMNbvOJ0lglNbxH`, last4 6789, function log `pi_status: requires_action`, bells **1882** (Jake) + **1883** (Tracy), and the `TAX_confirmationemail|ach_verify` Gmail draft **read end to end by Jake** — correct subject and body, *"$3,500.00"*, *"retainer"*. Micro-deposits then verified on Stripe's own hosted page → `retainer_status='succeeded'`, stamp back to **NULL**, invoice `INV-59524-001-0050` + receipt `REC-59524-001-0038` at 20:47Z.

**Holistic row 149** (Quarterly, net 5400, P1 $1,350): manual entry → `pay1_status='processing'`, stamp **20:51:41Z**, last4 6789, bells **1888** (Jake) + **1889** (Tracy), and the `CONTRACT_confirmationemail|ach_verify` draft read (Payment 1 of 4, Core Membership). Then a **dashboard Cancel** on the PaymentIntent → `payment_intent.canceled` at **20:54:27Z** → `pay1_status='failed'`, bell **1891** *"Payment FAILED — Test Client (MAP 1 first payment) … canceled (requested_by_customer)"*, log `payment_intent.canceled — MAP 1 pipeline_map1 row 149`. **That single click is the only exercise the widened `canceled` event has had**, and it proves `isFirstInstallmentCancel`, the `cancellation_reason` read and the block firing on the new event type. The stamp stays set on the failed row — nothing reads it, and clearing it would be a write with no reader; accepted.

**On the Stripe page itself**, the bolded first sentence was confirmed rendering **bold** by Jake (v816). The pre-v817 "client paid" bells (**1884 / 1885 / 1890**) fired with the OLD wording, which is exactly what v817 fixes — so the re-worded bells are code-only.

**Fixtures deleted afterwards:** tax plan 185 with its 5 `client_tax_progress` rows, and `pipeline_map1` row 149. **Bells were deliberately left** (18 unread on client 62).

**MIGRATIONS (2, both applied via MCP and both committed, #196).** `20260908120000_ach_bank_verification_pending_columns.sql` — 3 additive nullable `timestamptz` columns on two EXISTING tables, applied by `apply_migration`. `20260908120100_ach_verify_templates_and_rules.sql` — 4 `email_templates` + 2 `notification_rules`, applied by `execute_sql` per #373 and SELECTed back (4 templates, 2 rules, 3 columns all confirmed). **The security advisor was re-run after the DDL: GREEN at the exact baseline** (5 deny-all `rls_enabled_no_policy` INFO + the `pg_net` WARN, nothing else). Neither `pipeline_map1` nor `client_tax_plans` is on that INFO list and neither joined it — additive nullable columns on existing tables need no RLS change and none was made.

## 2026-09-04 / 2026-09-08 — Advisor + Accountant onboarding: sequential Stage 1, a preliminary-meeting reminder ladder, a refundable Membership Deposit and an off-session balance charge

**Both repos. `vfo-admin-api` v810 → v811 (2026-09-04 feature) → v812 (Jake added to the team map) → v813 (email button labels) → v814 (2026-09-08: the refund-email `"$$"` fix, the once-only CEO countersign stamp, `balance_charge_status` on ACH settle, and `[PAYMENT_NEXT_STEP]` / `[Deposit Note]` rendering). Frontend published by `npm run deploy` TWICE, 2026-09-04 and 2026-09-08. `boldsign-webhook` untouched at v40. SIX migrations, all applied via MCP and all committed as files. Action count 481 → 493 (twelve added, none renamed or removed). Route pages 33 → 34. pg_cron 16 → 17 jobs. `send_mode=true` census 11 → 17.** One shipping unit across two chats: Jake asked for it on 2026-09-04, Fable planned, Opus executed, Fable reviewed, and Jake click-tested every step live on both days. **Both onboarding pipelines are file-for-file clones, so everything below landed twice.**

The flow of record is the new **[flows/advisor-accountant-onboarding.md](flows/advisor-accountant-onboarding.md)**; PFT keeps the handoff and the stop-status in [flows/partnership-fast-track.md](flows/partnership-fast-track.md).

**Stage 1 is now a strictly sequential, tax-style locked cascade** — Team Member Responsible → **Meeting Reminder Setup (NEW)** → Preliminary Meeting → **Deposit (NEW, only when the outcome is `Completed - Send Deposit`)** → Implementation value (including deposit) [advisor] / Direct-or-Advisor Partnership + CC Connected Advisor [accountant] → Preliminary Meeting Decision. Each lock is backed by a handler 400 (#403): `prelim-meeting.ts` requires the reminder to have been **sent or skipped**, and refuses to move the outcome off `Completed - Send Deposit` once a deposit link has gone out; `meeting-reminder.ts` requires a Team Member, because the bells route to that person. **The reminder prerequisite fires only when `prelim_meeting_status` is currently NULL**, so pre-existing rows are never forced back through a reminder they cannot arm — deliberate, and it means legacy rows never arm the ladder at all.

**The outcome vocabulary is now four values**: `Completed - Send Deposit` | `Completed - No Deposit` | `No Show` (auto-stops the row and leaves the decision locked) | `Request no meeting`. **The stored `Request no meeting` literal was deliberately NOT renamed** — `actions/pft/ft-response.ts` writes exactly that string on the PFT fast path — so only the UI label moved, to *"Requested no meeting"*. Legacy `'Completed'` rows read and display as *No Deposit*; there was no backfill, so both values are live in the column. All Stage 1 completion dates became fixed MM/DD text (StepDate editing removed from both components), which leaves the backend action **`save_onboarding_step_date` with no frontend caller** — noted, not deleted. Opening an onboarding now writes `?onboarding=<id>` so a reload stays on the record.

**The preliminary-meeting reminder ladder is the branch's one genuinely new mechanism, and it is a COUNTDOWN, not a chase.** Green *"Send reminder (with date)"* → date / time / timezone (time REQUIRED) → a `window.confirm` reading *"This reminder will be sent to the prospective advisor 1 business day before the meeting."* → stores `meeting_at`, `meeting_reminder_due_at` (the same wall clock one BUSINESS day earlier, `utils/onboarding-meeting.ts reminderDueAt`) and a token; grey *"Skip reminder"* stamps `meeting_reminder_skipped_at`. A new 5-minute cron **`onboarding-meeting-reminder-sweep-5min` (pg_cron jobid 18)** fires PUBLIC `automation_ONBOARDING_MEETING_sweep` (`actions/onboarding/meeting-reminder-sweep.ts`) for BOTH pipelines: tier (a) sends `<PREFIX>_meeting_reminder` when `due_at <= now` **and `meeting_at > now`** — that second half is what makes a meeting booked *inside* the window send on the next tick instead of never — then tiers (b) 60-minute and (c) 10-minute, **both gated on `meeting_response='confirm'`**. Every query filters `status='active'`. Buttons **✓ Confirm / ✗ Cancel / Reschedule** land on the new public page `/onboarding-meeting` (`src/pages/OnboardingMeetingPage.jsx`, route 34, confirm-card-first per #290) → PUBLIC `automation_ONBOARDING_meetingresponse`, idempotent on `meeting_response`, raising FYI bells to the Team Member Responsible. **Reschedule RE-ARMS the whole ladder — the three `*_sent_at` stamps AND `meeting_response` / `meeting_response_at` — the exact inverse of #404** (gotcha **#472**).

**All three reminder templates × 2 pipelines are `send_mode=true`** (ids 247-249 and 254-256), taking the auto-send census from **eleven to seventeen** (#325). That is a deliberate break with the roster's old *"here is your link"* theme: **a draft nobody sends in time is not a reminder**. They obey the pipeline sandbox toggles like every other email.

**Zoom and calendar links are per-team-member maps in `constants/onboarding-team.ts` and are ENTIRELY BLANK** (owed from Jake). Blank is a supported state: the email renders *"The Zoom link for the meeting will be sent separately."* and drops the rebooking link. The Team Member Responsible dropdown became `ONBOARDING_TEAM_MEMBER_NAMES` — Ian Welham, Vanessa Smith, Rachael Hopson, Jake Latham — while the New Model Sale modal keeps the wider `SALES_TEAM_NAMES`; `"Jake Latham"` → `jlatham@elitert.com` joined `TEAM_MEMBER_LOGIN_EMAILS`.

**The refundable Membership Deposit ($500-$4,000)** is sent by AUTH `automation_<P>_depositemail`, which **creates the Stripe customer EARLY if missing**, mints `deposit_checkout_token` and drafts `<PREFIX>_deposit_payment_link`. **The SAME `/advisor-pay` and `/accountant-pay` pages serve it**: `load-payment.ts` and `stripe-checkout.ts` resolve `checkout_token` first and then `deposit_checkout_token`, the session AND the PaymentIntent carry `payment_kind='onboarding_deposit'`, and `setup_future_usage=off_session` saves the method so the balance can reuse it. **A new deposit branch in `checkout.session.completed`, guarded on the SESSION metadata and placed ahead of the old block**, books processing/succeeded and chains PUBLIC `automation_<P>_depositconfirmation` → `<PREFIX>_deposit_received` **on BOTH card and ACH** — a documented exception to #287, because no receipt is issued until the onboarding payment completes, so this is the deposit's only acknowledgement. `payment_intent.succeeded` branches on `pi.metadata.payment_kind`; failures route to the new `handleOnboardingDepositFailure` / `handleOnboardingBalanceFailure`, and **the generic first-payment resolver now skips both onboarding legs** because it writes `payment_status`, which belongs to the onboarding payment (gotcha **#473**). A **4th stall ladder (tier d)** joined both sweeps — `<P>_stall_deposit_email` 2 bd / `<P>_stall_deposit_bell` 4 bd, template `<P>_deposit_reminder`, ack column `deposit_pf_ack_at` whitelisted in `actions/automation/stall-ack.ts` with **no extra-meeting coupling**, since the deposit is sent before the decision email. A **Refund** button (cloned from the tax deposit-refund step) refunds the PaymentIntent in full, writes `deposit_status='refunded'`, **STOPS the onboarding**, drafts `<PREFIX>_deposit_refund` with a required `[Refund Reason]` and rings `<P>_deposit_refunded`; it refuses once `payment_status` is `succeeded` or `processing`.

**The money forks at CEO countersign.** `_stripecustomer` no longer early-returns on an existing customer; it forks on `deposit_status` — `succeeded` chains PUBLIC `automation_<P>_chargebalance` (an off-session PI on the deposit's saved method, card grossed up `(base + 0.30) / 0.971`, `payment_kind='onboarding_balance'`, idempotency `adv-balance-<id>-<pm>-<date>`, `amountDue <= 0` taking a paid-in-full path); `processing` parks `balance_charge_status='awaiting_deposit'`, released by the deposit's own settle branch; anything else takes the original link route. **`payment_amount` keeps its meaning — the TOTAL engagement value — and every fee base nets a settled deposit off it**, without which a deposit-paid card records a large negative fee. `[Deposit Note]` joined `<P>_payment_link` (renders `""` with no deposit) and `[PAYMENT_NEXT_STEP]` replaced the *"separate email with a secure payment link"* sentence in `<P>_agreement_sent`, with `send-agreement.ts` rendering the original sentence when there is no deposit.

**One invoice and one receipt, deposit-aware.** Schedule rows *Deposit* / *Balance Payment* each with their own card-fee and *Total Charged* rows, or a single *Deposit (paid in full)* row; Payment Plan label *"Deposit + Balance"* / *"Deposit (paid in full)"* / *"One-Time Payment"*; a Payment Breakdown box on the receipt. **The no-deposit output is byte-identical**, guaranteed by the `invoiceShellHtml` split. One small unrequested behaviour change rode along: **accountant money formatting now matches advisor — it used to drop cents.** Stage 2 rows became deposit-aware to match (link row hidden when a deposit is on file, *"Remaining payment collected after deposit"*, both hidden when the deposit covers the total, and an info line whose balance figure appears **only once `agreement_signed_by_ceo_at` is set**).

**Two defects found and fixed on 2026-09-08 that are worth their own gotchas.** `advisor_onboarding.payment_amount` carries a column **`DEFAULT 4000`**, and a default is indistinguishable from a written value by every ordinary test — so *"nothing further due"* rendered on records nobody had priced yet, which is why every derived figure is now gated on the countersign stamp (**#469**). And **BoldSign redelivers `Completed`**, so the unconditional `agreement_signed_by_ceo_at: nowIso` in that branch had been re-dating the countersign on every redelivery; it is now `existing || now` on both pipelines (**#470**). A third, cheaper lesson: *"Invalid or expired link"* on the meeting page turned out to be a **truncated token pasted from a chat message**, not a bug (**#471**). Cleaning the fixtures produced the fourth: `document_numbers`' *exactly one owner* CHECK means a test onboarding cannot be unlinked from its numbers — the number rows must be deleted, which is safe because the allocator counts rows and the number embeds the owner id (**#474**).

**MIGRATIONS (6, all applied via MCP and all committed as files, #196).** `20260905100000` — 35 columns per table (`meeting_*`, `deposit_*`, `balance_*`); `20260905100100` — 6 meeting bell rules; `20260905100200` — 8 deposit rules; `20260905100300` — 14 templates, 6 of them `send_mode=true`; `20260905100400` — pg_cron job 18, **its bearer redacted to a placeholder** because the real job was installed live by `execute_sql`, copying `reminder-sweep-5min`'s own stored command with the action name swapped (the file documents the reinstall); `20260908120000` — the two template body edits. **No new table, no policy, no DB function.** The security advisor was re-run after the DDL on 2026-09-04 and again on 2026-09-08: **GREEN at the exact baseline** (5 deny-all `rls_enabled_no_policy` INFO + the `pg_net` WARN, nothing else) — `advisor_onboarding` and `accountant_onboarding` were already on that INFO list and stayed there. Notification rules went 193 → **207**; areas *Advisor Onboarding* and *Accountant Onboarding* each 12 → **19**.

**PRODUCTION CONSEQUENCE — the sandbox window.** `pipeline_sandbox_config` rows `ADVISOR_ONBOARDING` and `ACCOUNTANT_ONBOARDING` were `sandbox_mode=true` **from 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-08 inclusive**, so **every real advisor and accountant email in that window — including the daily stall reminder ladders — was rerouted to `jlatham@elitert.com` and reached no prospect.** Both are `false` again and all eight pipelines were re-verified LIVE on 2026-09-08. Anything a real prospect should have received in those four days was not sent.

**TEST FIXTURES DELETED 2026-09-08:** advisor onboardings 20-24 and accountant onboarding 30, with their `document_numbers` rows and their bells.

**VERIFIED LIVE — Jake's click-through plus SQL and function-log checks.** *Advisor:* the reminder sent on the next 5-minute tick; a Confirm click recorded with its bell; a reschedule re-sent the reminder and cleared the recorded response; `No Show` locked the decision and filed the row under Stopped — **and left the 60/10 tiers unfired, because the row was stopped before the meeting time**. A **$500 card deposit** (fee $15.24) → countersign → **a $1,500 balance charged off-session 2 seconds later** (fee $45.11) with no link minted, `INV-ADV21-0050` / `REC-ADV21-0076` and the Ready-to-create bell. A **$750 deposit refunded in full** ($772.71 including the fee): refunded, Stopped, email drafted. ## 2026-09-04 (2nd branch) — Steve Peterson 59127-002 re-stated to the amounts actually collected

**Edge repo only. NO code shipped: `vfo-admin-api` went v808 → v809 → **v810**, where v810 reverts v809 and is byte-identical to v808 (`aa33e42`). Action count is unchanged at **481**. Tags `backend-good-2026-09-04-v809` and `backend-good-2026-09-04-v810` both exist and both record real deploys. `boldsign-webhook` untouched at **v40**. NO migration, NO DDL, NO template edit, NO cron, NO frontend change (so no `live-N`).**

### The data correction — the only lasting change

**Applied by `execute_sql`, not by a migration, so no file in the repo reproduces it. This entry is its record.** (`apply_migration` was refused by tooling; the write itself was approved and verified.)

`pipeline_map1` **142** (Steve Peterson, `59127-002`, member Jeff Rainer) re-stated:

| Column | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `net_invoice` | `5200` | **`5400`** |
| `member_share` | `2600` | **`2700`** |
| `vfos_share` | `2600` | **`2700`** |

The `UPDATE` carried `and net_invoice = '5200'` so a re-run is a no-op rather than a second bump.

**Why.** Installments 1–3 were collected at **$1,350** each on the legacy system but were migrated in as $1,300 — a transcription error at migration time. Installment 4 was then charged the migrated (wrong) $1,300 through the portal, and the $50 shortfall was collected by hand afterwards. All four installments now read **$1,350** with a **$675 / $675** split, and `member_share + vfos_share = net_invoice` exactly.

**Why it was safe, and the check that made it so.** Both nightly sweeps were proven inert on this row **before** the write, not after:

- **03:00 charge sweep** — all four `payN_status` are `succeeded`, and the sweep charges only an EMPTY slot (`if (status) continue`, #431/#444). No installment can be re-charged.
- **02:00 revshare sweep** — all four legs carry `recN_rev_share = 'Completed - Money Mapping'` with `rev_paid` in the terminal set (`N/A — No Share Due` on 1–3, `Money Mapping` on 4), which satisfies the sweep's `resolved` test exactly. No transfer can fire.

The engagement is **Money Mapping throughout**, so the member is never paid by Stripe transfer here and no payout was ever owed — the share is an internal allocation. The Drive receipt `REC-59127-002-0001` still says $1,300 for installment 4 and was **deliberately not reissued**; the extra $50 was handled outside the system.

**Changing `net_invoice` changes only reporting here.** Every consumer that could act on it is gated on a payment status that is already terminal; the per-installment figures on the Payments tab, the pricing split card and the Accounting panels all derive from these three columns and now agree with what was actually collected.

### Why there are two tags for one day

A draft-only tax-planner revenue-share tool (`tax_planner_revshare_draft`) was built and shipped as **v809** to produce two after-the-fact confirmation emails for shares settled on the legacy system, then **reverted in v810 at the user's request** — it was a one-off need that will not recur, and the code was not wanted in the repo. Both emails were produced and sent before the revert. `v810` restores `utils/tax-planner-payout.ts` to its exact pre-v809 form, so the draft for a planner share remains reachable **only** through `transferPlannerShare` on a successful transfer, as it was before. This paragraph exists so the v809/v810 tag pair is not a mystery later; there is no surviving code, action or script to look for.
