## 2026-08-27 — Recurring Growth Credit services: a cadence on the service, a subscription per member, and a nightly sweep that charges from the credit balance

**One chat, shipped as `vfo-admin-api` v797 with ONE migration (`20260827150000_gc_recurring_services.sql`, applied to prod via MCP and committed as a file, #196). Action count 477 → 480 (+3, all GC). One new cron: `gc-recurring-sweep-daily` @ 12:30 UTC, so the inventory is 15 → 16 jobs. `boldsign-webhook` untouched, still v40. No new `notification_rules` key. Frontend deploy NOT done in this session — it is the branch's headline owed item.**

### What it is

A `gc_services` row can now bill on a repeating cadence. `gc_services.billing_interval` is `'one_time'` (not-null default, so **every pre-existing row is unchanged and the entire one-time path is byte-for-byte what it was**) | `'monthly'` | `'yearly'`, with a CHECK constraint, edited through a new **Frequency** dropdown in Automation & Config → Growth Credits.

**The first charge of a recurring service is the ordinary redemption, completely untouched** — `gc_redeem` deducts the credits, files the `gc_redemptions` row the fulfilment queue works off, rings the `GC_credits_spent` bell and drafts the confirmation email. What is new is that a monthly/yearly service ALSO opens a `gc_subscriptions` row, and the nightly `automation_GC_recurring_sweep` charges every due row again straight out of `gc_balances`.

**Renewals deliberately write `gc_transactions` ONLY, never `gc_redemptions`** (description `"<name> (renewal)"`) — charge 2..n is not a new request for anyone to fulfil, so from the second charge on the ledger is the entire audit trail. That single decision is what keeps the Redemptions queue honest and is also why the reject branch below can assume what it assumes.

### The three new actions (477 → 480, all AUTH)

- **`gc_load_subscriptions`** and **`gc_cancel_subscription`**, both in `MEMBER_SCOPED_ACTIONS`. Cancel takes a `subscription_id`, and that list rewrites **only `body.member_number`** — so the handler's `.eq("member_number", …)` on the UPDATE **is** the ownership guard, not decoration (#455, commented at the site). `.select()` confirms a row was matched; zero rows returns 404 rather than a false success. Cancelling is not a refund and not a proration: the period already paid for stands, only the next charge stops.
- **`automation_GC_recurring_sweep`** in `PUBLIC_HANDLERS` behind the same service-role `Authorization` check as `automation_GROWTH_overdue_sweep`, which it is modelled on.

### The sweep, and the review catch that changed it

Daily at 12:30 UTC. Candidates are `status in ('active','on_hold') AND next_charge_date <= today`. Per row: re-read the service (a deactivated service, or one flipped back to `one_time`, **skips in place** — the row keeps its now-past due date, so restoring the service charges once on the next tick); then charge the service's **CURRENT `credit_cost`**, not a snapshot.

The charge is claimed **optimistically before the money moves**: the UPDATE advances `next_charge_date` with an `.eq()` on the value this run read, then `.select()`s, and a zero-row result means another run already claimed the period — skip, balance untouched. Short balance → `status='on_hold'` + an `on_hold_notified_at` stamp (one out-of-credits email per hold episode, guarded by that stamp), and **the date is deliberately NOT advanced**, so the member is charged for the period they are actually starting. There is **no weekend skip**, unlike the growth-overdue sweep it was cloned from — these are date-anchored charges and member-facing emails, not admin bells landing on a Saturday.

**The catch worth recording: as first written, the re-anchor derived from the stale due date.** A subscription that went on hold and was funded weeks later would have been charged again every single night until it "caught up" — the code comment said the right thing while the code did the wrong one. Caught in review before the deploy, changed to re-anchor from **TODAY, the day the charge actually happens**, and then live-proven: a row due `2026-07-15`, funded on the 27th, charged exactly once and re-anchored to `2026-09-27`. This is gotcha **#456**.

`gc_update_redemption`'s **reject** branch also cancels the member+service subscription, on top of the credit refund it already did. A rejectable *pending* redemption of a recurring service is always the initial one — renewals file no redemption row — so there is no ambiguity about which subscription is meant.

### Emails and data

`utils/gc-recurring-email.ts`, same safety contract as `gc-redemption-email.ts`: function replacers throughout (#438), sandbox-aware via `pipeline_sandbox_config`, a missing or inactive template is a logged skip rather than an error, and nothing in it may throw back into the sweep. Two templates seeded live, both `send_mode=false`, To `RECIPIENT` / Cc `TEAM_MEMBER`: **244 `GC_recurring_renewal`** and **245 `GC_recurring_out_of_credits`**. No new `notification_rules` key was needed — the existing `GC_credits_spent` bell fires on the initial redemption and renewals are not a new ask.

New table `gc_subscriptions`: `member_number` FK → `member_plugin_settings` CASCADE (mirroring `gc_balances`/`gc_redemptions`), `service_id` FK → `gc_services` **NO ACTION** (so a subscribed service cannot be deleted and history keeps resolving), `status` CHECK `active|on_hold|cancelled`, `next_charge_date`, `last_charged_at`, `on_hold_notified_at`, `created_at`, `cancelled_at`; indexes on `(status, next_charge_date)` for the sweep and `(member_number)` for the portal. **RLS + deny-all in the same migration** (#141), advisor GREEN at the exact baseline afterwards, and an anon probe on the table returned `Content-Range: */0`.

### Frontend

`src/components/shared/GCMarketplaceViews.jsx` is new and is now the **single** source for `GCServicesView` + `GCTransactionHistory`, rendering both the member marketplace's Services/History tabs and the admin per-member GC tab in `MembersPanel`. That admin tab's sub-tabs went **Dashboard | Member Details** → **Dashboard | Services | History**: the bespoke "Member Details" transaction/redemption lists were deleted in favour of the member-identical History, and admins can redeem or cancel on a member's behalf by passing that member's number (which member-scoping permits for an admin session). Recurring rows read `N credits / month|year`; a live subscription replaces Redeem with a **Subscribed — renews \<date\>** or **On hold — add credits to resume** pill plus a Cancel button behind a confirm modal, and the recurring confirm modal spells the repeat charge out in words before anything is spent. Bare `YYYY-MM-DD` dates are pinned to local midnight before formatting so they do not render a day early west of Greenwich.

Also fixed in the same file, and worth its own line because it is older than this branch: the GC banner had exactly ONE style, green, so **every error the marketplace has ever shown was rendered as a success**. It now discriminates on the `'Error'` prefix the hosts already funnelled failures through, and renders red.

### Verified live, and what was not

All live testing was on test member 59524, all fixtures wiped afterwards (balance restored to 1001, test service deleted, `gc_subscriptions` back to 0 rows). Owner click-through plus SQL-driven sweep runs proved: the frequency save; the member display and the recurring confirm modal; that first-redemption side effects are unchanged (bell, confirmation draft, pending queue); the renewal charge + email + re-anchor; sweep idempotency (a second run in the same day charged 0); the out-of-credits hold, its single Cc'd email, and that a second tick does not re-send it; the funded catch-up charging once (the #456 proof above); member cancel, admin cancel, and rejection auto-cancel + refund; a cancelled row ignored when due; an inactive service skipped in place; a stale-tab duplicate redeem refused with no double charge; and the admin mirror including an on-behalf redeem and the no-Buy-credits insufficient modal.

**Not exercised:** the forged cross-member `gc_cancel_subscription` 404 (the #455 negative case, code-proven only); the **yearly** interval, which never ran live at all — every live test was monthly, and `addInterval`'s yearly arm is spot-check/simulation only; the renewal email's `TEAM_MEMBER` Cc, which was added at the owner's request *after* the tested render, so the next renewal draft is that Cc's first verification; and an organic cron-fired run — every sweep run was hand-invoked.

**Superseded hub values moved here in this pass:** action count **477 → 480**; cron inventory **15 → 16 jobs, all active**; live `vfo-admin-api` **v796 → v797**. Route pages stayed 33 and the advisor baseline is unchanged.

**Discharged from the hub in this pass** (all fully settled, their prose retired from still-open OWED entries): the 2026-08-27 corporate-member branch's items (1) FE deploy and (3) the Wyatt `58147-C1` link resolution — both already marked DISCHARGED at their own ship, with the Wyatt link verified byte-identical to Sterling Hirsch's `stripe_account_id` and left linked deliberately; the 2026-08-26 Stopped-state branch's items (1) the FE deploy that closed the old-dropdown 400 window and (2) the #452 guard regression, fixed and live in v794 with plan 159 DB-verified untouched, plus that branch's shipped-gate list (smoke 5/5 vs v793, advisor GREEN after all three migrations, deno 0, build 33 pages, action count 473); the 2026-08-26 custom-retainer branch's discharged ship line (v792 deployed, `live-171-custom-split` landed, smoke re-run 5/5 vs v792); the 2026-08-26 four-feature branch's discharged item (1) (`live-170-cancel-misc` tagged, so the cancel UI, the two specialist email fields and the "No payout due" pill are live); the 2026-08-25 fee-process branch's three discharged items (1)–(3) (v787 + `npm run deploy` both landed, smoke 5/5 vs v787, and the `PENDING_minor_wording_tokens` SQL run post-v787 with all four rows verified tokened — the first real render of both tokens remains owed and stays in the hub); and the 2026-08-24 member-hold branch's discharged smoke gate (5/5 against the shipping v781, which carries v778's hold code).

## 2026-08-27 — Corporate Member lead in the header, a borrowed Stripe Connect account, a member Vault tab — and an IDOR found on the way past

**Three user-requested edits and one security fix, one chat, shipped as `vfo-admin-api` v796 with ONE migration (`20260827140000_member_stripe_linked_from.sql`, applied to prod BEFORE the deploy). Action count 473 → 477 (+1 members, +3 vault). `boldsign-webhook` untouched, still v40. The four revenue-share payout engines, `router/webhooks.ts`, and every existing `vault_gen_*` / `vault_tax_*` / `admin_ert_*` action were deliberately NOT touched.**

### Feature A — a Corporate Member's identity line names their lead member (frontend only)

A corporate member's profile header read `58147-C1 · Corporate Member · Active` — the suffix was the only clue whose corporate member they were. It now reads `58147-C1 · Corporate Member - Sterling Hirsch · Active`, on **both** the admin profile and the member's own portal profile (the user asked for both).

The lead is derived from the **member-number prefix** (`58147-C1` → `58147`), in the new shared `src/components/shared/corporateMember.js` (`CORPORATE_TYPES`, `isCorporateMember`, `leadMemberNumberOf`, `findLeadMember`). `members.connected_member_number` carries the same relationship and is preferred when non-empty, but the 2026-07-31 `member_connections` migration left it populated on only **3 of 40** corporate rows (#312) — the prefix resolves for **100% of the 40**, live-verified, and the 3 always agree. Three corporate types exist (`Corporate Member`, `Free Corporate Member`, `Free Corporate Member (Legacy)`; suffixes `-C<n>`, `-FC<n>`, `-FCL<n>`), and the helper tolerates both key spellings — admin roster rows carry `plugin_member_number`, the `load_data` blob aliases the same value to `member_number`.

`MembersPanel.jsx` renders it through `MemberNameLink` (an admin-only route) and dropped its local `CORPORATE_TYPES` const for the shared helper. `MemberPortal.jsx` renders the same line as **plain text**, because that link goes to `/admin`. **No backend field was needed:** the full roster was already fetched and discarded in `loadData` — it is now kept in state and passed to `MemberProfile`.

### Feature B — "Link to Lead Member's Stripe Connect" (backend + migration + frontend)

A corporate member with no Connect account of their own can have their rev-share paid into their **lead member's** account. **The mechanism is a COPY, and this is the load-bearing sentence: the lead's `stripe_account_id` is written onto the corporate member's row.** All four payout engines (`actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts:212`, `actions/tax/revshare.ts:227`, `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts:114`, `utils/specialist-revenue-payout.ts:392`) read `members.stripe_account_id` directly as the Stripe transfer `destination`; **none of them changed** — the copy IS the routing. The new `members.stripe_account_linked_from` (nullable text, no FK) is a **MARKER only**, naming whose account it is.

New action **`member_stripe_link_lead`** (`actions/members/stripe-link-lead.ts`, `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`), body `{ member_number, unlink?: true }`. The lead is resolved **server-side** from the member row — a lead id from the body would let a caller point any member's payouts at any account. It refuses: a non-corporate member type; an unresolvable lead; a lead that does not exist; a lead with no Stripe account; an **unlink when nothing is linked**; and a member who already has an account of their OWN (`stripe_account_id` set with no marker) — it will not clobber a real account id.

**The three guards are the reason this was built as link-and-guard rather than a bare copy** (gotcha #454). Each closes a hole the copy opens, because `stripe_account_id` is read by surfaces that mean *"this member's own account"*:

1. `actions/members/stripe-connect-request.ts` — **400s** for a linked member, naming the lead. Without it the setup email hands the corporate member an onboarding link **into the lead's Stripe account**.
2. `actions/payouts/connect-setup-link.ts` — the PUBLIC `/payout-setup?token=` page returns its **generic 404** for a linked member (reason logged, never leaked). Same hole, reached through a **durable token already sitting in an inbox** — closing only the admin button would have left it open.
3. `actions/payments/member-payments-load.ts` — skips the Stripe transfers-by-`destination` listing entirely and returns `payouts_linked_to: { member_number, name }`. Without it a linked member's Payments tab shows **the lead's whole payout history and every sibling corporate member's**.

Frontend: `MembersPanel.jsx` — a *"Borrowed Stripe Account"* label on the Details tab reading *"Payouts go to \<Lead\> (\<number\>)'s Stripe account"*, an Unlink with a confirm, the Link button beside the existing setup-email button (disabled with a tooltip when the lead has no account), the live status pill suffixed *"— \<Lead\>'s account"*, and the Settings tab showing the disclosure **instead of** the setup buttons. `MemberPaymentsTab.jsx` shows a note in place of the empty payout table.

### Feature C — a member Vault tab on their own client (backend + frontend, security-sensitive)

A member in the member portal (MSM → program → their client) now gets a **Vault** tab beside Profile. Permissions, chosen by the user (and amended mid-build — tax returns started view-only and became view+add): **General VIEW+ADD · Sensitive/tax-returns VIEW+ADD · ERT/VFOS VIEW ONLY.** No delete, no share, no request-documentation, no drag-to-move.

Three new actions — `member_client_vault_list`, `member_client_vault_download`, `member_client_vault_upload_url` (`actions/vault/member-client-vault-*.ts` + a shared file) — and **the gating is the interesting part.** None is in `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS` (that would 403 the surface they exist for) and **none is in `MEMBER_SCOPED_ACTIONS`**, which rewrites a `body.member_number` they never read and would therefore guard nothing (#455). Their confinement is the in-handler **`denyIfNotOwnClient`** (`utils/client-ownership.ts`), the **first statement of all three**, before any storage call — members are deny-by-**OMISSION** in `middleware/auth.ts`, so this is #309's shape, and `role-gates.ts` carries an 11-line comment naming the three actions and their guard so the next reader does not "fix" the omission.

**Bucket safety:** `member-client-vault-shared.ts` holds **TWO** maps — READ (`general`/`sensitive`/`ert`) and WRITE (`general`/`sensitive` only). `'ert'` is **ABSENT** from the write map rather than present-and-rejected, so widening READ can never widen WRITE. `bucketFrom()` is a `hasOwnProperty` **positive-allowlist** lookup with **no fallback** — deliberately unlike the older `memberBucketFor`, which silently defaults an unknown section to the general bucket (#204). Paths are built server-side as `${client_id}/${token32().slice(0,16)}_${safeName}`; the body selects neither bucket nor folder. Download additionally enforces `path.startsWith(`${client_id}/`)`; signed URLs are 300s.

A member upload fires the existing **`VAULT_planner_document_added`** bell through a new sibling helper `notifyMemberVaultDrop` — a sibling rather than a branch because `notifyPlannerVaultDrop` resolves a planner session first and would silently no-op for a member caller. Same rule key, same title shape, same recipients (Tracy + the client's assigned PF on their portal-login email), same fires-at-MINT-time caveat (#393). It **deliberately does NOT call `maybeStampAssessVaultUpload`**, which the admin/planner minters do: that stamp satisfies the **tax planner's** assess step for vault-assess groups, and a member dropping a file must never green a planner's step on their behalf.

Frontend: `ClientDetail.jsx` (member tab strip gains Vault; `validTabsForProgram`'s member array becomes `['home','vault']`) and `ClientVaultTab.jsx` (a new `memberMode` prop, `MEMBER_SECTIONS` beside the renamed `ADMIN_SECTIONS`; **every added condition is `&& !memberMode`**, so admin/planner rendering is bit-for-bit unchanged; the section blurb now accepts a JSX node so the General warning can bold without `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`). That warning reads exactly: *"General documentation only. **DO NOT UPLOAD TAX RETURNS OR SENSITIVE TAX DOCUMENTS HERE** — those belong in the Sensitive Documents section above."*

### Security fix — the `msm_load_clients` IDOR (found in passing, user approved folding it in)

Found while exploring the member portal for Feature C, by no gate and no report. **`msm_load_clients` took `enrollment_id` from the body and returned whole `clients.*` rows — names, emails, phones — with no ownership check.** Being in `MEMBER_SCOPED_ACTIONS` only rewrites `body.member_number`, which it never reads. Enrollment ids are sequential integers, so **any logged-in member could enumerate any other member's entire client list by incrementing a number.** `msm_load_training_progress` had the identical shape. Both now take `auth` and call the pre-existing `denyIfNotOwnEnrollment` first, with `dispatch.ts` passing `c.auth`. `msm_load_training_track` was checked and needs nothing — it keys on `program_id` and returns shared curriculum templates. See gotcha #455. **Shipped code-only: no forged-enrollment call was ever attempted.**

### Verification

`deno check --no-lock` **0** · action count **477** · `npm run build` exit 0, **33** route pages · security advisor at the **exact GREEN baseline** re-run after the migration (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN — an `ADD COLUMN` on an existing table never changes its policies) · **smoke gate 5/5 against v796**, run by Jake. Features A, B and C were all **user-tested live**, including Feature B's disabled negative case (Greg Keiper `59151-C1`, whose lead has no account) and its refusal path, and Feature C's uploads to both writable sections and downloads from all three. The IDOR fix is the one thing on this branch with no live exercise.

## 2026-08-27 — The ROI deck stops hard-coding "50%" and starts mirroring the revised tax fee process (template v6)

**One feature in one chat, shipped as `vfo-admin-api` v795. No frontend change, no migration, no new action — the count stays at 473. Template `ROI-template-master-v6.pptx` uploaded to the `presentation-templates` bucket BEFORE the deploy, v5 retained as the rollback. `boldsign-webhook` untouched, still v40.**

**The problem.** On 2026-08-25 a tax engagement stopped having one payment shape and started having two: at or below $30,000 the client pays a retainer and an implementation fee, each half the total; above $30,000 the retainer itself splits into a flat **$15,000 initial** and a **final** retainer of `total/2 − 15,000`. The client-facing ROI deck knew nothing about it. It had baked in the old shape as literal text — a *"One-Time Fee"* headline with two rows beneath it reading *"50% Planning & Education"* and *"50% Implementation"*, both filled from a single `{{FEE_HALF}}` token — plus three *"50% …"* chips on the Congratulations slide, a Double-Guarantee promising to refund *"the initial 50% tax plan retainer"*, and two speaker-note scripts that said *"50%"* out loud. **Every one of those was wrong for a plan above $30,000, on a slide the client reads in the meeting.**

**Template v6 — seven parts, and the reason a template cannot solve this alone.** A .pptx cannot branch, so v6 stops NAMING the rows and starts TOKENISING them, and the handler decides what goes in. Exactly seven parts differ from v5 — slides **24, 26, 27, 28, 29** plus **`notesSlide26`** and **`notesSlide27`** — built by the new committed `scripts/roi-presentation/make_v6.py` from the LIVE v5 object (base SHA `e479ad2a…`, so v5's two 2026-08-19 hot swaps are already in the base; v6's SHA is `1d8995d2…`):

- ***"One-Time Fee:"* → *"Total Fee:"*** on slides 24, 28 **and 29**. The label was three runs (`One` / `-` / `Time Fee:`, the hyphen carrying its own `rPr`); they collapse into one run reusing run 1's `rPr` verbatim, so the line renders in the same face it always did. **Slide 29 — the year-2 appendix — gets the label and nothing else:** it has no fee rows and its value stays the literal `"$0"`. Making all three fee surfaces agree was a user decision.
- **The two 50% rows on 24 and 28 became token rows, and a THIRD was cloned in** one row pitch (317400 EMU) lower. The label shapes' two runs collapse to one and **the colon moved inside the token's value** — a 3-payment label is not the 2-payment one with a word swapped, so *"Retainer:"* and *"Initial Retainer:"* are each a whole token. The value shapes keep their separate `"$"` run.
- **Slide 24's below-section moved DOWN 317400 EMU** to clear the new row — the *"Your investment in VFO Specialists:"* header and the *"Plan Investment: ${{CASH_OUTLAY}}"* row beneath it, the second of which hides its text in an `<a:t xml:space="preserve">` run that a naive scan misses. **Slide 28 was NOT shifted:** its rows sit higher and row 3 fit in the existing gap with 165000 EMU to spare.
- **Slide 27's three chips tokenised**, the literal *"50% "* prefixes gone. Chip 3's was a whole PARAGRAPH and was deleted whole; chip 1's amount lives in the same shape as its label, three centred paragraphs.
- **Slide 26's guarantee drops *"50% "***, and — the edit most easily forgotten — **so do both speaker scripts.** *"the initial 50% deposit"* → *"the initial deposit"* is a plain deletion; *"an initial invoice of 50% tax planning retainer"* → *"…of THE tax planning retainer"* had to be a **replacement**, because a bare deletion is ungrammatical and a presenter reads that line aloud.

`{{FEE_HALF}}` is retired outright. So is the string *"50%"*: **`make_v6.py` asserts a package-wide count of ZERO across all 570 entries, slides and notes alike** — a far stronger tripwire than "no 50% on the slides I edited", and the assert that caught the two notes parts in the first place. `NOTES_FIFTY_SURVIVORS` is left as an empty named dict so a future deliberate exception has a home instead of an edit to the assertion. Token count **22 → 31**: `FEE_ROW{1,2,3}_{LABEL,VALUE}`, `CHIP1_LABEL`, `CHIP1_VALUE`, `CHIP2_TEXT`, `CHIP3_VALUE` in, `FEE_HALF` out.

**The generator — a second, independent mode.** `threePayment = feeCents > THREE_PAYMENT_THRESHOLD * 100`, strict, so exactly $30,000 stays 2-payment. **`THREE_PAYMENT_THRESHOLD` and `INITIAL_RETAINER_FLAT` are IMPORTED from `constants/tax-fee-process.ts`, never re-typed** — the deck and the money can now never disagree about where 2 payments become 3, and a future change to either constant carries the deck with it automatically. The split is nonetheless computed **locally** in whole cents rather than by calling `deriveFeeSplit()`, which throws outside $0–$60,000: a legacy plan with an out-of-band assess fee must still generate a deck. The sum identity is asserted in code. In 2-payment mode `dropFeeRow3()` deletes the row-3 shapes from **both** fee slides and un-shifts slide 24 **only** (slide 28 passes `shiftBack=false` and must keep doing so).

**The composition problem, which is the part worth remembering (#453).** Slide 24 now takes up to two raw-XML surgeries before substitution, and **the fee surgery must run first** — its un-shift selects by an absolute y threshold that the header surgery would already have moved shapes above, so the wrong order fails loudly for entirely the wrong reason. Because the row surgery changes how many shapes sit below the header, the header surgery's expected count became mode-dependent (`SHIFT_EXPECTED_2PAY = 12` / `SHIFT_EXPECTED_3PAY = 14`) — and it is **passed in** rather than derived, deliberately, so that a silently no-opping row surgery cannot be quietly agreed with by the assertion that should have caught it. Each surgery asserts on its own evidence.

**Four user decisions shaped this.** (1) **One template, not two** — a branching handler over one master, rather than a 2-payment and a 3-payment package to keep in sync. (2) **The year-1 appendix mirrors the ROI slide** — slides 24 and 28 show the same three rows with the same values, because the fee is a single engagement-level figure attributed entirely to year 1. (3) **The deck always quotes the flat $15,000** — the 2026-08-26 custom-initial-retainer allowlist is deliberately NOT wired in, so an allowlisted client's deck shows the standard figure; the deck is generated on *"Tax 2 - Deeper Dive"*, upstream of the Tax 3 decision where a custom quote is taken, and the client sees their real numbers on the agreement and the invoice. (4) **De-percent everything**, including the two speaker scripts and slide 29's label, not just the slides whose numbers changed.

**What was tested, precisely.** Smoke gate **5/5 by the owner against v795**. Fixture plan **163** (test client 62), two rounds on the same plan, each deck downloaded via `/export/pptx` and checked mechanically. **2-payment $20,000** → Total Fee $20,000; rows Retainer $10,000 / Implementation $10,000; **no third row**; below-section back at v5 geometry; chips *"Retainer: $10,000 (refundable)"* / *"Retainer non-refundable"* / *"Implementation Fee: $10,000"*. **3-payment $46,038** → Total Fee $46,038; rows Initial $15,000 / Final $8,019 / Implementation $23,019; chips *"Initial Retainer: $15,000 (refundable)"* / *"Final Retainer: $8,019 (non-refundable)"* / *"Implementation Fee: $23,019"*. Both: 27 slides, zip clean, **package-wide "50%" count 0**, zero leftover tokens, zero *"Time Fee"* residue, guarantee reading *"refund the initial tax plan retainer quoted in today's meeting"*. The owner eyeballed both decks.

**What was NOT tested, and is now owed.** **(a) No TWO-YEAR deck has been generated against v6** — all four mode combinations pass in python simulation, but slide 28's mirrored rows and its no-shift geometry are simulation-verified only. **(b) The exact-$30,000 boundary** was simulated (stays 2-payment), never generated. **(c) A product gap this session found and did not close: nothing validates that the fee is less than the gross benefit.** Round 2's numbers produced a legitimately NEGATIVE *"Net Tax Savings"* of $(21,038) on a client-facing slide — fee $46,038 plus outlay $15,000 against $40,000 of savings. The arithmetic is correct and the deck rendered it honestly in accounting parentheses, but **no guard exists on the assess form**; the owner was told and made no decision. The same case surfaced a pre-existing cosmetic nobody had ever seen, because it is only visible on a negative net: the template's `$` sits OUTSIDE the token, so a negative renders `$(21,038)` rather than the conventional `($21,038)`.

**Cosmetics flagged and accepted, not blocking.** Chip 2's 3-payment string (~39 characters in a 1.36" box) may wrap to three lines — no collision, the next shape is ~120000 EMU clear, and the owner eyeballed it. Chip 3's text now sits ~5.3pt higher than chip 1's first line, a consequence of deleting chip 3's *"50% "* paragraph whole.

**Superseded values moved here from the hub and the docs this pass:** the live template object was `ROI-template-master-v5.pptx` at **22 tokens** (since v761/2026-08-19) and is now `…-v6.pptx` at **31**; the bucket held **NINE** objects as of 2026-08-19 and now holds **TEN**; `SHIFT_EXPECTED` was a single constant equal to **12** and is now the pair `SHIFT_EXPECTED_2PAY` 12 / `SHIFT_EXPECTED_3PAY` 14; `FEE_HALF = F/2` was the deck's fee-breakdown derivation and the only cents-tolerant token, and is now retired in favour of the six `FEE_ROW*` and four chip tokens; slide 29's label was *"One-Time Fee"*.

## 2026-08-26 — Stopping an engagement becomes a real column, and a tax allocation that used to destroy itself becomes two slots

**Two features in one chat, shipped as `vfo-admin-api` v793 with three migrations applied live, then `v794` for the guard regression the wrap-up doc audit caught (see the end of this entry).**

### Feature A — "Stopped" becomes a first-class state (MAP 1 + advisor / accountant / specialist onboarding)

**The problem.** Only specialist onboarding had a real `status` column. Everywhere else, "this engagement is over" was *inferred* — from a `final_decision` string, a `c13_decision`, a manual progress task — and a sweep cannot read an inference. So a client who had said no thank you kept being chased by three reminder ladders, and there was no way at all to stop an engagement that ended for a reason nobody had recorded in a decision field.

**What was built.** Two migrations, both bare `text` with no CHECK (#431) and both **NOT NULL DEFAULT** — deliberately, because the sweep filters are `.eq` and PostgREST `.neq` silently drops NULL rows (#437), so a nullable column would have hidden every legacy row from its own ladders:

- `20260826180000_pipeline_map1_status.sql` → `pipeline_map1.status` (`live`/`stopped`). Backfill on `c13_decision='No' OR c15_final_decision='No'` matched **0 rows**. `overview-map1.ts`'s third `declined` leg — a manual `client_progress` task — was deliberately **not** backfilled: it lives in another table keyed by program task ids and a wrong guess would silence a live engagement. The 2 clients that leg affects (102 Dan Niemerg, 136 Francisco Hervella) have no `pipeline_map1` row at all, so nothing was owed.
- `20260826181000_advisor_accountant_onboarding_status.sql` → `advisor_onboarding.status` + `accountant_onboarding.status` (`active`/`stopped`). Backfill flipped **exactly one row — accountant 24, Jon Bell** — and *that row is the whole point of the migration*: its value was `'Auto-Declined'`, the sweep's 14-day implicit No, and **the frontend classify had only ever tested for `'No'`**, so every auto-declined onboarding had been rendering as in-progress. A real live bug, found by writing the backfill predicate honestly. Two exclusions are deliberate: `'ExtraMeeting'` parks the decision while a meeting is pending, and `prelim_meeting_status='Request no meeting'` is the PFT fast-track, which means *proceeding without a meeting*, not stopping.

Three new admin actions (**470 → 473**): `map1_update_status`, `advisor_update_status`, `accountant_update_status` — all `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`, none tab-gated, each writing one column behind a positive value allowlist. Auto-stop writers were added to `pcadmin-final-decision` (No), `pcadmin-extra-meeting` (No), `pipfu-decision` (c13 No), advisor + accountant `client-decision` (No), `decision` (prelim No), `extra-meeting` (No), `prelim-meeting` (No Show), and the 14-day auto-decline, which now writes `status:'stopped'` beside `final_decision:'Auto-Declined'`. Deliberately **not** stopping: `ExtraMeeting`, `'Request no meeting'`, every tax handler, `agreements/declined.ts`.

**The user decision that shaped the rest: silence the ladders, never the money.** In `contract-revshare-sweep.ts` the six reminder-ladder queries (c14 / c17 / pay1, each in an email tier and a PF-bell tier) gained `.eq("status","live")` — and the rev-share candidate loop, the strategic-partner retry and the PIP held-release **in that same handler** were left unfiltered. `contract-chargescheduled-sweep.ts` and `contract-check-reminder-sweep.ts` were never opened. A signed client who owes money keeps being charged and chased after a stop; **cancelling money is a different tool** ("Cancel all remaining payments", shipped the day before). The advisor / accountant sweeps took the stricter version — all six ladders *and* the auto-decline — because no money path reads their column at all. Specialist sweeps were already filtered.

Also: `overview-map1.ts` gained a `closedReason` precedence rule (a recorded decline still reads *"Client declined"*, because that says why; plain *"Stopped"* is what is left for a hand-closed row) and `track_status` became `pd.status`, having been hard-coded `null`. `onboarding/update.ts` gained a `{active,stopped,completed}` allowlist as hardening. Frontend: a Live/Stopped toggle on the MAP 1 track header and on all three onboarding detail headers (hidden on completed rows), the advisor/accountant list classify now reads `ob.status`, and the specialist list — a flat list of every row until now — gained collapsible **Completed** and **Stopped** sections.

### Feature B — tax allocation becomes two slots

**The problem.** `client_tax_plans.tax_planner_id` had been carrying two different people at two different times: the partnership's **Team Member** coordinator holding the plan first, then the **Advanced Tax Planner**, by *overwrite*. The hand-off therefore destroyed the coordinator's connection to the client — bells stopped, the portal lost the row — and for the whole pre-hand-off window the one column that decides who gets paid pointed at somebody with no payout entitlement.

**What was built.** `20260826210000_tax_team_member_slot.sql` adds `tax_team_member_id` (bigint, nullable, no FK — `tax_planner_id`'s exact shape). The data move flipped **exactly one row**: plan 159, Katie Williams (ICG), out of the planner slot into the new column, with no money columns set, so no leg changed hands. `tax_allocate_planner` was reworked around it:

- **The slot is chosen by BODY KEY**, not by a role argument — `tax_planner_id` or `tax_team_member_id`, never both (400). **A missing key reads as the planner slot**, which is what keeps every pre-two-slot caller working untouched.
- **Role/slot enforcement in both directions**, with the fix in the error string; a legacy NULL `planner_role` reads as `'Tax Planner'`.
- **A state-based bell chain.** The old `planner_role === 'Team Member'` branch is *deleted as unreachable*. The hand-off ask now fires on the resulting STATE — team member set, planner empty — which correctly catches both the team member arriving *and* the planner slot being cleared out from under an existing one, and is silent when both slots are filled. The planner slot clears five bell prefixes; the team-member slot clears exactly one (its own ask, via the new `clearAllocatePlannerBells`); the withheld-share release is gated planner-slot-only.
- **Bells go to both slot-holders** (user decision). `notifyAllocatedPlanner` resolves both ids into `defaultRecipients`. **Emails deliberately did not move** — `taxPlannerEmail` / the `TAX_PLANNER` token stay planner-only.
- **Group scope widened to either slot** (`slotFilter()` in `tax-planner-ownership.ts`, all three deny\* guards; `portal-clients.ts` `.or()` over both). Before the hand-off the team member is the plan's only holder, so keying on the planner slot alone would have fenced them out of the very client they are being asked to allocate a planner for.

Eleven handlers had `tax_team_member_id` added to their explicit `.select(...)`. The resolver was built so that a miss would not have been fatal anyway — see #451 below.

**Four rounds of frontend iteration on user feedback** turned the single dropdown into select→Add with removable chips: chip order settled at `[name pill][×][Stripe chip]`; the step goes **green when either slot fills**, because allocating the team member is the admins' whole job on that step (the planner requirement is enforced downstream by the unchanged *"Allocate a Tax Planner (not a Team Member) first"* gate); the progress-row echo names the current holder; the admin dropdown lists Team Members first and offers Tax Planners only once a team member exists — **UI-only, the API accepts any order**; and in the planner portal the caller's own `self_role` decides write rights, with a **Tax Planner caller getting the step read-only, fail-closed** (an unresolved role, including the first paint, reads read-only).

### The six user decisions

1. Silence the reminder ladders on a stop — **but leave every money loop alone.** 2. Tax handlers keep their existing stop behaviour, unchanged. 3. Plan bells go to **both** slot-holders. 4. MAP 1 auto-stops on a recorded No. 5. Admin allocation dropdown lists **Team Members first**, planners after. 6. The portal allows removing **either** slot — but a **planner caller sees it read-only**.

### Gotchas

- **#451** — a shared resolver's optional column must distinguish `undefined` (the caller's select never carried it → look it up) from `null` (genuinely none), or every explicit-select caller silently drops the second recipient. The defensive half of #448, and the reason the one un-updated caller (`webhooks.ts`'s `mintDecision2Bell`) is merely a query slower rather than broken.
- **#452** — **splitting one column into two silently invalidates every OTHER guard that read the old column as "somebody is allocated", and the guards that break are the ones you did not touch.** `ready-for-tax3.ts` and `skip-roi-meeting.ts` both kept testing `!plan.tax_planner_id` while *meaning* "anybody" — their own error strings say *"Allocate a Team Member / Tax Planner"*, which is the tell. After the split, a plan held by a Team Member alone could neither send its ROI confirmation email nor skip the meeting: exactly the pre-hand-off state the feature exists to support. A second-order casualty: the branch's own team-member re-nag in `ready-for-tax3.ts` was **unreachable**, because the guard above it returned 400 first — dead code that read as a working feature.

### The regression, and the same-session fix (v793 → v794)

**Nothing in the feature work caught #452.** The build, `deno check` and the whole live click-through passed, because they exercised the *new* paths and never re-walked the old ones. It surfaced during the **wrap-up doc audit** — reading the guard while rewriting the allocation section and noticing its error string promised something the code no longer allowed. The doc sentence *"a Team Member is allocated, and Tray books the ROI meeting off the back of that allocation"* was a written-down invariant, and checking it against the diff is what exposed the break; that is the argument for auditing docs against the code rather than from memory.

**Fixed in the same session and shipped as `v794`.** Both guards widened to `!tax_planner_id && !tax_team_member_id`, and — the trap inside the fix — `skip-roi-meeting.ts`'s explicit `.select(...)` gained `tax_team_member_id`, without which the added term would have read `undefined` and left the guard permanently true. That is **#448 nested inside the fix for #452**: the audit rule caught the bug, and the audit rule was needed again to fix it correctly. The re-nag is reachable again.

**Zero live occurrences.** The only exposed row was `client_tax_plans` **159** (client 145, Katie Williams / ICG), the single plan the migration moved. It was DB-verified after the fix with `ready_for_tax3_email_sent`, `roi_meeting_skipped_at` and `tax3_meeting_date` all still NULL — neither guard ever fired during the hours v793 was live. Test plan 161 holds both slots and was never affected.

### Verification

`deno check` 0 · action count 473 · `npm run build` exit 0, 33 route pages · security advisor at the exact GREEN baseline (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN) after all three migrations, which only ADD columns to tables already carrying their deny-all policy · **5-pipeline smoke gate 5/5 PASS against v793** (run by the user) · Feature A live-tested against v793 + a dev-server frontend (Jon Bell in the Stopped section, his toggle both ways, advisor toggle round-trip, specialist sections + toggle, MAP 1 toggle + reload persistence) · Feature B live-tested on test client 62 plan 161, sandbox-forced (team-member-only allocation going green, hand-off from a Team Member portal login, planner add/remove/re-add, chip placement, dropdown ordering, and the Tax Planner portal read-only view).

**NOT touched:** `contract-chargescheduled-sweep.ts`, `contract-check-reminder-sweep.ts`, `boldsign-webhook` (still v40), `router/webhooks.ts`.

**One deploy-time nuance worth knowing, not a gotcha.** The #337 freshness check (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`) printed **1** in the edge worktree immediately before the v794 deploy, which normally means "you are about to deploy reverted code". Here it did not: the branch had been **squash-merged**, so main carried a new commit whose *content* was already in the worktree — `git diff origin/main --stat` was **empty**, which is the check that actually answers the question. The count is a history-shape measure and a squash merge deliberately changes history shape without changing content. **The commit count is still the right routine check; when it is non-zero, diff the content before concluding anything.**

**Shipped state:** backend `v794` (v793 plus the two widened guards), frontend deployed. Until that frontend deploy landed, production served the old single allocation dropdown against the new two-slot API, so allocating a Team Member 400'd with *"… is a Team Member — add them to the Team Member slot"* — the two deploys had to go together.

## 2026-08-26 — One client's initial retainer stops being $15,000, three three-payment predicates that had never once been true, and a card fee that was overwriting itself

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v789 → v790 → `v791`, and v791 is LIVE; `v792` is COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED** (`constants/tax-fee-process.ts`, `actions/tax/decision.ts`, `actions/tax/confirmation-email.ts`, `actions/tax/payment-email.ts`, `actions/tax/paidbycheck.ts`, `actions/tax/final-retainer-receipt.ts`, `actions/tax/implementation-receipt.ts`, `actions/tax/invoice-receipt.ts`, `router/webhooks.ts`, `utils/tax-invoice-html.ts`; migration `20260826170000_tax_per_payment_card_fees.sql`, applied live via MCP **and** committed as a file). **Frontend: `src/components/admin/tax/TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` — `npm run deploy` OWED, so the custom-split control is production-invisible.** Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-79fcb8`, the second branch of the day, one chat. **`boldsign-webhook` was NOT touched and remains at v40.** Gotchas **#448**–**#450**.

Three pieces of work, and the middle one exists only because the first one was being tested. The revised tax fee process shipped the day before (2026-08-25, `fee_process_version='2026-08-25'`); putting one real client through it end-to-end found three live bugs in it, and putting a *second* payment through it found a schema defect that predates it.

**1. A custom initial retainer, for a two-client allowlist.** The revised process derives everything from ONE total: above $30,000 the retainer is collected in two payments, a **flat $15,000 initial retainer** plus a final retainer of `total/2 − 15000`. Chris Colby (`clients.id=105`, ref 59481-002) is the first engagement that could not be priced that way — total **$46,038** with an initial retainer of **$8,331.50**, final **$14,687.50**, implementation **$23,019**. `constants/tax-fee-process.ts` gained `CUSTOM_SPLIT_CLIENT_IDS: number[] = [105, 62]` (62 is the standing sandbox-forced Test Client, member 59524, kept on the list **so the path stays click-testable** rather than only reachable through a live engagement), and `deriveFeeSplit(total, customInitial?)` takes an optional second argument in dollars that **replaces** `INITIAL_RETAINER_FLAT`. It throws on anything else: a custom value on a 2-payment total, or a value outside `0 < customInitial < retainerHalf` (new exported `CUSTOM_INITIAL_NOT_THREE_PAYMENT_MESSAGE`, `CUSTOM_INITIAL_RANGE_MESSAGE`, `CUSTOM_INITIAL_NOT_ALLOWED_MESSAGE`).

**The opt-in is per-call-site, not per-constant, and that is the safety.** `parseFeeTotal(fd, opts?: FeeParseOptions)` reads `fd.customInitialRetainer` and **refuses it unless `opts.allowCustomInitial`**; `buildFeeColumns(plan, fd, opts?)` threads the same options through. `actions/tax/decision.ts` is the **only** caller that passes the opt-in, and it passes it only when `CUSTOM_SPLIT_CLIENT_IDS.includes(plan.client_id)`. `pricing.ts`, `extra-meeting.ts` and the Undecided branch pass no options at all, so a `customInitialRetainer` key arriving at any of them — from a hand-crafted call or a future copy-paste — is rejected by default rather than honoured. The Undecided quote still quotes the flat $15,000 on every client including an allowlisted one; that divergence is deliberate and was left alone.

**Amendments needed no change whatsoever, and that is worth recording as a property of the 2026-08-25 design rather than luck.** Every arm of `actions/tax/amend-fee.ts` reads the ROW's `initial_retainer_amount` / `retainer_amount`, never the flat constant, so a custom initial survives a Tax 4 amendment, the `≤ $30,000` conversion, the conversion back, and Tax 5 intact. The Tax 4 amend floor — which refuses a total at or below twice the initial — therefore quotes the custom figure, not $15,000, with no code touched.

**Frontend.** `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` mirrors the constant and both `deriveFeeSplit` / `feeSplitFromInput` second arguments (the three-copy coupling of **#440**, now with a fourth thing to keep in step). `TotalFeeField` gained optional `rangeInvalid` and `children` props, both defaulting to prior behaviour, so the custom control can render **inside** the total field without the total's own range error firing on an invalid custom value. A pill toggle **"Allow custom split"** appears only for an allowlisted client and only once the typed total is in 3-payment territory, and the payload key `customInitialRetainer` is **absent** unless the toggle is on and the value valid — the backend refusal is the second gate, not the first. The control is deliberately named nothing like the pre-existing `splitType === 'Custom'` in the same form, which is the **revenue** split (member / planner / VFOS): two unrelated concepts a shared word would have merged.

**2. Three live bugs in the 2026-08-25 fee process, all one root cause.** Testing the above surfaced a retainer-paid PF bell reading *"paid the $23,019.00 retainer"* where it should have read *"$8,331.50 initial retainer"*. The cause was not the wording logic: `actions/tax/confirmation-email.ts`'s `.select(...)` fetched `fee_process_version` and `initial_retainer_amount` but **omitted `final_retainer_amount`** — the column `isThreePaymentPlan` is keyed on (**#440**). PostgREST returns the row without the unselected column, the property is `undefined`, and the predicate is therefore **always false**: every 3-payment plan was silently treated as 2-payment, with no error and no missing-field symptom, because the false branch is the pre-existing legacy behaviour. Auditing the other consumers found the same omission in two more handlers, both of them worse:

- `actions/tax/payment-email.ts` — **live-wrong on real sends.** `[RETAINER_LABEL]` and `[LATER_PAYMENTS]` are present in `email_templates` rows 22 and 131 *today*, so the payment email said "retainer" and promised only "the implementation fee" to a client who still owed a final retainer. The in-file comments asserting those tokens were "no-op on today's bodies" were **stale** and were corrected in the same change — a doc-vs-code drift where the code loses (**#399**).
- `actions/tax/paidbycheck.ts` — **live-wrong and the most serious of the three.** A check-paying client on a 3-payment plan would have been asked to write a check for the **full $23,019 retainer** instead of the $8,331.50 initial.

A full audit of all **21** consumers of `isThreePaymentPlan` / `isNewFeeProcess` / `isLegacyFeeRow` found no further gaps — every other site either uses `select("*")` or already carries the column — and confirmed no **#427**-class stale-row mutation anywhere in the family. Shipped as **v791**, after which the corrected bell was confirmed live. Written up as **#448**, which is the enforcement half of #440: a predicate is only as good as the SELECT feeding it.

**3. `card_processing_fee` was one column that three different charges wrote.** Each tax charge — retainer, final retainer, implementation — stamped `client_tax_plans.card_processing_fee`, overwriting the last. Proven live rather than reasoned about: an $8,331.50 initial retainer stamped **$249.14**, then the $11,668.50 final retainer replaced it with **$348.80**, and the initial payment's fee no longer existed anywhere on the row. Nothing was corrupt — every receipt renders at charge time from the just-written value and is then a static PDF — so the loss shows up only on a **re-render**, which is exactly what the new fresh-invoice paths do. The strongest signal was already in the code: two receipt handlers passed `cardProcessingFee: 0` with comments explaining that the column holds *this* charge's fee and therefore could not be trusted for the invoice's retainer row. That workaround documented the defect precisely while normalising it (**#450**).

Migration `20260826170000_tax_per_payment_card_fees.sql` adds nullable `numeric` columns **`final_retainer_card_fee`** and **`implementation_card_fee`**, plus `comment on column` on all three stating which payment each one describes — the ownership belongs in the database, not only in the handler. **No backfill, deliberately:** production exposure was verified to be exactly zero (no plan carries `fee_process_version`, `final_retainer_amount` or `final_retainer_status`), so there is nothing to move and a backfill could only invent values. No RLS work was needed — adding columns to an existing table does not change its policies. `router/webhooks.ts`'s `payment_intent.succeeded` final-retainer and implementation branches now write their own columns and the retainer writer is untouched, keeping `card_processing_fee` pinned to the FIRST retainer payment so no legacy reader or writer had to move. Readers were repointed: `final-retainer-receipt.ts` → `final_retainer_card_fee`, `implementation-receipt.ts` → `implementation_card_fee`, `confirmation-email.ts` kind-branched (with `implementation_card_fee` added to its select — the same discipline #448 is about), and `invoice-receipt.ts` left reading `card_processing_fee`, which is correct because that IS the first retainer payment.

**Both re-issued invoices now pass the real fee instead of `0`.** `utils/tax-invoice-html.ts` renders its card-fee row exclusively against the first retainer payment (*"Total Charged for Initial Retainer"* / *"for Retainer"*, amount = initial + fee), so `0` was a workaround for the shared column and not a semantic requirement. Passing `plan.card_processing_fee` restores parity between a fresh amended invoice and the original.

**4. Chris Colby's plan 58 was reset mid-flight, by hand, on a live client.** He had signed a contract quoting the pre-2026-08-25 numbers ($16,663 total) and held a live payment link; the engagement is being re-done under the new process with the custom split. By SQL: `checkout_token` and `payment_email_sent_at` nulled (killing the link **and** disarming the payment-reminder ladder in one move), agreement / BoldSign / signature fields and `stripe_customer_id` cleared, signing and payment ladder stamps nulled, and the fee columns `total_fee`, `retainer_amount`, `implementation_amount` nulled. **That last one is load-bearing, not tidiness:** with the old total still present, `buildFeeColumns` would have taken the `isLegacyFeeRow` path and silently ignored the custom split entirely. The legacy fee keys were stripped from the step's `notes` JSON for the same reason on the frontend. **His old countersigned BoldSign contract still exists and must be voided by hand.**

**What was proven live, and what was not.** Everything in section 1 and section 2 was click-tested against the deployed version on Test Client 62 (sandbox-forced, all fixtures since deleted): the custom split written cent-exact ($46,038 → 8,331.50 / 14,687.50 / 23,019, version stamped); the 3-payment agreement rendering all three figures; the initial retainer paid by card with the fee derived from **$8,331.50** ($249.14) and not from the full retainer; the Tax 4 amend floor refusing a total at or below twice the custom initial with a message quoting **"$16,663.00"**, which is the proof that the guard reads the ROW and not the $15,000 constant; a Tax 4 amendment $46,038 → $40,000 re-deriving a final retainer of $11,668.50 with cent-exact share re-scaling and a clean audit row; **the `≤ $30k` conversion SAVED for the first time** ($25,000 → `final_retainer_amount` NULL, `initial_retainer_amount` KEPT, retainer becomes the paid $8,331.50, implementation $16,668.50) **and the conversion back** — discharging the largest gap the 2026-08-25 entry left open; and a full second pass on a fresh plan through Client decision 1, with the final retainer charged, receipt plus fresh invoice issued, and **both** revenue-share transfers (member and tax planner) completing on the FULL $20,000 retainer through the deferred mechanism.

**What that does not cover, stated plainly.** **Every member-paying twin of the custom split is unexercised** — agreement row 24 and the member templates; the whole feature has only ever run client-paying. **ACH and check appear nowhere in the custom-split flow** — card only, throughout. The custom split has never run on a 2-payment total and by construction never can, and the Undecided quote path still deliberately quotes the flat $15,000. **Section 3 is CODE-ONLY: `v792` is not deployed at the time of writing, and neither new column has ever been written or read by a real payment** — the migration IS applied to production, so the columns exist and are NULL everywhere. Separately, `webhooks.ts`'s fresh-`/tax-pay`-link final-retainer branch (`checkout.session.completed`) writes **no card fee at all** and never did — a pre-existing gap left unchanged, so a card-paid fresh-link final retainer whose `payment_intent.succeeded` never lands leaves `final_retainer_card_fee` NULL and the receipt omits the fee breakdown entirely. And `plan.payment_method_type` is **still** a single shared column across all three payments, so a re-issued invoice for a plan whose payments used different methods reads the LATEST method and can drop the initial retainer's card-fee disclosure; that is the same family as section 3, is knowingly unfixed, and is named in **#450**. `actions/tax/charge-implementation.ts` around line 124 computes a `const cardFee` that is never used — dead since before this change, left alone.

**Gotchas.** **#448** (a discriminator column missing from a handler's `.select(...)` makes its predicate silently, permanently false — the enforcement half of #440), **#449** (a date-less Stripe idempotency key is scoped to a logical payout, so an amendment inside 24 hours collides, and an amount that has NOT changed replays the earlier transfer as a fresh success), **#450** (a column named for a concept that occurs more than once per record will be overwritten by each occurrence; the tell is a caller passing `0` instead of reading it).

**Gates.** `deno check --no-lock` **0 errors**; action count **470**, unchanged — the custom split added no dispatch action, only an optional argument; `npm run build` exit 0, **33 route pages**; cron inventory **15 jobs, all active**; sandbox posture **all 8 pipelines live** (the testing used the client-keyed force on member 59524, #251, so the global toggles never moved). The security advisor was re-run after the migration and returned the documented baseline **exactly** — 5 deny-all `rls_enabled_no_policy` INFO plus the `pg_net` `extension_in_public` WARN, nothing else — which is the expected result for a migration that only ADDS COLUMNS to a table already carrying its deny-all policy. **The one gate that is NOT green against the shipping version: the 5-pipeline smoke gate passed 5/5 but against `v790`, two deploys ago.** It has not been re-run against `v791` or `v792`, and per the wrap-up's own rule an earlier version's green is not this version's green — it is carried as an OWED line in the hub rather than counted here.

## 2026-08-26 — Cancelling the payments a client will never make, and three smaller corrections that each removed an email nobody wanted

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v787 → v788 → `v789`, and v789 is LIVE** (24 files changed + 1 new handler `actions/payments/cancel-remaining.ts`, + 3 migrations, all three applied live AND committed: `20260826120000_experts_personal_email.sql`, `20260826150000_cancel_remaining_stamps.sql`, `20260826160000_specrev_connect_reminder_stamps.sql`). **Frontend: 7 files changed — `npm run deploy` OWED, so every surface below is production-invisible.** Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-ab28d3`, one chat, no handoffs. **`boldsign-webhook` was NOT touched and remains at v40.** Three `notification_rules` seeded live; three `email_templates` bodies edited live by SQL with no deploy. Gotchas **#444**–**#447**. Action count **469 → 470**.

Four unrelated pieces of work rode one branch. Three of them are subtractions — an email that should not have been sent, a button that should not have been offered, a sentence that invited a reply nobody reads — and the fourth is the first thing in this system that can tell a payment schedule to stop.

**1. "Cancel all remaining payments" — and the sweep predicate that would have ignored it.** A new superadmin-only action `payments_cancel_remaining` backs a button at the bottom of an expanded MAP 1 or Tax group on the admin client Payments tab. It writes the literal status `'cancelled'` onto every still-uncollected slot in ONE engagement group plus a `*_cancelled_at` audit stamp, and does nothing else: no Stripe call, no email, no bell, no revenue-share column. What is cancellable is a **positive allowlist** (`NULL`/`''`, `declined`, `auth_required`, `manual_required`) rather than a denylist, per **#431**; `succeeded`, `processing`, `pending` and `check_pending` mean money is collected or in flight and are refused. **MAP 1 payment 1 is deliberately excluded**: it is the engagement's opening payment, not an installment — a NULL `pay1_status` means the client has not paid anything yet, the `/pay` link is live, and payments 2–4 do not even have dates until it settles. "Cancel the remaining payments" on such a row really means "cancel the engagement", which is a different decision with different consequences. Nothing touches `rec{N}_*` or the tax `*_rev_share` legs, because writing a terminal value onto a payout leg for money that was never collected is how money gets silently swallowed (**#303**/**#377**).

**The companion change is the one that mattered.** `contract-chargescheduled-sweep.ts` chose what to charge with a **denylist** — `skipStatuses = {succeeded, processing, pending, declined, auth_required}`, i.e. *charge unless the status is one of these five*. That was correct only because those five plus NULL were all the values that existed. Introducing a sixth would have had the nightly cron **charging every cancelled installment**, off-session, on saved cards, against precisely the clients VFO had just decided to stop billing. `skipStatuses` is deleted and the gate is now `if (status) continue;` — charge only an untouched slot. The behaviour is identical for every value the column has ever held (a check row never reaches the loop; the select filters `payment_method_type` to card/ach), so this is a no-op today and a load-bearing guard tomorrow. Written up as **#444**, the money-side twin of #431.

Roughly a dozen readers were then taught that `'cancelled'` means CLOSED: both passes of `contract-check-reminder-sweep.ts`, `contract-checkcleared.ts` (refuses to clear it), `migration/connect-load.ts`, `migration/outstanding-links.ts`, `utils/migration-schedule.ts` (the emailed schedule table), `payments/card-update-shared.ts` (not a future charge), `clients/overview-map1.ts` (no next-action), `tax/charge-final-retainer.ts` + `tax/charge-implementation.ts` (a 400 **before** any Stripe call), `tax/load-payment.ts` + `tax/stripe-checkout.ts` (a closed state on the public `/tax-pay` page), and `utils/map1-open-installment.ts` (comment only — it already tested for a NULL status). In `payments/normalize.ts` the `PayStatus` union gained `'cancelled'` with a `VFO_CANCELLED` display constant and a red chip, and the implementation `revShareStatus` now reports `hasCharge=false` on a cancelled slot. **`normStatus` itself is deliberately unchanged** — its FAILED set still contains Stripe's own `canceled` spelling, which is a different thing arriving from a different place, and collapsing the two would have made a VFO decision indistinguishable from a Stripe outcome.

**The webhook does not skip a cancelled slot that gets paid anyway.** If money lands on an installment VFO already cancelled — a client using an old `/pay` link, a late ACH — the P2–P4 succeeded branch still records `succeeded`, still issues the receipt and still runs the revenue share, because **the money is real and refusing to book it would only lose it**. What it additionally does is raise an action-required bell, `FAILURE_map1_cancelled_installment_collected` (rule seeded live, to Jake), asking a human whether a refund is owed. Recording the money and escalating the contradiction is strictly safer than either alternative.

**2. The portal-setup button came out of all four first-payment emails, and a column lost its last writer.** The TAX pair (`TAX_invoicereceipt_email`, `TAX_invoicereceipt_retainer`) had the `[PORTAL_SETUP]` token stripped from their bodies by live SQL — no deploy needed. **For rollback: the removed tail on both rows was the literal string `[PORTAL_SETUP]` at the end of the body, nothing else.** The MAP 1 pair moved in code: `contract-invoice-receipt.ts`'s `[TAX_UPLOAD]` token now renders **only** the tax-form block, with the portal intro sentence and the `#00488d` *"Set up your secure portal login"* button deleted from all four of its cases. **For rollback, the code-side strings removed were** the `portalIntro` variants (*"Finally, … can now set up their secure client portal login using the button below:"* and its member-paid twin) and that button. Because a non-tax client's block now collapses to nothing, the substitution is spelled `replace(/\[TAX_UPLOAD\]<br>/…)` so the template's trailing `<br>` is swallowed along with it — the empty case renders clean rather than leaving a stray blank line. `tax/invoice-receipt.ts`'s dead `[PORTAL_SETUP]` path was deleted outright.

The consequence is the interesting part. **Both handlers stopped minting `clients.client_setup_token`, so that column now has no writer anywhere in the system** — while `/client-setup` and its two readers (`load_client_setup` / `submit_client_setup`) still exist and still work. Every static signal says dead code; it is not, because every client ever sent a first-payment email holds a live link to it. That state is **orphaned, not retired**, and it is now said in those words at the column, at the route, in the action catalog and in the auth doc, precisely so the next tidy-up pass does not delete a working route on impeccable reasoning (**#446**). A client's route into the portal is now the manual login-setup email to `/set-password`. This was raised as a decision and accepted, not discovered as a bug.

**3. `TAX_request_additional_info` stopped inviting a reply.** Rewritten by live SQL, no deploy. **Prior body, in full, for rollback:** `Dear [Client First],<br><br>We are requesting the following additional information:<br><br>[REQUESTED_INFO]<br><br>Please use the secure button below to provide the additional information:<br><br>[UPLOAD_BUTTON]<br><br>If you have any questions, please reply all to this email and we'd be happy to help!<br><br>Thank you,`. The closing reply-all invitation and the old button intro are gone; the intro now reads `<b>Please do not reply to this email.</b> Instead, use the secure button below to provide the additional information:`. Its three siblings — `TAX_request_returns`, `TAX_request_returns|holistic` and `VAULT_request_documentation` — were **deliberately left alone** at the user's decision, so the family now diverges on purpose and should not be "reconciled".

**4. Specialists gained a work/personal email split, and the payload contract that makes it dangerous.** `experts.personal_email` mirrors the member change from v765: **record-only, never emailed**, and deliberately absent from the narrow `anon`/`authenticated` column grant (re-verified — that grant is still its original short list). `SpecialistsPanel.jsx` labels the two fields side by side (*"Work email (emails sent here)"* / *"Personal email (not emailed)"*), `SpecialistOnboarding.jsx` says *"Work Email \*"*, and every specialist send-site was checked to read `experts.email`. **The trap is that the `experts` payload redacts in the opposite direction from the members payload.** Members' is `select` over an explicit column list — additive, so a new column is private by default and a forgotten entry is a loud missing field. `experts` is `select("*")` followed by **subtractive** per-caller redaction, so a new column is **exposed by default** and a forgotten strip leaks silently to every non-admin caller with no symptom at all. `personal_email` therefore had to be added to **three** strip sites — `data/load-data.ts` (non-admin branch), `data/specialist-showroom-load.ts` and `data/client-showroom-load.ts`. That inversion is now **#445**, admitted to the hub's curated list, because it is a security contract and the members precedent actively misleads.

**5. The $0.00 email that had been going out every night.** The complaint that opened this was concrete: `SPECREV_connect_setup` was **real-sending** *"revenue share payment of $0.00"* daily to an Elite Resource Team member, line 40 of request 27. Two independent bugs stacked. First, a zero `member_share` had no branch of its own and fell all the way through to the no-Connect-account arm, which minted an account, sent the setup email and parked `awaiting_connect` — a status inside `PAYABLE_STATUSES`, so the nightly sweep re-entered the line forever. Second, and the reason the re-send existed at all, **the email carried a raw Stripe `account_links` URL, which expires in minutes**; it *had* to be re-minted to stay valid, so the daily send was a technical constraint masquerading as a chasing policy. Nobody had chosen it (**#447**).

The zero case is now the **first** branch in the chain: `memberShare <= 0` writes the terminal `payout_status='no_payout_due'`, retires any held bell an earlier run parked on the line (`clearJakeFailure`), and sends, mints, charges and notifies **nothing** — `email_drafted_at` and `payout_sent_at` both stay NULL, because nothing was drafted and no money moved. It gets its own `zero` counter rather than folding into `sent`, since both callers spread the summary straight into their JSON and `sent` must never report money that did not move. **It sits ABOVE Money Mapping, which is the one place this engine deliberately diverges from MAP 1's `contract-revshare.ts`**, where Money Mapping comes first and a $0 line settles as "Money Mapping". There, the notice is a draft and the value is just a column; here it would real-send *"$0.00 allocated to money mapping"* and stamp two timestamps for an email not worth sending. A $0 allocation is not an allocation. Nothing downstream loses by the ordering — the reconciliation panel buckets dollars off `revenue_decision`, not `payout_status`. The old, unreachable $0 block that wrote the terminal `revenue_share_sent` was deleted.

The status vocabulary is now written down exhaustively at the engine, which is the column's only writer: **non-terminal** (= `PAYABLE_STATUSES`) `pending` · `awaiting_connect` · `failed` · `held_member_suspended` · `held_member_paused`; **terminal** `revenue_share_sent` · `money_mapping` · `no_payout_due`. The stale five-value enum comment in the `20260629000000` migration was **deliberately not edited** — a migration comment is a dated snapshot, not a constraint (**#431**).

The email itself became **once-only**, guarded on a pre-write read of `email_drafted_at` and stamped only on an actual send, and its button became the **durable `/payout-setup?token=` page** (`ensureConnectSetupToken` — one token per entity, shared with the four existing "Set Up Payment Details" flows), which never expires and mints a fresh Stripe onboarding link per click, covering a brand-new and a half-built account with one path (**#268**). Chasing then moved to where chasing belongs: two new sweep passes in `payout-sweep.ts`, **2c** at 2 business days (`SPECREV_connect_reminder_email` — re-sends the same template with a *"Reminder: "* subject and the same durable link, stamps `connect_reminder_sent_at`) and **2d** at 4 business days (`SPECREV_connect_tracy_bell` — a **dismissible** FYI to Tracy, stamps `connect_pf_notified_at`). Both are once-only by an `IS NULL` clause in their own candidate queries, both paced with `businessDelayCutoffIso` (**#396**/**#397**), both rule-configurable so an operator can re-time or switch them off without a deploy. **Member-with-no-account lines are excluded from both tiers by construction** — their `email_drafted_at` is NULL because nothing is ever drafted to them, and their nag remains the action-required `SPECREV_member_share_held` bell. The migration adds no backfill on purpose: every column starts NULL, so the first sweep after deploy sends exactly one final reminder to lines that had been receiving the same email daily, and then stops. On the frontend `specialistRevenueShared.jsx` gained a grey *"No payout due"* pill; the reconciliation and automation panels needed only comments, since their positive sets already exclude the new status.

**What was proven live, and what was not.** The MAP 1 half of cancel was click-tested for real against `v789`: client 149 / `pipeline_map1` 130 had payments 3 and 4 cancelled, with the chips, the tally, the button correctly disappearing afterwards and persistence across a reload; an all-paid client showed no button; the member, specialist and global payment surfaces showed none either, and the global page rendered read-only. The specialist Work/Personal email fields were saved, loaded and persisted, then cleaned up. **That is the whole of the live coverage.** The **entire Tax side of cancel is code-only** — final-retainer and implementation cancel, every refusal branch, the `/tax-pay` closed state. **The inverted sweep predicate has not yet met a cancelled row**: the next 03:00 UTC pass over client 149 is its first live proof, and until then "the sweep will not charge a cancelled slot" is an argument, not an observation. The cancelled-collected bell and its rule have never fired, nor have the checkcleared refusal, the check-reminder skip, the `/connect-card` quote, the outstanding-links count, the migration-schedule table, the card-update gates or the overview-map1 suppression. The repeat-click and Pay-in-Full count-0 branches are unreachable from the UI once the button hides, and are accepted as such. No email render was verified: the MAP 1 `[TAX_UPLOAD]` seam in both its `hasTax` and `!hasTax` shapes, the TAX retainer render and the next `TAX_request_additional_info` draft are each their own first verification. `personal_email`'s absence from the portal payloads was proven by code and by the grant, never eyeballed from a non-admin login. On SpecRev, line 40 closes at the next 11:00 UTC sweep as `no_payout_due` with no email — the inbox staying quiet is the test — and **the once-only initial email, the durable link, the 2-day reminder and the 4-day Tracy bell have never fired live**, because no non-zero `awaiting_connect` line exists to fire them. Until `npm run deploy` lands, production renders a cancelled row as a grey *"Not paid"* through the STATUS fallback (harmless, verified against `origin/main`) and the new pill renders *"Pending"* through the shared default arm.

**Gates.** `deno check --no-lock` 0 errors; action count 470 (the +1 is `payments_cancel_remaining`); `npm run build` exit 0, 33 route pages; the security advisor at exactly the documented baseline (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN), re-confirmed after all three migrations and all three seeds — every one of them only adds columns to tables that already carry their deny-all policy, and adding a column never changes a table's policies; the 5-pipeline smoke gate 5/5, run by Jake against `v789` and again earlier against `v788`.

**Superseded hub values moved here.** Action count **469 → 470**; live `vfo-admin-api` **v787 → v789** (`boldsign-webhook` unchanged at v40). The 2026-08-20 `login_type` entry (**#425**/**#426**, v772) was **removed from the hub as fully discharged** — re-verified this session, `admin_sessions` holds 8 rows with **zero** NULL `login_type`, so the legacy email-precedence fallback is unreachable in practice and retiring that code is a safe cleanup rather than an owed item; the rule itself survives in the hub's curated list. Three separate "Flagged, not built" hub bullets (2026-08-14 `payout_status`/`revPaidValue`, 2026-08-16 `tax/decision.ts`, 2026-08-17 `tax4_meeting_date`) were **merged into one bullet** with the new `client_setup_token` orphaning added as its fourth clause — nothing was dropped. `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md`'s per-area snapshot moved **VFO Specialist Revenue 9 → 12** (the old 9 was already stale — `SPECREV_member_share_held` had been added on 2026-08-24 without the count table being touched) and **Payment Failure Alerts 18 → 19 live / 17 → 18 documented**; the residual one-row gap is `FAILURE_tax_planner_share`, which exists live and has never been written up, and is now named in that file's caveat rather than left looking like an arithmetic error. GOTCHAS **#341** was amended in place: its claim that the MAP 1 invoice/receipt handler *"mints only `client_setup_token` (the portal-setup link, unchanged)"* is superseded — the handler now mints nothing at all.

## 2026-08-25 — Revised tax planning fee process: one total in, amounts derived, a three-payment retainer above $30k, and two steps that can re-price a signed engagement

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v781 → v782 → v783 → v784 → v785 → v786, and `v787` is COMMITTED BUT NOT DEPLOYED — v787 is the version that ships** (30 files + 1 applied migration + 6 pending-SQL records: new `actions/tax/amend-fee.ts`, `charge-final-retainer.ts`, `final-retainer-receipt.ts`, new `constants/tax-fee-process.ts`, new `utils/tax-invoice-html.ts`, new `utils/tax-review-bell.ts`, plus `router/dispatch.ts`, `router/webhooks.ts`, `constants/role-gates.ts`, `utils/tax-plan-steps.ts`, `actions/payments/normalize.ts`, `actions/holistic/tax-load.ts` and thirteen `actions/tax/*` handlers; migration `20260825120000_tax_fee_process_v2026_08_25.sql`). **Frontend: 6 files changed — `npm run deploy` OWED, production still runs `live-168`.** Branch `claude/tax-planning-portal-additions-8cf096`, one long chat, no handoffs. **`boldsign-webhook` was NOT touched and remains at v40.** New flow doc: [flows/tax-fee-process.md](flows/tax-fee-process.md). Gotchas **#438**–**#443**.

**What this is.** From 2026-08-25 a NEW tax engagement is priced from **one input — the total fee** — and every payable amount is derived server-side. Below $30,000 nothing visible changes: two payments, 50:50. **Above $30,000 the retainer is collected in TWO payments** — a flat **$15,000 initial retainer** at the retainer step and a **final retainer** (`total/2 − 15000`) collected later — making the engagement a three-payment shape. `$60,000` is a hard cap. Two new admin-only steps can **re-price a signed engagement** before the client's next decision email goes out. **Legacy plans are untouched forever**, and that is enforced by a column, not by care: `client_tax_plans.fee_process_version` is NULL on every plan priced before today, no revised-process validation applies to a NULL row, and the stamp can only be written while `retainer_status IS NULL` — so a plan holding retainer money can never change process in either direction.

**Why `retainer_amount` did not change meaning.** The obvious implementation — make `retainer_amount` the first of three payments — would have rewritten every invoice, receipt, revenue-share and sweep calculation in the tax pipeline. Instead `retainer_amount` **stays the full 50% retainer in both shapes**, and the 3-payment split describes only *how* that retainer is collected (`initial + final === retainer`, always, in whole cents). Every pre-existing calculation kept working untouched, including `actions/tax/revshare.ts`, which needed **no change at all**. The cost of that choice is a trap the branch then had to pay for twice: any code reading `retainer_amount` as "one payment that moved" is wrong on a 3-payment plan. It bit the **Payments tab** (which showed the full retainer as a single collected payment) and, more seriously, the **Stripe webhook's card-fee derivation**, which grossed the received $15,000 against the full retainer and wrote a large **negative** `card_processing_fee`. Both were fixed here; the webhook fix was proven live at `+$448.30`.

**The deferred retainer revenue share — the part that needed the most care.** On a 2-payment plan the client's green click on Client decision 1 releases the retainer revenue share immediately, as it always has.
