On a 3-payment plan only half the retainer is in hand at that moment, so the click instead chains the new `automation_TAX_charge_final_retainer` (off-session, saved method, **exactly one call site**, mirroring `automation_TAX_charge_implementation`'s #398 rule), and the revenue share is **deferred** to the `payment_intent.succeeded` branch that confirms that charge — where it fires **once, on the FULL `retainer_amount`**, with `payment_kind='retainer'`. **What holds the payout until then is not the guard you would guess.** The tax revshare sweep's *candidate* precondition is `retainer_receipt_number`, and that is stamped at the **initial** payment — so the sweep sees the plan as a candidate the entire time it waits. The only thing preventing an early payout on half the money is that the legs stay NULL and the sweep is retry-only. That is now written down as gotcha **#441**, because "it hasn't fired yet" is not evidence of a guard.

**The two amend steps.** `automation_TAX_amend_fee` (AUTH, `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS`, deliberately **not** in `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` — re-pricing a signed engagement moves the final retainer, the implementation charge and every revenue-share leg) backs a **"Amend fee"** step at Tax 4, before Client decision 1, and an **"Amend implementation fee"** step at Tax 5b, before the Implementation decision. Both are `program_client_tasks` rows in **both** tax programs (ids 178/179 and 180/181), and the two NAMES are deliberately different — a step row is resolved by name, so one shared name would make the Tax 5 gate pass the moment the Tax 4 step was answered. The handler is server-authoritative: the caller sends only the new total. Guards are ordered by what has already happened — Tax 4 needs the initial retainer settled and Client decision 1 **not yet sent** (that email quotes the amended figures to the client); Tax 5 needs Client decision 2 unrecorded and, on a 3-payment plan, the final retainer settled; money in flight freezes both. Revenue-share legs are re-scaled by `new/old` with the **residual on `vfos_share`** (#252, #394), and deliberately are **not** forced to sum to the new total when they did not already sum to the old one — otherwise an amendment would invent money onto the VFOS leg of a partially-priced plan. Each amendment writes an audit row to the new `client_tax_fee_amendments` table (RLS + deny-all in the same migration), which is audit-only: nothing reads it to make a money decision, so a failed insert is logged and surfaced but never unwinds an amendment that already committed.

**Conversion, and making it reversible.** A Tax 4 amendment to `≤ $30,000` converts a 3-payment plan back to two payments. The design decision that matters: it **nulls `final_retainer_amount` and KEEPS `initial_retainer_amount`**. The kept value is both the record that $15,000 was collected as an initial retainer and the marker that lets a later above-threshold amendment convert *back*. That is why `isThreePaymentPlan` is keyed on **final**, not initial — a predicate keyed on initial is identical on every non-converted row, passes all normal testing, and then silently misclassifies exactly the converted plans (gotcha **#440**). The predicate has three copies — the edge constant and both frontend mirrors — that must move together, the same coupling class as #339.

**Agreements, and the page-number trap that nearly shipped.** `agreement_templates` rows 8 and 20 gained an addendum paragraph, and NEW rows 23 (`Client Paying - 3 Payments`) and 24 (`Member Paying - 3 Payments`) split the retainer line into `[INITIAL_RETAINER]` and `[FINAL_RETAINER]`. Row 23 was verified byte-exact against the user-approved HTML. **The addendum grows the document to four pages**, which moved the signature block from page 3 to page 4 — while `field_map` still said `p:3`. Had the body UPDATE shipped as first drafted, every live BoldSign send off those rows would have placed client and CEO signature fields on blank space, on documents real people sign. The fix landed in the same statement as the body edit, and the coordinates for all four rows were re-sourced by **placing the fields visually in BoldSign template editors and reading them back** through a throwaway `boldsign-template-fields` edge function (v1, deployed today, safe to delete). Gotcha **#439**. Along the way `agreement_templates.boldsign_template_id` — a read-but-unused column for years — became meaningfully stamped for exactly this workflow. Four static review PDFs were re-uploaded to the `tax-agreements` bucket, and the Undecided quote email now attaches the `-3pay` variant above $30,000 with a fallback chain.

**`client_signed_at` stopped being a dead column.** `actions/tax/ceo-countersign.ts` stamps it (the client signature is what triggers that chain) and `actions/tax/stripe-customer.ts` belts it for a BoldSign `Completed` that skipped the intermediate event — both once-only, behind `.is("client_signed_at", null)`, because the amendment paragraphs quote that date back to the client. This **partially unparks #384** without touching `boldsign-webhook`, which is why it needed no approval. `ceo_signed_at` and the whole MAP 1 side stay parked.

**Documents and wording.** The invoice HTML renderer was extracted to `utils/tax-invoice-html.ts` and is now shared by three handlers. A **fresh invoice** is issued when an amendment is not yet reflected on any invoice: at the final retainer when `fee_amended_at_tax4` is set, and at the implementation payment when `fee_amended_at_tax5` is set **or** (`fee_amended_at_tax4` is set and the final-retainer step never issued one). **Declining implementation after a Tax 4 amendment deliberately issues NO corrected invoice** — the amended schedule will never be billed, so invoicing it would document a fiction; the reasoning is commented at the code site rather than left to be rediscovered. Eleven new `email_templates` rows (233–243, all draft-mode; the system-wide `send_mode=true` count is unchanged at eleven) plus four token families: `[RETAINER_LABEL]` on 16 rows makes retainer emails say *"initial retainer"* on a 3-payment plan, `[FINAL_RETAINER]`, `[AMENDMENT_PARAGRAPH]` (substituted **unconditionally on every shape including legacy**, purely to prevent a token leak, and split Tax 4 / Tax 5 so a Tax 4 amendment does not re-announce itself at decision 2), and the still-pending `[LATER_PAYMENTS]` / `[ATTACHED_DOCS]`.

**Two bugs found by building.** A `String.replace` **replacement string** containing a dollar amount has its `$1…` read as a capture reference — it bit the final-retainer sentence, was fixed, and then bit the confirmation email's `[Payment Amount]`. Every money-bearing substitution on this branch now uses a replacer **function**; gotcha **#438**. And the client's green-click write was made **conditional on `post_review_client_decision` still being NULL** with the affected rows counted, because a double-tap or a link-prefetching email client would otherwise draft two confirmations and start two charges.

**Display.** The client Payments tab renders a 3-payment retainer as two grouped rows (*"Retainer payment 1 of 2" / "2 of 2"*) sharing a `subGroup`, drawn as one indented block with a tie bar and tie-broken on payment sequence for the same-day case, with **the revenue-share preview on the Final row** — because that is where the transfers actually fire. The Accounting Tax Planning revenue tab pairs them the same way. The step machine marks both amend steps not-applicable on a legacy plan. The amend dropdown **confirms before committing** and stays editable until the downstream decision is recorded, because the house save-on-select convention would otherwise finalise a price on a stray click (gotcha **#442**).

**What was proven live, and what was not.** A full end-to-end run on test client 62 in sandbox covered **both shapes**: a $20,000 2-payment plan through agreement, signature, card payment and invoice; and a $50,000 3-payment plan through the Undecided quote, the 4-page agreement with visually-placed fields verified on the real render, the $15,000 initial retainer with the correct card fee, a Tax 4 amendment to $40,000 (both reject branches exercised, shares scaled to the cent), the Client decision 1 3-pay email, the green click, the confirmation draft, the $5,000 final retainer, its receipt and fresh amended invoice, the **deferred retainer revshare firing only on settle and on the full $20,000**, a Tax 5 amendment to $45,000, and the $25,000 implementation charge with its receipt and fresh invoice. **That coverage is narrower than it sounds** and the hub's OWED list enumerates fifteen gaps. The load-bearing ones: **neither half is deployed** (v787 and `npm run deploy` are both owed, so every frontend surface here is production-invisible); the **smoke gate's last green run was against the v784 era and is not a gate for v787**; the **2-payment conversion has only ever been PREVIEWED — no amendment has ever been SAVED at ≤ $30,000**, and the reversible re-conversion is code- and parity-checked only; **every member-paying twin** is unexercised; **ACH appears nowhere in the new money paths** (both charges were card-only, so the `processing` branch and both late-bounce branches are untested); the **entire final-retainer failure path** — declined charge, the failed-charge email, both new notification rules and the `/tax-pay` retry branch — has never fired; and **2-payment NEW-PROCESS Client decision 1 was never clicked**, only the 3-pay route.

**Housekeeping found at wrap-up.** Four `supabase/migrations/PENDING_*.sql.txt` files carried `EXECUTION STATE` headers that had gone stale — two claimed work was still pending that the live DB shows was executed (the `[AMENDMENT_PARAGRAPH]` UPDATEs on rows 35/36/138/139 and 32/33/142/143) and one claimed the amend-step task seed had not been run when ids 178–181 are present. All were corrected against a live query rather than against the file. **`PENDING_minor_wording_tokens.sql.txt` (4 rows) genuinely is still pending** and is gated on the v787 deploy: running it first would leak raw `[LATER_PAYMENTS]` / `[ATTACHED_DOCS]` tokens into client drafts.

**Superseded hub values moved here.** Action count **466 → 469**; handler files ~477 → ~480; live `vfo-admin-api` **v781 → v786** (v787 owed); the hub's react deploy-tag line was two releases stale at `live-166-speclic-continuation` and is now `live-168-vfos-residual`; the hub's claim that `boldsign-template-fields` **"is GONE"** is superseded — it was re-deployed at v1 today as a throwaway. `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md`'s per-area snapshot moved Tax 37 → 39 live / 22 → 23 documented and Payment Failure Alerts 17 → 18 live / 16 → 17 documented. Test client 62's fixture description was re-derived: plan 148 and its five progress rows are gone, and the DB side is now genuinely clean (one virgin plan 152, zero progress rows, zero amendment rows) with every remaining leftover outside Postgres.

## 2026-08-24 — Existing specialists move onto a portal-native $99/mo ACH license subscription, charged on a day they pick

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v779 → v780 → v781 (10 files + 1 migration: `actions/specialist-license/continuation-start.ts`, `continuation-load.ts`, `license-payments-load.ts`, `actions/onboarding/license-checkout.ts`, `license-load-payment.ts`, `license-confirmation-email.ts`, `license-invoice-receipt.ts`, `sweep.ts`, `constants/role-gates.ts`, `router/webhooks.ts`; migration `20260824210000_specialist_license_continuation_charge_day.sql`). Frontend: 8 files changed, 3 added, 1 deleted — `npm run deploy` OWED.** Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-dbeb30`, one chat, no handoffs. New flow doc: [flows/specialist-license-continuation.md](flows/specialist-license-continuation.md). Gotchas **#435**, **#436**, **#437**.

**What this is.** VFO Specialists who signed on before the portal existed pay their $99/mo license fee on the legacy system. This moves them onto a portal-native **ACH-only $99/mo Stripe subscription** billed on an admin-chosen day of the month, driven from a **"Setup Monthly License Fees"** button on the Accounting tab. It is not onboarding — these specialists are already live, already in the `experts` directory, and never touch Stages 1–5.

**How it was built.** By re-pointing the **License Fee Continuation** engine — shipped 2026-06-30 and, in the fourteen months since, **never once run** — at the SpecRev recurring ACH setup pattern. The engine's shape survived: continuation work still rides `specialist_onboarding` rows flagged `license_continuation=true` with the `lic_*` columns, and the whole existing licence webhook chain (routed by `lic_stripe_customer_id`) does the money. Its *behaviour* changed substantially.

**The charge day and the two first-charge shapes.** New column `specialist_onboarding.lic_charge_day` (integer **1–15**; onboarding licence rows leave it null and keep charging at checkout time). `continuation-start.ts` now requires `charge_day` and 400s anything outside 1–15; it stamps the day on insert **and** on reuse. `license-checkout.ts` gained a `continuationCheckout()` branch — card is refused with a 400, the amount is a flat 9900 with no gross-up, and the shape is decided at session-creation time:

- **DEFERRED** — this month's charge day is still ≥2h away: one recurring line, `subscription_data[billing_cycle_anchor]` on that date, `proration_behavior=none`. **Nothing is collected at checkout.** This is the SpecRev-proven construct.
- **CATCH-UP** — the charge day has gone by: the recurring line **plus a one-time $99** "First month license fee (charged today)", with `subscription_data[trial_end]` set to *next* month's occurrence. Catch-up exists because of an explicit user requirement — **the month of setup always gets charged, so a missed charge day never silently skips a month.**

`trial_end` rather than a second anchor is the load-bearing decision. A one-time line item under a future `billing_cycle_anchor` is held and invoiced **at the anchor** — the money the admin thinks was collected today would arrive a month later on a $198 invoice, with nothing erroring. Under a trial, Checkout invoices one-time items immediately at completion. The price is that Stripe's hosted page then shows its own trial/free wording, which cannot be removed; that was raised and **accepted** by the user, mitigated with `custom_text[submit][message]`. Written up as **#435**. Date bounding (17:00 UTC preferred, stepping down to 04:05 then 00:05 then a hard clamp, with a 1h `expires_at` on the session) is copied from the SpecRev setup, as is the deliberate **absence** of a `verification_method=instant` pin (#298).

**A new status, `scheduled`.** A deferred setup completes Checkout with a subscription and **zero money moved**. Recording that as `processing` would claim a payment that does not exist, so `checkout.session.completed` writes `lic_payment_status='scheduled'` with progress `task_key='payment_setup'`. Classification reads `metadata.first_charge` first; Stripe's `payment_status='no_payment_required'` is only a fallback for a session minted before that stamp. The knock-on is the point of **#437**: "set up" and "paid" became different questions on the same row, so the sweep's completion test is `lic_subscription_id IS NOT NULL` rather than a payment test, and the double-enroll guard could not key on payment status either — with the sharp edge that PostgREST's `.neq("lic_payment_status","canceled")` **drops NULL rows**, i.e. exactly the deferred subscription it needs to catch. That test is now done in JS over a subscription-id filter, scanning **every** row for the expert rather than the latest, and row reuse is restricted to `license_continuation=true` rows so a real onboarding row is never borrowed.

**A guard that the docs claimed and the code never had.** While adding the $0-invoice skip to `processSpecialistLicenseInvoicePaid`, `07-server-chains.md` turned out to have asserted for two months that the processor already skipped the $0 `subscription_create` stub (**#198**) — **it did not**. This was a live pre-existing bug on the **onboarding** path, not just the new one: a $0 stub would have claimed `lic_last_invoice_id`, minted a bogus $99 invoice + receipt to Drive, drafted the email and written a $99 ledger row for money nobody paid, after which the real first invoice would have been skipped as already-processed. It survived only because live onboarding subscriptions billed immediately and never emitted the stub; the deferred branch is the first shape that does. Now fixed for both paths, and written up as **#436** — a doc asserting a code guard is a claim about code, and the handler is the authority.

**Everything else on the backend.** Both continuation actions moved out of `SUPERADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS` into `TAB_ACTIONS.accounting` with their in-handler superadmin checks removed — full parity with `specialist_revenue_recurring_create` (the 2026-08-07 / #338 decision). Stage 4→5 advance and `license-invoice-receipt.ts`'s two Tracy go-live bells (Skool invite / Create specialist) are gated `!license_continuation`, since the specialist is already live. `license-load-payment.ts` adds `continuation`/`ach_only`/`charge_day`/`charge_day_ordinal`/`first_charge_note` plus a subscription-already-set guard on the public link, with the **onboarding response byte-identical**; its header comment, which claimed superadmin-only, was corrected to accounting-gated. `license-confirmation-email.ts` drafts from the new template with a dynamic `[FIRST_PAYMENT_SENTENCE]` covering both shapes, and tolerates a missing template without stamping. `sweep.ts` gained **tier 7b** — the same 2-business-day reminder / 4-business-day Tracy bell ladder on the rows tier 7 excludes, reusing tier 7's rule keys (`SPECIALIST_stall_licpayment_email`/`_bell`, so **no new `notification_rules`**) and its guard columns; `sendReminder()` took an optional pipeline argument for it and tier 7 is untouched. `license-payments-load.ts` gained a `pending[]` array (`setup_pending`/`scheduled`/`processing`/`failed`, unknown values like `past_due` passed through raw) — the isolated, read-only change that was the whole of v781.

**Templates** (live DB, all `send_mode=false` draft-only, recipients `to` SPECIALIST / `cc` Tracy / `bcc` Anton + Paul): row **171** `SPECIALIST_lic_continuation_request` rewritten with user-approved copy; NEW rows **231** `_confirmation` and **232** `_reminder`. All three carry the new pipeline label `SPECIALIST_LICENSE_CONTINUATION` — templates only; Stripe metadata, bells and the sandbox toggle stay `SPECIALIST_ONBOARDING`.

**Frontend (NOT deployed).** `SpecialistLicensePanel.jsx` got the gradient toggle button + inline `LicenseSetupForm` (expert picker via a new `allExperts` prop, 1st–15th ordinal select, fixed *$99.00 · ACH*), and its monthly table was rebuilt as SPECIALIST · DATE · AMOUNT · STATUS with one money column and a "Payment received" chip only. The amber already-enrolled note keys on the loader's `already_active`, with an `/already/i` message match as fallback because `callApi` discards the HTTP status. The whole License area now renders through the **same `AccountingCombinedPanel` wrapper SpecRev uses**, three pills: License Fees | **License Reconciliation** (NEW `SpecialistLicenseReconciliationPanel.jsx` — all-time per-specialist aggregate, deliberately no year filter and no member-# column since `expert_id` is a raw DB id) | **Outstanding Payment Links** (NEW `SpecialistLicenseOutstandingPanel.jsx`, reusing `OutstandingLinksPanel`'s now-exported internals; read-only, no resend). `SpecialistPayPage.jsx` renders continuation links ACH-only with charge-day copy and a security note reworded to stop claiming "nothing is charged", since catch-up collects at setup. **The License Fee Continuation profile subtab was removed entirely** and `SpecialistLicenseContinuationTab.jsx` deleted — a user decision: the Accounting button replaces it. NEW shared `src/lib/ordinal.js` (three pre-existing private copies deliberately left alone).

**Unrelated restyle done in the same pass, at user request:** `SpecialistRevenuePanel.jsx` moved to the Holistic totals-above-table format — an uppercase header row and a TOTALS row (member/VFOS/gross, sub-labelled *"&lt;period&gt; · received"* because the totals sum received only) above the rows in **both** By-specialist and By-member views, with the old top-right totals strip removed and the By-member totals row gaining a held sub-note. `specialistRevenueShared.jsx`'s `RequestRow` took an optional `grid` prop (card layout unchanged when absent, so `SpecialistRevenueAutomationPanel` is untouched) and its expanded detail was extracted verbatim to `RequestDetail`; the table chrome consts are now exported for reuse.

**Live-tested this session** (sandbox flipped ON then back OFF, all fixtures cleaned, posture re-verified all 8 pipelines false): the **catch-up branch end-to-end** on a test expert — draft email, ACH-only page, two-line Stripe session, payment settled, status `succeeded`, invoice + receipt drafted, exactly 1 ledger row, **zero Tracy bells (DB-verified)**, stage stayed 4, and the amber already-active refusal on a re-send; and the **deferred branch end-to-end** on a second test expert (charge day hand-set to 28 by SQL to reach the branch in late August) — one-line session, no charge, status `scheduled`, 0 ledger rows, the deferred confirmation sentence. The pending band and Outstanding tab were checked rendering at each stage. Verification: `deno check` 0, action count 466 (unchanged), `npm run build` exit 0 / 33 route pages, security advisor at the exact green baseline after the migration, **smoke 5/5 against the shipping v781**.

**Decisions to record.** Accounting-tab gate parity, not superadmin, for the two continuation actions. The profile subtab is REPLACED, not kept alongside. Charge days restricted to 1–15. Amount locked at $99. Stripe's hosted-page trial/free wording on the catch-up branch is accepted. Catch-up always charges the month of setup. **Rollout coordination is out of code scope: Tracy must cancel each specialist's legacy license billing from their first portal month, or they pay twice (the #361 exposure) — nothing checks this automatically.**

**Not exercised — carried to the hub's OWED list**, including that no real specialist has been sent anything and none can be until the frontend deploys.

## 2026-08-24 — A suspended or paused member's revenue share is HELD instead of paid, and releases itself the moment they are reinstated

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v777 → v778 (10 files: NEW `utils/member-payout-hold.ts` + `utils/member-payout-release.ts`, plus `actions/members/profile-save.ts`, `actions/membership/sweep.ts`, `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts`, `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts`, `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare-sweep.ts`, `actions/specialist-revenue/payout-sweep.ts`, `actions/tax/revshare.ts`, `actions/tax/revshare-sweep.ts`, `utils/specialist-revenue-payout.ts`). Migration `20260824120000_member_revshare_hold_seeds.sql` APPLIED (one `email_templates` row + one `notification_rules` row; no DDL, no new table or column). Frontend: 19 files, **NOT deployed at the time of writing**. `deno check` 0, action count **466 unchanged** (no new dispatched action — the release is a util, deliberately), `npm run build` exit 0 / 33 route pages, crons **15 unchanged**, security advisor re-confirmed at the exact GREEN baseline (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN) after the seed migration.**

**The gap, and the money that already moved through it.** `members.suspended`, `members.paused` and `members.membership_suspended` were **display-only**. Every surface ORed them into a "Suspended" pill (#240) and nothing else read them — no payout engine, no sweep, no webhook branch. On **2026-08-21**, Sandra Jones' MAP 1 catch-up ran and paid **Timothy Mustapha (member 59448), who is `suspended=true`, two $675 member revenue-share transfers**. Nobody stopped it because nothing was looking. **Those two payments were deliberately NOT clawed back** — the money reached the right person for the right work; the decision was to stop the next one, not unwind the last one. Timothy is still `suspended=true`, so the next real payment on one of his clients is production's first hold.

**The model: a fourth non-terminal leg state, not a new pipeline.** A held leg is exactly the shape of the two that already exist — `AWAITING_CONNECT` (`utils/member-share-held.ts`) and `PLANNER_SHARE_WITHHELD` (`utils/tax-planner-payout.ts`): **no transfer, no member confirmation email, no completion stamp, no `transfer_id`**, and the leg parks in a status the nightly sweeps already re-attempt. That is the whole safety argument — reinstating a member pays them **without anyone having to remember**, because the retry machinery is pre-existing (#303: a non-terminal status is safe only if every retry path accepts it). `memberHoldReason()` reads the three booleans with **suspension outranking a pause** (`suspended || membership_suspended → "suspended"`, `paused → "paused"`), so a member who is both reads as suspended.

**Four engines, two status vocabularies.** `pipeline/contract-revshare.ts` (`rec{N}_rev_paid`), `tax/revshare.ts` (`{kind}_rev_paid`) and `msm/pip-revshare.ts` (`pip_rev_share_status`) are Title-Case TEXT columns and take **`"Held - Member Suspended"` / `"Held - Member Paused"`**. `utils/specialist-revenue-payout.ts` writes `specialist_revenue_lines.payout_status`, whose family is snake_case, so it carries its **own two literals** — `held_member_suspended` / `held_member_paused` — and the header says so, because the one thing that must never happen is a Title-Case status leaking into that column. **Only the MEMBER leg is ever held**: strategic-partner, tax-planner and specialist/expert legs pay normally beside a held member leg, which is the point — the client's other partners did nothing wrong.

**Where the branch sits in each chain is load-bearing.** It goes **above** Connect resolution, account creation, the setup email and the transfer (a suspended member must be sent *nothing at all* and must not have a Stripe account minted for them), and **below** Money Mapping and the `$0` close. Money Mapping moves no cash, so there is nothing to hold; a zero share has no payout to withhold, so it closes normally and raises no notice. PIP's branch chain was **reordered to be exhaustive** while this landed (#303), and its held leg writes no `completed_at` and no `transfer_id` — but the **child-meeting unlock still runs on a held leg**, deliberately: the client's next meeting must not be gated on the member's standing.

**The notice email is a DRAFT, and that was a decision.** `draftMemberHeldNotice` drafts to Paul (cc Anton / Tracy V / Tracy M) through `email_templates` **`MEMBERS` / `MEMBER_revshare_held` (id 230, `send_mode=false`)**, deduped **once per hold episode** by testing the leg's status from *before* this run's write — so a nightly sweep tick or a retry click does not re-draft. It carries a hardcoded fallback body so a missing template row can never block the hold itself. **Auto-send was considered and rejected**: eleven rows system-wide auto-send (#325) and this one names a member's financial standing to four people — a human reads it before it goes. The consequence is explicit: **the first production hold puts a draft in Gmail that somebody has to actually send.**

**Release is instant, and it fires from two places.** `releaseHeldMemberPayouts(memberNumber)` re-fires every held leg by HTTP chain into `vfo-admin-api` with the service-role key — the same shape the sweeps use — keyed `automation_CONTRACT_revshare {client_id, payment_number}`, `automation_TAX_revshare {tax_plan_id, payment_kind}`, `automation_PIP_revshare {priority_track_id}`, `specialist_revenue_payout {request_id}`. It is a **util, not a dispatched action**, because both callers already hold service-role context and there is no third-party trigger. **Both member→client linkages are collected**, and that is not belt-and-braces: Tax and PIP read the owner off `clients.member_number`, **MAP 1 keys on the `client_ref` prefix only**, so querying one column would silently miss a whole pipeline. Trigger 1 is the members **profile save**, which reads the row before the upsert and **RE-READS it after** to detect the transition. Trigger 2 is the **membership sweep's pass 4**, which fires the release only when *no* hold reason remains — the auto-unsuspend clears `membership_suspended`, but a manual `suspended` or `paused` must still hold. Every re-fire is idempotent: the engines re-check standing on entry and re-hold, so firing a still-flagged member is a no-op.

**Rejected alternative: sweep-only release.** The nightly sweeps already retry held legs, so doing nothing at all would have worked — with up to a 24-hour gap between an admin reinstating a member and that member being paid. The instant release removes the wait and adds no new capability; **the sweeps remain the backstop and were proven to be one live** (below), which is why the release path failing is not a money bug.

**Sweep pickup was widened in four places, because a non-terminal status is invisible to a predicate that does not name it.** MAP 1 (02:00) retries held legs naturally through its existing unresolved test; **tax (02:30) needed `MEMBER_HELD_STATUSES` added to `isRetry`**; **SpecRev (11:00) pass 1 now queries the exported `PAYABLE_STATUSES`** rather than an inline list, so the sweep's candidate set is the engine's by construction and cannot drift; and PIP gained a **NEW final held-only pass** — deliberately held-only, because PIP `"Pending"` failures stay manual and folding them in would have changed unrelated behaviour.

**SpecRev stopped minting Stripe accounts for members, and the investigation behind that is worth keeping.** A member line with no Connect account used to create an Express account, mint an onboarding link and draft `SPECREV_connect_setup`. It now mints nothing and emails nothing: the line parks `awaiting_connect` (with **no `email_drafted_at` — nothing was drafted**) and raises an action-required bell **`SPECREV_member_share_held`**, titled through `memberShareHeldTitle("Specialist Revenue", name, member#)` so it reconstructs byte-identically at payout time and self-clears (#122) — on the transfer **and** on the `$0` close, which is that path's only chance to clear. **Why not just email the durable link?** Because `actions/payouts/connect-setup-link.ts` **404s on a member with no `stripe_account_id`** — the durable `/payout-setup?token=` page (#268) resumes an account, it does not create one. Minting belongs to the admin's **"Set Up Payment Details"** button in `MembersPanel.jsx`, which is also the only flow that issues that token. A member who *has* a half-built account still gets the fresh-link email, because that link works. **Experts are completely unchanged.** The member `select` in both the SpecRev engine and the PIP engine was extended to carry `member_number` + the three standing columns — a hold that cannot see the flags is not a hold (#240's "a new consumer needs it in its select", now with money behind it).

**Frontend — 19 files, and one of them is a judgement call, not a rendering fix.** `shareLegState.jsx` gains the two held states (notes read **"Held - Suspended"** / **"Held - Paused"**, Title-Case kept deliberately to match the stored value an admin may see in SQL) plus `HeldNote`/`heldReason`. Alongside them is a **new exported `isMoneyMappingLeg(state, decision)`**, which changes how *settled* legs are bucketed between the **Revenue Share** and **Money Mapping** columns across all six Holistic / Tax / PIP revenue + reconciliation panels: **a settled leg is bucketed by what actually happened to it** (its own note — `'paid'` vs `'money mapping'`), and only an **unsettled** leg falls back to the member's *current* `revenue_decision`. **The owner's decision:** Flood and Cito legs that were paid as cash must keep showing under Revenue Share even though Cito's member record says Money Mapping today — the columns are history, not a live restatement of a member's current preference. Held and pending notes **partition** the owed money rather than adding to it, so nothing double-counts.

`specialistRevenueShared.jsx` gains held pills, a **"By member"** view, and `memberShareNote` annotations — worth naming because the SpecRev member-dollar cells previously carried **no paid note at all**; the recurring pill also renames `"Completed"` → `"Payment received"`. `SpecialistRevenueAutomationPanel`'s `OPEN_PAYOUT` and `SpecialistReconciliationPanel`'s `PENDING_PAYOUT` sets both admit the held statuses, and both `PricingSplitCards` carry explicit held cases. `AutomationPanel`'s `revDecision` reads **"Share held — member suspended/paused"** (its own em-dash idiom kept, deliberately diverging from the leg notes' hyphen). `MembersPanel`'s suspend/pause toggle descriptions now **state the payout consequence** — the toggles finally do something, so they had to say so. `taxShared.jsx`'s retainer strategic leg gained a `'tax_retainer'` context ("awaiting client decision"). And `EmailTemplatesPanel.jsx` + `templateMeta.js` gained the `MEMBERS` / `MEMBER_revshare_held` row under **Miscellaneous**, so the notice is editable in the tab like every other template.

**Live verification — all four pipelines held AND released, on test member 59524 / client 62.** Tax: held on all three flags (`suspended`, `paused`, `membership_suspended`); the **dedupe proved by log** (a second fire drafted no second notice); **instant release twice, ~1s, real transfer `tr_1U805z…`**. MAP 1: held on `paused`, instant release **$400**. PIP: held, instant release `tr_1U80Gl…` **$150**. SpecRev: held, then the release chain re-fired to `awaiting_connect` + the bell, with **`stripe_account_id` confirmed still NULL and no email sent** — the no-mint decision verified at the row level. **The sweep backstop was proven live**, not reasoned about: the `tax-revshare-sweep-daily` cron command was executed by hand at 16:49Z and paid the held leg + drafted the member's confirmation. Every fixture was cleaned afterwards (plan 152 back to all-NULL including `retainer_status`/`retainer_date`, the MAP 1 row / PIP track / SpecRev request + line deleted, Tracy bells 1410/1411 and specrev bell 1412 deleted, the member's flags restored).

**Note on the sandbox that is worth reading before the next SpecRev test:** SpecRev is **not** per-client sandboxed. It reads the **global `"MAP 1"` `pipeline_sandbox_config` row**, so `constants/test-sandbox.ts`'s force-sandbox for test member 59524 (#251) does **not** cover it — see gotcha #432.

**What was NOT exercised, carried to the hub as OWED.** (1) The SpecRev member-line **actual transfer branch** never live-fired — global-live-mode versus a sandbox destination account made it unreachable in the test window; the transfer block itself is unchanged code. (2) The **membership sweep pass-4 release trigger** never live-fired — it needs a real dues catch-up, and the tax-sweep backstop covers the money in the meantime. (3) Three FE renders were never seen: the **two-note render** (a member with both a suspended and a paused leg in one period), the **PIP held case**, and the **SpecRev "By member" held header total**. (4) The **first production hold's notice draft** sits in Gmail until a human sends it. (5) A **post-v778 code edit** dropped the sentence *"No money was transferred and the member was not notified."* from `DEFAULT_BODY`, the migration and the DB row, so the **deployed fallback diverges by one sentence until the next backend deploy** — live behaviour is correct because the DB row governs and only the fallback is stale. (6) The **smoke gate against the final shipping backend version is owed** — the v778 run was performed but its result was not recorded, and the queued redeploy makes that run moot anyway.

**Discharges:** nothing from a prior session was settled by this branch. Superseded hub value retired here: live `vfo-admin-api` **v777** (now v778).

**Gotchas #432 / #433 / #434** came out of the build (the global SpecRev sandbox + its email-safety trap; the "teach every enumerating predicate" cost of a non-terminal status; and blind-spread partial profile upserts forcing a post-write re-read). **#240 was amended in place** — the three standing flags are no longer display-only.

## 2026-08-21 — A VFO Specialist Revenue request that was sent and never acted on can now be deleted

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v776 -> v777 (3 files: NEW `actions/specialist-revenue/delete-request.ts`, plus `router/dispatch.ts` and `constants/role-gates.ts`). Frontend deployed to `gh-pages` (2 files: `src/components/admin/specialistRevenueShared.jsx`, `src/components/admin/SpecialistRevenuePanel.jsx`). No migration, no DDL, no new table/column/template/bell, and no Stripe call anywhere in the change. `deno check` 0, action count **465 -> 466** (6 + 460), `npm run build` exit 0 / 33 route pages, security advisor at the exact GREEN baseline (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN, unchanged because nothing touched the DB schema), pipeline smoke gate **5/5 PASS against v777**.**

**The gap.** `specialist_revenue_send_request` persists a request plus its recipient lines, mints a Stripe customer, and drafts the payment-request email with a `/specialist-revenue-pay?token=` link. Until now there was no way back. A request built against the wrong specialist, with the wrong deal list, or simply superseded, sat on the Accounting card forever in `payment_status='requested'`, its emailed link still live and still payable. The only controls on that card were "Mark payment received" (house-account rows only) and, in the Automation tab, "Retry payout". Deleting one meant hand SQL.

**What shipped.** A new AUTH action `specialist_revenue_delete_request` that hard-deletes one genuinely pre-payment one-off request and its `specialist_revenue_lines`. The line delete is explicit even though `specialist_revenue_lines.request_id` is FK `ON DELETE CASCADE` — belt-and-braces, and it produces a precise error if the FK is ever changed. The FE half is `canDeleteSpecrevRequest()` (a mirror of the backend guard) plus a red `DeleteRequestButton` with a `window.confirm`, both in `specialistRevenueShared.jsx`, built on the existing `MarkReceivedButton` idiom.

**The gate is `TAB_ACTIONS.accounting` and nothing else, deliberately.** That is the one list `specialist_revenue_send_request` sits in, and there is no in-handler check — the #338 full-parity decision, which took the in-handler `auth.isSuperadmin` off every Accounting-tab control in 2026-08-07/v707, applies unchanged: the accounting grant is the whole boundary, money included. An admin who can send a request can withdraw one that was never acted on. Adding a second gate here would have re-introduced exactly the split #338 removed.

**Three guards, all of them evaluated before any row is touched.** `recurring_plan_id` non-null returns 400 (a recurring month belongs to a plan and `specialist_revenue_recurring_cancel` owns it). `payment_status !== 'requested'` returns 400 quoting the offending status. `stripe_payment_intent_id || payment_method_type` non-null returns 400 — the belt-and-braces column test, true of "money was entered" regardless of what the status string says. An unknown id returns 404 rather than a silent success.

**Two states are deliberately NOT deletable, and both look deletable at a glance.** `pending` is the 2026-07-07 house-account model: the specialist was handed the shared VFO ACH details and the admin is waiting on a wire. Those rows carry `payment_method_type='bank_transfer'` **from creation**, so they fail the third guard as well as the first, and "Mark payment received" is the control that owns them. `failed` is terminal and kept **as the record of a dead payment** — deleting it would erase the only evidence a payment was ever attempted. Neither is an oversight.

**Nothing is asked of Stripe, on purpose.** Pre-payment there is no PaymentIntent and no checkout session to cancel. The customer minted by `send_request` is left dangling: it holds no payment method, no balance and no subscription, it costs nothing, and every webhook block that resolves by `stripe_customer_id` is a null-tolerant `maybeSingle()` that now simply finds no row and falls through. The one visible consequence is documented in [integrations/stripe.md](integrations/stripe.md): a `checkout.session.expired` arriving for a since-deleted request raises no abandonment bell, which is correct and must not be "fixed". The emailed link dies naturally — `specialist_revenue_pay_load` looks the token up and 404s *"Invalid or expired payment link"*.

**Delete safety was proved reader-by-reader before the handler was written**, not after: the payout sweep's four passes, every webhook block that touches SPECREV, `resolve-stripe-failure`, the invoice/receipt engine, both load surfaces, the Outstanding Payment Links panel and the public token pages were each checked for a hard join or a count that a vanished row would corrupt. All are `maybeSingle()`/null-tolerant, and a `requested` row has by definition contributed nothing downstream — no invoice or receipt number allocated, no payout line moved.

**Live verification.** Smoke gate 5/5 by Jake against v777, then a real click-through: request **29** (Deborah Snyder, $4,180, 16 deals, 13 lines) was deleted from the Accounting card; SQL confirmed the request row and all 13 `specialist_revenue_lines` at **0**, and the emailed payment link was confirmed dead in a browser.

**What that click-through does NOT cover — carried to the hub as OWED.** The three refusal branches (a paid or processing row, a recurring child, an already-deleted id) were desk-checked only; no live 400 has ever been provoked, and none is reachable by clicking, because `canDeleteSpecrevRequest()` hides the button on exactly those rows. A live refusal needs a hand-crafted call. Separately, **`SpecialistRevenueAutomationPanel.jsx` was deliberately not wired**: it renders the same `RequestRow`, the change is two lines, and it was scoped out — so the Automation tab shows no Delete button on a row the Accounting tab would let you delete.

**Gotcha #431** came out of the build. `specialist_revenue_requests.payment_status` is a bare `text` column with **zero CHECK constraints**, and its migration comment lists four values; the live vocabulary is six. Building the guard from that comment would have quietly admitted `awaiting_verification` — a row with a live PaymentIntent open on it — into the deletable set. The full six-value vocabulary now lives in the handler header, where the next reader of this code will actually be standing.

**Doc counts moved with it:** 465 -> 466 actions and ~476 -> ~477 handler files in `README.md`, `architecture/01-system-map.md`, `architecture/03-edge-functions.md`, `architecture/05-api-action-catalog.md` and the hub's SYSTEM MAP; the AUTH half of the dispatch split is now 132 PUBLIC + 328 AUTH. Superseded hub values retired here: live `vfo-admin-api` **v776** (now v777) and the action-count derive expectation **6 + 459 = 465** (now 6 + 460 = 466).

## 2026-08-21 — Monthly transfer memberships keep the charge day they already pay on; their setup link stops collecting money

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v775 → v776 (6 files, all under `actions/membership/`). Frontend deployed to `gh-pages` (2 files). No migration, no DDL — `charge_day` already existed. `deno check` 0, action count **465** (unchanged, no new actions), `npm run build` exit 0 / 33 route pages, security advisor at the exact GREEN baseline (5 deny-all INFO + the `pg_net` WARN), pipeline smoke gate **5/5 PASS run by Jake against v776**.**

**The complaint that started it.** Manos Cito (member 58114, plan 49) has paid his membership on the **10th** for as long as he has been a member. He was transferred onto portal billing, paid his setup link on **August 21**, and the system did what it had always done for transfers: it derived his charge day from *the day he happened to click the link*. That produced three wrong things at once — he was **charged at the link** for a month he had already paid on the old platform, his day was re-anchored (a day-21 payer becomes a **1st** payer under the after-the-15th rule), and **September was skipped** entirely because the first derived slot was October 1. Every one of the fifteen transferring members has a fixed day they have always paid on; Tray holds the list. Deriving that day from a click was the bug.

**The model, and the one line that carries it.** A monthly transfer may now carry an admin-entered **`charge_day` (1–15)**. When it does, three things follow: **the setup link charges nothing** (mode=setup, save-the-method only), **the whole year-1 ledger is scheduled on that day**, and **the catch-up folds into the FIRST scheduled charge** instead of into a payment at the link. `transferDaySchedule(plan, basisDate)` in `actions/membership/shared.ts` returns **null** for anything that is not a monthly transfer with a valid 1–15 day, and **that null is the entire legacy switch** — a transfer with no day keeps `transferLinkPulls` and the pay-at-the-link behaviour byte for byte. `transferLinkPulls` and `buildActivatedSchedule` were not touched; the legacy path is unchanged by construction, which is what made it safe to ship against 12 pending plans in one afternoon. Days are capped at 15 so a month never clamps, and the helper stays a function of its **basis date** like its older sibling (#349): the page and checkout pass today, `activate` passes the save date, `send-setup-link` passes the draft date.

**The maths, in `shared.ts`.** New `dayOccurrencesAfter(basis, day, {count, untilExclusive})` — every day-D occurrence **strictly after** the basis (so saving *on* day D bills from the next one), same 24-iteration cap as `subsequentChargeDates`, stopping **before** `renewal_date` because a row landing on the renewal 15th reads as a generated year 2 and blocks renewal forever (**#235/#350**). Module-private `placeMonths()` lays the owed months onto those slots and is the only place the three cases live: **AHEAD** stops early; **BEHIND** (more months owed than slots left) folds the shortfall into the **first** row as **ONE combined row** — never several rows on one date (**#315**) — carrying `perPull × k` and `creditPer × k` so `monthsCoveredByRow` reads it back as *k months* rather than one payment (**#316**); and the **zero-slot** edge (a day-15 member whose renewal is the next 15th) collapses the year onto the save date itself, which the next nightly sweep collects. `buildTransferDayRows(sched, basis, perPull, grossPer, linkPulls)` is one builder for both completions the link can produce: `linkPulls = 0` is the normal save-only case (every row `scheduled`); `linkPulls >= 1` is the **stale-link race** — a Checkout session minted *before* the plan had a charge day, completing as `mode=payment` *after* it gained one — where the money still has to be recorded, so row 1 is the paid link row at the basis date and the rest land on day-D slots after it, with no fallback row allowed to collide with it.

**The other five backend files are small and each closes one hole.** `plan-save.ts` accepts an optional `charge_day` (400 *"Charge day must be a whole number between 1 and 15"* when present and invalid), writes it **only** for monthly transfers and **unconditionally** — so editing a plan to annual, or away from transfer, clears it rather than stranding a stale day (the same discipline `remaining_payments` already uses). `activate.ts` gains `chargeDayOut`: annual → 15, day-carrying → **the admin's day**, else the legacy `chargeDayFor(basisDate)` — so a day plan is never re-anchored to whenever the member got round to saving; the save-only branch builds an all-`scheduled` day-D ledger and the legacy path is byte-identical. `setup-checkout.ts` and `setup-load.ts` extend their `saveOnly` predicate; `setup-load` returns eight **additive** fields (`charge_day`, `charge_day_ordinal`, `per_pull_amount`, `payments_remaining`, `first_charge_date`, `last_charge_date`, `first_charge_amount`, `first_charge_months`) so the page never re-derives the schedule. `send-setup-link.ts` selects a new template for day plans and adds four tokens — `[Charge Day]` `[Last Charge Date]` `[First Charge Amount]` `[Catch Up Note]`; a **missing template degrades gracefully** (200 + `email_skipped`, the link still works).

**Two files were deliberately NOT touched, and both were verified rather than assumed.** `router/webhooks.ts`: the `mode=setup` path already passes `payDateIso` null, and the first-signup confirmation email is gated on the `membership_first_payment` kind, so a save-only completion **cannot** fire it. `sweep.ts`: the renewal pass already reads `plan.charge_day`, so **year 2 lands on the chosen day automatically** with no change at all.

**Frontend.** `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx` gains a **required** ordinal select — *"Day of the month they currently pay on (1–15)"* — on monthly transfers, blocking save with *"Pick the day of the month they currently pay on (1–15) — the whole remaining year is charged on that day."* `dayOccurrencesAfter` and `transferDaySchedule` are **mirrored beside the existing `transferSlots`/`catchUpCliff` mirrors** (the established pattern in this panel; they must move together with the backend). The transfer preview is rewritten for day plans — a save-only quote, an **amber Behind line** naming the combined first charge, and a zero-slot line — while a **legacy `editPlan` without a day** still renders the old pay-at-link copy plus an amber *"Pick the day … it is now required to save"* prompt. The `saveOnly` predicate was extended at **both** sites (the `emailCtx` builder ~line 444 and `OutstandingLinkRow` ~line 1242 — missing either would have made the panel and the email disagree), a **"Charge day"** `LinkDetail` row was added, the new template joined the `StepEmailsChip` list, and the transfer hint text is now frequency-aware. `MembershipPayPage.jsx` renders day plans **completely number-free**.

**DECISIONS made by the owner this session, each of which could reasonably have gone the other way:**

1. **The link is save-only, not pay-at-link.** Collecting "this month" at the link is exactly what produced the Cito complaint; a transferring member has already paid the old platform for the current month.
2. **Backfill all fifteen, not just the complainant.** Every pending transfer plan was carrying the same latent bug.
3. **Do NOT resend the twelve stale setup emails.** Their text promises a payment at setup that will no longer happen — but **the links themselves render correctly live** (they are recomputed server-side on every load), so the wrong copy is a one-time cosmetic mismatch and a resend would confuse fifteen people to fix it. Deliberate.
4. **The member's pay page carries NO numbers.** After the page was first built *with* a schedule box and a catch-up note, both were **removed**: any figure on a page the member reaches by clicking "set up payment" reads as a charge happening today, which is the exact misconception this feature exists to prevent. Precedent: the existing update-method page. The card fee-rate **badge** was deliberately kept (it describes the rail, not a charge).
5. **The EMAIL keeps its numbers**, and the template is **Draft mode**. Its two siblings (191, 215) are send-mode; 229 was seeded `send_mode=false` on purpose, because for a **behind** member the human review of that draft is their only advance warning that the first charge will be larger than a normal month.
6. **Todd Villarrubia's plan 51 is not to be recreated.**

**Data, all via MCP SQL — no DDL, no migration.** `email_templates` id **229** seeded: `MEMBERSHIP_transfer_setup_link|monthly-saveonly`, pipeline `MEMBER_MEMBERSHIP_FEES`, **Draft**, subject later trimmed to *"We're moving your ERT Membership billing over"* (the siblings keep their longer dashed subjects: 191 *"… — one quick step"*, 215 *"… — nothing to pay today"*). **`send_mode=true` remains at exactly ELEVEN rows** — 229 does not join them (#325 unchanged). Charge days backfilled from Tray's list onto all fifteen transfer plans: **15th** → 36, 37; **10th** → 38, 43, 44, 46, 48; **1st** → 39, 45, 47, 35 (Simms), 41 (Charpenter); plan 40 (Coffman) was already correct on the 1st. Two ACTIVE plans also had their existing ledgers re-dated under the rule **"keep each row's month, fix the day"** — never shifting a row into a different month, so **September is never double-charged** (the link payment already covered it): plan **42** (Ladas) `charge_day=12` with 3 scheduled rows moved +11 days to Oct/Nov/Dec 12, and plan **49** (Cito) `charge_day=10` with 10 scheduled rows moved +9 days to Oct 10 2026 – Jul 10 2027. **Deleted:** test plan **50** (member 59524, the full sandbox e2e) and **Todd Villarrubia's plan 51**, which had been created on the LIVE portal through the old form during the sandbox window and so was sandbox-stamped with a null charge day.

**What was actually exercised live.** A full sandbox click-through on test plan 50: the form (both the normal and the **behind** preview variants), the Gmail draft render, the save-only page in **both** its with-numbers and final no-numbers versions, the card save, and activation → **11 all-`scheduled` rows, Sep 10 – Jul 10, charge day 10, no paid row**. After the deploy, Gary Watts' **real** live link was eyeballed: save-only page, *"1st of each month"*, no figures.

**The live incident this caused, and gotcha #430.** While the `MEMBER_MEMBERSHIP` sandbox toggle was ON for that e2e, the v619 mode guards **inverted for every real plan at once** — all live plans are `sandbox=false`, so every outstanding setup link started returning *"link is out of date"*. Gary Watts hit his during that window. Nothing was broken and nothing needed re-issuing; the toggle was flipped back and the link worked. **The blast radius of a sandbox toggle is every outstanding token link in the pipeline**, and membership has no per-record alternative because the test-member 59524 force-sandbox override is client-keyed and does not cover this member-keyed pipeline (#251).

**A consequence for the PREVIOUS session's open item, worth stating plainly.** The 2026-08-21 v775 entry recorded that *"the 13 queued transfer plans (ids 35–48) are its live verification"* for the `Payment 2 of 1` confirmation-email fix (#427). **That route is now gone**: all thirteen carry a charge day, so their links are save-only, and the confirmation email is gated on the `membership_first_payment` kind — a save-only completion cannot fire it. Plan 49 (Cito) already drafted its confirmation pre-fix. **v775's fix therefore has no queued live verification left** among transfers; only a NEW transfer plan deliberately saved *without* a charge day, or a fresh non-transfer sign-up (which always read `1 of 12` and never hit the miscount), would exercise it. The hub's OWED entry was corrected accordingly rather than left to look satisfied.

**New gotchas: #429** (a NULL that *is* the legacy money switch, plus `charge_day`'s new second writer) and **#430** (a sandbox toggle breaks every live link in its pipeline).

## 2026-08-21 — Admin Strategic Member profiles gain the CIQ feature tab (parity with advisors and accountants)

**Frontend-only, two lines in one file (`src/components/admin/MembersPanel.jsx`). No backend change, no migration, no deploy of `vfo-admin-api` (still v775) or `boldsign-webhook` (still v40). `npm run build` exit 0, 33 route pages.**

**The ask:** an admin viewing a **Strategic Member's** profile could not reach that member's CIQs, while the same admin viewing an advisor or accountant could. The fix gives Strategic the same feature tab.

**What was verified before changing anything** — the whole point of the investigation, since "add a tab" invites three separate wrong assumptions:

1. **Advisor and accountant CIQ are not two paths — they are one.** All three admin member views feed `MemberDirectoryView` through a single `extraTabs` prop, sourced from two module-level constants in `MembersPanel.jsx`: `DEFAULT_EXTRA_TABS` (advisors + accountants, line ~53) and `STRATEGIC_EXTRA_TABS` (line ~63). There is **one** render site for the feature tabs (line ~453) and **one** `MemberCIQ` mount with `isAdmin=true` (line ~465). So the change was never "port a feature to strategic" — it was "stop omitting an entry from a list", and advisor/accountant behaviour is unchanged by construction.
2. **The member-FACING portal already had CIQ for strategic members.** `MemberPortal.jsx` builds its tabs from a static list that has always included `ciq`; strategic members logging into their own portal have always seen it. **Only the admin-side profile view was trimmed** — so this was an admin-visibility gap, not a missing feature.
3. **No backend change was needed.** The `ciq_*` actions are **not** in `TAB_ACTIONS`, so they are not tab-gated (contrast #167, where a new action behind a tab-gated surface must join the list or granted admins 403). Admin callers already pass the admin gate. `constants/role-gates.ts` was not touched, and the action count stayed **465**.
4. **The Growth Plan button cannot leak in.** It renders off a separate `growthPlan` prop that defaults `false`, and `StrategicMembersPanel` never passes it — so widening the tab list could not drag the advisor-only Growth Plan along with it.

**The change:** `['ciq', 'CIQ']` appended to `STRATEGIC_EXTRA_TABS` after Showroom, plus the comment block above `DEFAULT_MSM_OPTIONS` (lines ~41-44) re-worded so it now reads "Specialists + Showroom + CIQ (no Website Plugin / GC Marketplace / Growth Plan)" instead of listing CIQ among the exclusions. Strategic keeps its trimmed MSM options (Holistic + Tax Planning only) and its two program toggles.

**Click-through, run by the owner and passed:** the CIQ tab appears on a Strategic Member profile and opens the questionnaire; advisor and accountant profiles are unchanged (regression check); and no unwanted tab leaked into the strategic view — **Website Plugin, GC Marketplace and Growth Plan are all still absent**.

**Test data cleaned:** a client created during testing — `clients` id **279** ("Jake Test", under member **20007**) — was deleted along with its CIQ tree and its `client_progress` row (the CIQ-complete auto-tick from the 2026-08-03 `syncMap1CiqStep` side effect). Re-queried afterwards: **0 rows** remain for all three.

## 2026-08-21 — Three real-money/real-email defects found by one client's failed installment: `/pay` was payment-1-only, the Connect setup email double-sent, and a membership confirmation said "Payment 2 of 1"

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v772 → v773 (`/pay` + email fixes) → v774 (setup-email guard) → v775 (membership confirmation re-read), all deployed; v775 is live. TWO frontend `npm run deploy` publishes. One migration `20260821120000_members_connect_setup_email_sent_at.sql` (applied via MCP + committed, #196). `boldsign-webhook` untouched at v40.** Smoke 5/5 was run by the owner after **each** deploy including v775; the security advisor was re-checked after the migration and matches the documented baseline exactly. New gotchas **#427** (post-activation stale object) and **#428** (`send_mode` flip without a UI-copy audit).

### 1. `/pay` was a payment-1-only surface while the installment-failure email mailed that URL for P2–P4

Lenny Genna (client 272, `pipeline_map1` 143, Quarterly, `net_invoice` 2700, `card_fee_waived=true`) had P1 and P2 succeed and **P3 decline** on 2026-08-15. The nightly sweep did exactly what it should: marked P3 `declined`, rang the bell, and drafted him the failure email carrying `https://vfoportal.com/pay?token=…`. **That link could not work.** Both public handlers hard-guarded on `pay1_status` being truthy and returned *"Payment already completed"*, and `contract-load-payment.ts` hardcoded `payment_x: "1"`. The dead end had existed since the installment-failure email shipped; Lenny was simply the first client to walk into it.

Four separate defects sat behind that one URL, and all four are fixed:
- **Open-installment resolution.** New shared `utils/map1-open-installment.ts` — the lowest N in 1..4 whose `payN_status` is `declined`/`auth_required`, or is null with `payN_date` set and ≤ today. `pending`/`processing`/`succeeded` are deliberately NOT open, so a processing ACH can never be paid twice. **Payment 1 is open on a null status alone**, a deliberate divergence from the literal spec: `pay1_date` is only written when payment 1 clears (verified — all 5 rows with `pay1_status IS NULL` have `pay1_date IS NULL`), so a date test would have broken every new `/pay` link. No open N ⇒ 400, *"Payment already completed"* when every scheduled installment succeeded, else *"No payment is due right now"*. Exercised against 10 real and synthetic row shapes.
- **The card-fee waiver was ignored.** `contract-stripe-checkout.ts` grossed up by 2.9% + $0.30 unconditionally, so a `card_fee_waived` client was overcharged relative to what the nightly sweep would have taken. It now mirrors the sweep's math exactly. Lenny pays a flat **$675**.
- **The webhook could not tell which installment it was.** The session now stamps `payment_intent_data.metadata.payment_number=N`, which routes it to the existing `payN_status` + receipt + revshare chain. **Both webhook branches were read and verified before shipping, not assumed:** `payment_intent.succeeded` books N=3 correctly, and the `checkout.session.completed` MAP 1 branch self-skips on `if (pipeRow && !pipeRow.pay1_status)` so a P3 payment cannot double-book as P1. No webhook code was changed. The memo also reads *"Payment N"* instead of *"Payment 1"*.
- **A DB error masqueraded as a bad token** (#187) — both handlers now destructure `{data, error}` and return a distinct 500.

The frontend matched the backend: `PayPage.jsx` hardcoded the gross-up in **four** places (badge, headline, breakdown row, footer copy), all now switched by a new `card_fee_waived` field on the load response, backward-compatible when the field is absent.

**Live-verified:** Lenny's page renders *Payment 3 of 4*, **$675.00**, a green "No Fee" badge, and the Stripe session shows $675 with memo *"Payment 3"*. The owner sent his failure email and the link works.

**Two pre-existing gaps were deliberately NOT fixed** and are now documented: a `/pay` ACH payment for N≥2 leaves `payN_status` at `declined` while the debit is in flight (the same link is payable twice for 2–4 days — the identical window already exists for P1), and a `/pay` payment for N≥2 never refreshes `payment_method_type` / `acct_last4` / `default_payment_method_id`, because the `checkout.session.completed` branch that writes those self-skips. **One new consequence to watch:** once a check-paying client's first check clears and `pay2_date` arrives, the resolver now calls P2 open, so an old `/pay` link would let them pay that quarter by card/ACH. Money is still collected exactly once, but the row would mix payment methods.

### 2. `member_stripe_connect_request` real-sends and had no guard, while the UI told admins to go send a draft

`member_connect_setup` (template id 159) was flipped `send_mode=true` back on 2026-08-03, but both success messages in `MembersPanel.jsx` kept their draft-era wording — *"Account … created — send the draft from Gmail"*. An admin, told to send something that was already sent, found nothing in Drafts and clicked again; the action had **no re-send guard**, so **Ade 30007 was emailed twice, three minutes apart** (confirmed in the logs). A third defect compounded it: the Settings card branched on the stale `member.stripe_account_id` prop from `allMembers`, which the Profile card's send deliberately does not refresh (#245), so the card still showed the first-time CTA after a successful send.

All three halves are fixed. `members.connect_setup_email_sent_at` (nullable timestamptz) is the guard: when set, the handler returns `200 {already_sent_at, to_email}` **before any side effect** — no Connect account, no token, no email — unless `force: true`. A successful send stamps it (`{error}` destructured and logged, never fatal, since the mail is already out). Both FE handlers show a `window.confirm` naming the prior date and re-call with `force: true` on OK; both are backward-compatible with a backend that never returns `already_sent_at`. The Settings card now asks `member_connect_status` on mount instead of trusting the cached prop, with a skeleton while it loads — and its pre-existing `onDataChange()` was swapped for a local refetch, since a global reload here is the exact #245 skeleton flash. **Backfilled** 29 members from `connect_setup_tokens.created_at`; Ade's stamp reads 2026-08-20 20:22:26Z.

**Sibling audit:** all four connect-request templates are `send_mode=true`, and all three siblings claimed a draft. Their **copy** was corrected (`SpecialistsPanel.jsx`, `StrategicPartnersPanel.jsx`, `TaxPlannersPanel.jsx` — one string each); **their guards were not built** and remain owed.

### 3. "Payment 2 of 1" on a membership confirmation (Manos 58114, plan 49)

The `checkout.session.completed` membership branch loads the plan once, then `activateMembershipPlan` **rewrites `start_date` to the pay date** and writes the ledger under it — after which the branch passed its **pre-activation** object to `draftMembershipConfirmationEmail`, which counts the year via `.eq("year_start", plan.start_date)`. Zero rows matched, so `yearMonths = 0` and the ordinal rendered as `prior + 1` over `prior + 0`. Fixed caller-side: re-read the plan by id after activation, pass the fresh row, fall back to the stale one on a re-read failure (a garbled draft beats no draft — it is Draft-mode and human-reviewed). **`membership-confirmation.ts` was not touched**: its `year_start` filter is the correct #316 row-money derivation, and "fixing" it would break the money math to paper over a staleness bug. Only `plan.transfer` plans could hit it, and only when creation and payment fall on different UTC days. **No money was affected** — the ledger and the charge were always right; only the sentence was wrong.

### 4. Email hygiene that rode along

The shared `VFO_SIGNATURE` footer is now appended **in code** by three more handlers (`utils/map1-installment-failure.ts`, `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts`, `actions/tax/charge-implementation.ts`), and the old baked-in *"AI-PC / Proactive Coordinator / VFO SERVICES"* block was stripped from template rows **175, 176, 179, 180** so no draft carries two footers. Rows 179 and 11 also had subject/tail cleanups. `[Client Name]` now substitutes in the MAP 1 installment-failure email. A **$0 revenue share no longer drafts a pointless email** in all three revshare handlers — and, after review, the skip was **restructured so only the Gmail draft is suppressed**: every stamp (`rec{N}_rev_email_sent`, `pip_rev_member_email_sent_at`, `{retainer,implementation}_rev_email_sent`) still writes exactly as before, because the first attempt would have left Tax 5 permanently incomplete and Tax 6 locked on a zero-share plan. The inaccurate *"Client emailed with a fresh /pay link"* bell text is now *"Client emailed a payment link."* in both the sweep and the ACH-late-failure webhook branch, and in the `notification_rules` row.

**Known cosmetic consequence:** rows 175/176 are boxed card layouts, so the code-appended footer now renders **below** the card, full-width and unstyled. The next real rev-share draft is its first eyeball.

## 2026-08-20 (4th) — Sessions record their minting portal (`login_type`) — the dual-identity collision flagged in the previous session is fixed (#425/#426)

**Backend `vfo-admin-api` v771 → v772, deployed and live-verified; one migration `20260820210000_add_login_type_to_admin_sessions.sql`. Frontend banner changes are committed on the branch (`97ad5a5` + `8ce96a2`) with the FE deploy still pending at the time this entry was written.** No allowlist, gate list or role-gate constant changed anywhere in the session — the whole change is in *how the caller's role is decided*, not in what any role may do.

**The incident, restated in one paragraph.** Carson Grover (`cgrover@wealthig.com`) is **tax planner id 3** and, from 2026-08-20 18:41Z, also **member 58014**. He signed into the MEMBER portal, got a perfectly valid session, and every tab rendered blank with Growth Plan showing *"Coming soon"*. The session was never wrong; the **role lookup** was. This is the prose that used to sit in a ⚠️ box in `architecture/04-auth-and-sessions.md`, preserved here because the box is now a resolution note: *`admin_sessions` stored the token, the email and an expiry and **no `login_type`**, so `middleware/auth.ts` re-derived the caller's role at request time by probing the login tables in a fixed order — **admin → client → specialist → tax_planner → member** — and returning on the first hit. Which portal actually minted the session was not recorded and could not be recovered. Therefore **any** email holding two portal identities resolved to the higher-precedence one, in both directions, for every session.* Carson's member session resolved as `callerRole "tax_planner"`, so the deny-by-default gate matched his member-portal actions against `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` and **403'd every one of them** (`function_edge_logs`: bursts of three 403s per tab click, 18:41:44 through 18:45). The reverse direction was worse and quieter — creating a tax-planner row on an email that already had a member login **silently promoted that person's existing member sessions**, an authorization widening rather than a blank screen. The two long-documented "admin-collision caveats" (a specialist, and a client/planner, whose email is also an admin) were never special cases at all; they were two instances of this one structural fact. The interim rule while it was unfixed — **one email may hold at most ONE portal identity, check the other five login tables before creating any login row** — is now **retired**.

**The mechanism.** `admin_sessions` gained a nullable **`login_type text`** with a CHECK constraint (`admin | member | client | specialist | tax_planner`). **All six login actions stamp it** — the five portal logins stamp their own type and the legacy `login` action stamps `'admin'`. `middleware/auth.ts` resolves the caller's role **from `login_type`**, and then **re-verifies the identity row still exists** in the matching login table (`allowed_admins` / `client_logins` / `specialist_logins` / `tax_planner_logins` / `member_logins`). **A missing row is a `401`, never a fall-through to another role** — that direction of failure is what created the bug in the first place, so it is now closed by construction rather than by ordering. Two hardenings rode along: a **non-admin-typed session gets `allowedTabs = []`** even when the same email also holds an `allowed_admins` row (a lower portal must not inherit admin tabs), and **`isSuperadmin` now requires `callerRole === "admin"` as well as the `SUPERADMIN_EMAIL` match** (previously an email-only test, so a superadmin signing into a lower portal would have kept the superadmin bypass). `utils/tax-planner-ownership.ts` learned the same rule through a shared **`isPlannerSession()`**: a session with a known `login_type` decides on its own (only `tax_planner` is a planner), and critically a **`tax_planner`-typed session SKIPS the old `allowed_admins` bail-out**, so an admin-email planner session stays inside the group fence instead of sailing through unrestricted. Both `resolvePlannerGroupIds` and `resolveCallerPlanner` go through it.

**The email precedence chain is kept, as a fallback and nothing more.** A session with `login_type IS NULL` — i.e. minted before the deploy — is resolved by the old admin → client → specialist → tax_planner → member probe, verbatim. Those sessions all carry the standard **8h** expiry, so the branch becomes dead weight roughly 8 hours after the v772 deploy and is **retirable later**; until it is deleted, a legacy session still exhibits the original shadowing behaviour exactly as documented. No backfill was attempted: stamping a type onto a session whose minting portal is genuinely unknowable would be inventing data.

**The frontend half (#426), which is presentation only.** `src/lib/api.js` was **NOT changed** — it still redirects on a 401 and still merely throws on a 403, which was the correct call: a 403 must not redirect (the session is valid, so it would loop). What changed is that the four portal shells that had been catching-to-empty-state — **Member, Admin, Client and Specialist** — now render a visible *"We couldn't load your portal"* banner when their startup load fails; the tax-planner portal already had one, so all five surfaces now say something. That does not make 403s loud everywhere, and the diagnostic rule is unchanged: a blank surface whose data provably exists means **read `function_edge_logs` for 403s first**.

**The verification story, stated precisely.** Carson's case was walked **in both directions on the shipped code**: a member-typed session reaches the member portal and its actions **200**, a planner-typed session reaches the planner portal and works, and **every cross-portal probe 403s** — the fix is a lock, not a widening. A **five-portal click-through** covered the other roles, and the **5-pipeline smoke gate ran 5/5 PASS** against v772 (mandatory here: `middleware/auth.ts` is shared routing code). **The one path nobody has exercised is Carson's own organic re-login** — his broken pre-deploy sessions expire **2026-08-21 ~02:40Z**, and the next time he signs in normally is the first non-staged run of the whole change.
