## 2026-08-20 (3rd) — The extra Cc moves off the form and onto the person: Additional Contacts now Cc themselves onto every client email and can be named in the greeting — plus a dual-identity login collision that was found, not fixed

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-b987ab`, BOTH repos, one chat, no handoff blocks.** `vfo-admin-api` v766 → **v767** (phase 1) → **v768** (phase 2) → **v769** (phase 3) → **v770** (phase 4) → **v771** (phases 5–6), each deploy explicitly approved, shipping version **v771** ACTIVE with `verify_jwt=false`. `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**; `draft-agreement-pdfs` still v1. **Three migrations, all applied to live:** `20260820190148_client_contacts_cc_toggles` (schema) plus the two one-time data backfills `20260820193959_backfill_client_contacts_cc_from_extra_cc` and `20260820200601_backfill_client_contacts_cc_peg_buehrle` — the backfills ran through MCP first and were committed as files afterwards, **named to match their recorded `schema_migrations` versions exactly** so a rebuilt environment neither misses them nor double-applies them (#196). Action count **464 → 465** (`msm_update_client_contact`). `deno check --no-lock` **0 errors**; `npm run build` exit 0, **33 route pages** (unchanged); security advisor at the **exact GREEN baseline**, re-confirmed after the schema migration *and* after the data backfills. The **5-pipeline smoke gate ran 5/5 PASS against every deployed version including v771**, the one that ships. At the time this entry was written the **frontend was NOT yet published** (live site still `live-158`).

**The bug that started it.** `pipfu-decision.ts` saved the MAP 1 decision form's *"Additional CC recipients"* into `pipeline_map1.extra_cc` — and then **its own Undecided/No email never read the column back.** Veronica Esmero was entered as an extra Cc on Dane Rogol (client **163**) and was **not** on the 2026-08-17 `PCADMIN_followup|Undecided` email, because the handler that captured her address was not one of the handlers that used it. The audit that followed found the real shape of the problem: **portal-wide, only 5 of ~114 sender files ever read `extra_cc` at all.** The mechanism had been sold to admins as *"these email addresses will be CC'd on all client emails"* and delivered on that promise in under 5% of sends. Fixing the one handler would have left the same lie in place everywhere else, so the mechanism itself was replaced.

**The replacement, in one sentence: an extra Cc is a property of a PERSON, not of a form submission.** `client_contacts` — the existing "additional contacts" list on the client profile — gained two boolean columns, `cc_on_emails` and `use_in_greeting`, both defaulting `false`. A contact flagged `cc_on_emails` rides along on every client-facing email for that client, forever, regardless of which pipeline or which form produced it. A contact ALSO flagged `use_in_greeting` gets their first name folded into the salutation.

**Phase 1 (v767) — the data and the switches.** Email became **REQUIRED** on every newly added contact (`actions/msm/add-client-contact.ts`, validated against the same regex `dedupeEmails` uses, so nothing unusable can be stored in the first place); pre-existing blank-email rows keep working but can never be flipped on. A NEW action **`msm_update_client_contact`** (`actions/msm/update-client-contact.ts`) edits one row: name and email are editable by anyone who reaches the handler (a member on their own client passes `denyIfNotOwnClient`), and **the two toggles are admin-only**. That admin test is written `auth.callerRole === "admin"` and **deliberately not** the looser `!== "member"` idiom used by `msm_update_client` — a tax planner authenticates as `callerRole "tax_planner"`, so the loose form would have handed planners the switches. Its gate placement mirrors `msm_add_client_contact` exactly: `MEMBER_SCOPED_ACTIONS` only, no `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS` entry. Both invariants are enforced on the **final state** (stored row merged with the incoming patch), never on the incoming fields alone, so a two-step edit cannot sneak past them: **Cc requires an email on the row; greeting requires Cc.** Blanking the email out from under a live Cc is refused with its own message. `ClientDetail.jsx`'s profile card gained the required-email add form, an inline per-row Edit, and the two checkboxes.

**Phase 2 (v768) — the resolver.** `utils/additional-contact.ts` exports `loadAdditionalContacts(supabase, clientId)` → `{ ccList, greetingFirsts }`. It **never throws and never propagates a DB error** — a missing Cc must not take an email down with it — and it feeds `resolveTemplateRecipients`'s pre-existing 6th `extraCc` parameter, so sandbox suppression, To-collision filtering, dedupe and validation are all inherited rather than re-implemented. Wired at the 13 MAP 1 / contract sites first, **including the original bug site**. The legacy `pipeline_map1.extra_cc` read in `contract-send-agreement.ts` was **REPLACED, not merged** — merging would have double-Cc'd every backfilled address.

**Phase 3 (v769) — TAX.** 25 more sites. The three legacy `client_tax_plans.extra_cc` reads (`send-agreement`, `extra-meeting`, `final-decision`) replaced the same way, and `decision.ts`'s in-request `ccArray` appends replaced. **`utils/extra-cc.ts` was DELETED** — zero importers remained. `revshare-sweep`'s assess-reminder tiers were deliberately left alone: those emails go to the **planner**, not the client, so a client's Cc has no business on them.

**Phase 4 (v770) — the remaining 17 sites**, across PFT (six, threaded carefully around the previous session's #424 `MEMBER` lines), PIP (four), Regular (two), migration, the vault request-docs **client** branch and the card-update **client** branch. **Two sites were wired and then REVERTED before deploy, on the user's call: `login-setup/send-email.ts` and `request-reset.ts`.** A password-reset or login-setup link is a **credential**, and an additional contact is not entitled to one — so login-security emails are permanently outside this mechanism. `presentation-sweep` was kept wired even though its To is the member, on the grounds that the client is a subject of that email rather than a bystander.

**Phases 5–6 (v771) — the greeting, and the form teardown.** `withGreetingNames(first, greetingFirsts)` joins with `" and "` → *"Dane and Veronica"*, applied to the `[Client First]` token at **42 sites**. It is **body-only**: `tax/request-returns.ts` and `request-additional-info.ts` carry an explicit subject-guard keeping the plain first name, because a compound name in a subject line reads as a mistake. **The wrap-up diff audit found two sites that cannot carry that guard** — `utils/map1-installment-failure.ts` and `actions/tax/deposit-refund.ts` render subject and body through **one shared `subst()` closure**, so the greeting lands on both by construction. Neither template's subject contains `[Client First]` (a portal-wide query returns **zero** subjects holding that token), so nothing is wrong today; it is recorded as a latent trap rather than fixed, because the code was already deployed and the correct fix is to split those two substituters, not to patch around them. Both decision forms (`PIPDecisionForm.jsx`, `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx`) had their Cc chip UI and payload field removed, leaving a muted one-liner — *"Extra Cc is now managed on the client profile (Additional Contacts)."* — and `pipfu-decision.ts` / `tax/decision.ts` **stopped writing `extra_cc` entirely**. **The two columns still exist and are now dormant: nothing reads them, nothing writes them.** They were kept rather than dropped so the historical values stay auditable, and for the same reason the `AutomationPanel` / `TaxAutomationPanel` **read-only "Extra CC" display rows were deliberately kept** — they show what a past submission recorded, which is history, not routing.

**Final wiring, as derived at wrap-up:** 45 files import the helper, **53 `loadAdditionalContacts` call sites**, **42 `withGreetingNames` call sites**, and **zero live reads or writes of `extra_cc` anywhere in `vfo-admin-api`** (the ten remaining matches are all explanatory comments).

**Decisions the user made, recorded because the code cannot explain itself.** Member-pays-on-behalf emails **still Cc the client's contact** (the client remains the subject even when the member is the payer). Every legacy `extra_cc` address was backfilled with **Cc ON, greeting OFF** — greeting is opt-in per person and nobody had consented to it. **Exactly one legacy address was deliberately dropped: `cmoses@tes85.com` (client 149, Fredric Moses)**, on the user's instruction; it is the only exclusion and must not be "restored" by a future tidy-up. Peg Buehrle (client 156) was dropped by *mistake* while applying that exclusion and was restored by the second backfill migration — which is why there are two backfill files rather than one. Toggle labels are *"Cc on all client emails"* / *"Include in the greeting"*. Toggles are admin-only, per-contact, with **no limit** on how many contacts a client may have. A contact with no email cannot enable Cc, and the refusal explains why rather than sitting silently disabled.

**Late UI polish (frontend only, uncommitted until this wrap-up):** the toggles now **stage** locally and commit through a per-row **Save** button with a green *"Saved"* flash, instead of firing a write per click; and the ClientHome contact list grew a second read-only pill, *"Included in greeting"*, beside the existing *"Cc'd on client emails"*.

**What was actually live-fired, stated precisely, because the CHANGELOG is where this gets overclaimed.** Phase 1's UI was click-tested end to end including the no-email refusal (Karen Flood) and toggle persistence. Then **four real sends**, each on the shipped code, each cleaned up afterwards: `pip1-reconfirmation` on Dane 163 (Veronica Cc'd; `client_progress` 913's `completed_date` restored to 2026-08-07), `tax request-returns` on Lorente 131 (Andrea Cc'd; both timestamps restored exactly), `card-update` on Hurst 123 (Dan the only Cc; token row deleted, table back to 0), and a greeting re-run of `pip1-reconfirmation` that produced *"Dear Dane and Veronica,"* (toggle flipped back off, stamp restored). Both stripped forms were checked in view and edit mode, and the UI polish got a full six-step click-through. **That is four sites out of 53.** Every other wired site — **including `pipfu-decision.ts`, the handler whose bug started this** — is verified by code review and the shared-resolver pattern only, and **the next real send of each is its verification**. The same qualification covers the greeting subject-guard (a latent-trap disarm — no active subject currently holds `[Client First]`) and the member/planner read-only view of the new badges.

**Separate investigation, zero code: one human, two portal identities, and a blank portal (gotchas #425 + #426).** Carson Grover (`cgrover@wealthig.com`) is **tax planner id 3** and, as of 18:41Z that day, **member 58014**. His member portal rendered every tab blank and Growth Plan as *"Coming soon"*. The session was fine; the **role** was wrong. `admin_sessions` stores no `login_type`, so `middleware/auth.ts` re-derives the caller's role from the **email address** with a fixed precedence — admin → client → specialist → tax_planner → **member** — and `tax_planner` wins, so his member session was gated against `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` and **403'd on every member action** (`function_edge_logs`: bursts of three 403s at 18:41:44, 18:42, 18:43, 18:44, 18:45 — one per tab). His member category *is* `advisor`; the Growth Plan data simply never loaded. Compounding it, **`src/lib/api.js` redirects on a 401 but swallows a 403**, so an authorization denial is indistinguishable on screen from an unbuilt feature. The fix — a `login_type` column on `admin_sessions` stamped by all six login actions and read by `middleware/auth.ts`, with the email probe kept as the fallback for pre-existing sessions — is **queued as a separate task and NOT built here**. Until it lands, **one email address may hold at most one portal identity**; check the other five login tables before creating any login row.

## 2026-08-20 (2nd) — Six small corrections and one that had been wrong since the pipeline was built: every email signs off as one team line, members get a personal-email field that nothing emails, the assess reminder gains an early tier, and PFT finally CCs the member

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-b1dc45`, BOTH repos, one chat, no handoff blocks.** `vfo-admin-api` v764 → **v765** (items 1–6) → **v766** (item 7, added after a mid-session user report), both deploys explicitly approved and both ACTIVE, `verify_jwt=false`. `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**; `draft-agreement-pdfs` still v1. **Two migrations, both applied:** `20260820140000_members_personal_email.sql` and `20260820141000_tax3_assess_reminder_early.sql`. Action count **unchanged at 464** — no dispatch action was added, removed or renamed; existing handlers changed shape. `npm run build` exit 0, **33 route pages** (unchanged); crons **15** (unchanged); `deno check --no-lock` **0 errors**; security advisor at the **exact GREEN baseline, re-confirmed after BOTH migrations**. The **5-pipeline smoke gate ran 5/5 PASS twice — once against v765 and again against v766** (the shipping version). At the time this entry was written the **frontend was NOT yet published**.

**1. Presentation-link chip wording.** `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` — *"Email drafted — "* became *"Email drafted for "*. Frontend microcopy only; the data source (`presentation_send_date`) and every handler are untouched. No doc surface: nothing in `docs/` ever quoted the old string.

**2. A "Custom" specialist on Regular Priorities.** The Add Regular Priority picker gained a trailing **Custom** option that swaps in a free-text input (placeholder *"Name"*). `msm_add_priority_track` accepts `custom: true` + `custom_name` and **the server owns the `"Custom - "` prefix** — the sanitizer was copied from the tax add-specialist path rather than re-derived. The frontend *also* sends an already-prefixed `specialist_name` purely for **deploy-window compatibility**: the currently-published handler stores that same value, so the interim is correct either way. Live-tested against v765: the empty-name refusal, and a stored `"Custom - Jake Latham"` verified in the DB and then deleted. `tables/clients.md`'s `specialist_name` row now records that it may hold `"Custom - <name>"` and that the prefix is server-owned.

**3. The member email split — `members.personal_email`.** A new nullable column that **nothing ever emails**. `members.email` is and remains the sole routing address, and the whole point of the change is to make that unambiguous **at the point of entry**, so the relabel is the substance: **"Work email (emails sent here)"** on Edit Profile, **"Work email"** on profile details, and **"Work Email \*"** on the three add forms plus the accountant and advisor onboarding start forms. The new field is edited as *"Personal email (not emailed)"*. It needed **no read or write code**: `member_profile_load` is a `select *` and `member_profile_save` is a passthrough upsert. It is **deliberately absent from `load-data.ts`'s whitelisted member payload** (#207), so it cannot leak to the member portal or the admin roster. All labels click-tested. **One REAL personal email is deliberately stored** on member **58088** (Jack Branch) as the proof row — a hub line says keep it.

**4. Name sync — the portal display name finally follows a rename.** `member_plugin_settings.name` is what the admin header, the members list, avatar initials and the member's own login greeting read — **not** `members.first_name`/`last_name` — and it was written once at member creation and **never resynced**, so renaming a member on the profile form left the old name on every one of those surfaces. `member_profile_save` now also updates it to the whitespace-collapsed `"first last"` after the `members` upsert, **skipping when the result is empty** rather than blanking the row. A one-time backfill resynced the **2** rows that had already diverged (**30005** Satonya→Santonya Jones; **90417** a double space). Both directions live-tested post-deploy. `tables/members.md` carries the fix plus a drift-detection query.

**5. Footer consolidation — 57 literals became one constant.** `VFO_SIGNATURE` in `utils/gmail-draft.ts` now renders a **single line**, *"VFO Services - Proactive Coordinator Team"*, in the same styling as before. **All 57 inline `const signature = '<p …'` literals across 52 action files were deleted and repointed to the constant** — the two-paragraph **AI-PC / Proactive Coordinator / VFO SERVICES** persona block is gone system-wide. Greps for `"AI-PC"` and `signature = '<p` over `supabase/functions/` both return **0**, and the result was confirmed in a real drafted email. `glossary.md` retires the **AI-PC** entry to historical (the name survives only in the `aipc@vfo-services.com` From: address, still used by `automation_CONTRACT_sendagreement`); `integrations/gmail.md` and `tables/membership-fees.md` carry the new shape.

**6. A 5-business-day EARLY tier for the Tax 2 assess-form reminder.** A second, independent tier beside the existing 2-day chase in `actions/tax/revshare-sweep.ts`: rule **`TAX_tax3_assess_reminder_early_email`** (default **5**, sort **214**), guard column **`client_tax_plans.tax3_assess_reminder_early_sent_at`**, templates **`TAX_tax3_assess_reminder_early`** + a **`|vault`** verbatim clone, both Draft-mode and seeded. **The two tiers cannot share a stamp** — they fire on different nights for the same plan — so this is two independent one-shots, not a ladder. The early window is **strictly beyond** the 2-day horizon (`.gt(tax3_meeting_date, assessHorizon).lte(tax3_meeting_date, assessEarlyHorizon)`), which is what stops the tiers double-drafting; the **cost of that design is a config edge** — an admin setting the early delay to **≤ 2** makes it silently never fire. `ready-for-tax3.ts` **re-arms BOTH stamps** on a genuine date change. `templateMeta.js` gained the pair, sorted ahead of the 2-day rows, whose labels became *"LATER, last-call"*. **Live-tested both variants** against v765 on test plan **152** / client **62** (sandboxed): a manual sweep drafted the **vault** variant (test planner) *and* the **standard** variant (planner Steven Cox), both stamps verified, the **2-day stamp stayed NULL**, and the fixture was fully reset afterwards. **Also fixed in passing:** the OLD 2-day rule's `notification_rules.description` still said *"days"* — it was never updated when the unit changed to business days on 2026-08-14 — and now reads **"BUSINESS days"** (SQL, no code).

**7. The one that had been wrong all along — PFT never CCd the member (v766, gotcha #424).** Reported by the user mid-session, after items 1–6 had already shipped. **Nine of the ten `PARTNERSHIP_FAST_TRACK` templates** (ids 104–110, 196, 197 — every meeting-confirm, meeting-declined, decision and reminder row) list **`MEMBER` in `cc_list`**, and had since they were seeded. **No PFT handler had ever passed a `MEMBER` key** into `resolveTemplateRecipients`, so the token resolved to nothing and was **dropped silently on every send** — the connected member has never been CC'd on a single PFT email in the pipeline's entire life.

**Nothing could have surfaced it.** Unresolvable tokens are dropped by design (#413 — the safe direction, deliberately not hardened into a throw); the drafts were well-formed; the `to` list was always non-empty so the `rcp.to.length === 0` guard never fired; sandbox suppresses all Cc anyway; and every row in the pipeline agreed with every other, so there was no odd one out. **Consistency across a pipeline is evidence of a shared code path, not evidence that the code path is correct** — that is the new lesson, and the reason this is #424 rather than another instance of #324/#413. The same class was caught once before at *two*-template scale (`CLIENT_PAYMENT_CONTINUATION`, fixed 2026-08-03 in v696); at whole-pipeline scale it is strictly harder to see.

**The fix.** New helper **`memberEmailForClient`** in `actions/pft/_shared.ts` — `clients.member_number` → `members.email`, returning `null` for a client with no member and **swallowing lookup errors**, since `resolveTemplateRecipients` drops unresolvable tokens and a failed lookup must never break a send. Then a one-line **`MEMBER: await memberEmailForClient(...)`** at the **four** ctx-building call sites that between them cover all nine templates: `decision-email.ts` (shared ctx, ~41), `meeting-email.ts` (~55), and `sweep.ts`'s `sendDiscoveryReminder` (~196) + `sendFtReminder` (~269). **`sendUndecidedReminder` / `undecided-email.ts` were deliberately left untouched:** their template `PFT_decision_undecided` (id 193) carries **no `MEMBER` token at all** — empty `to_list`, `cc_list` of two literal staff addresses — so there is nothing to resolve, and adding the token would change who receives the client's own decision email, which is a decision rather than a patch.

**HOW IT WAS TESTED, and exactly where the coverage stops.** Beyond the gates above, item 7 was **live-tested on one path**: Justin Rosen (client **117**, member **Gary LoDuca 60101**) — `ft_reminder` re-armed, the PFT sweep triggered, and the resulting draft **showed Gary in Cc**; the draft was deleted and the stamp restored to its original `2026-08-15 08:00:06.607+00`. **The other three call sites are the identical one-line addition and are code-reviewed only, so the next real send of each is its verification** — recorded in the hub's OWED list, along with four other unexercised paths: the **2-day assess tier was never re-run after the early tier landed beside it** (its code is untouched and the early test confirmed its stamp stayed NULL, but the two have never both fired on one plan); the early tier's **≤ 2-day config edge**; and the name-sync's **empty-name skip** and **plugin-update-error** branches.

**DB data operations beyond the two migrations.** The name backfill (2 rows); the template seeds (2 rows + 1 rule); the 2-day rule's description text fix; and test rows created **and removed** — priority track id 94 on client 267, the plan-152 fixture set (fully nulled afterwards), and `pft_engagement` 13's stamp (nulled, then restored). **Gmail:** the PFT test draft was deleted by the user; the **two assess-reminder test drafts** (vault + standard, both addressed to the sandbox) may still sit in Drafts — a hand-cleanup item on the hub.

**Docs.** New gotcha **#424**, **registry-only** — it is a recipient-routing trap, but #324/#413 already hold the hub's curated slot for that family and the hub must not carry two entries saying "read the handler", so it was deliberately **not** promoted. `flows/partnership-fast-track.md` gained an **"Email recipients"** section (the four ctx sites, the helper, the historical gap, and the `PFT_decision_undecided` exception) and **lost a stale count** — it claimed the pipeline had *"9 rows"* when it has **10**, contradicting `integrations/gmail.md`'s independently-correct *"PARTNERSHIP_FAST_TRACK (10)"*; per **#402** the number was replaced with the query rather than corrected. `integrations/gmail.md`'s resolution-contract section gained the PFT instance beside the existing payment-continuation one. `architecture/05-api-action-catalog.md`'s `automation_PFT_meetingemail`, `automation_PFT_decisionemail` and `automation_PFT_sweep` rows each record the ctx change, and the sweep row records the undecided exception. Items 1–6 were documented by an earlier in-session pass across 13 files; a diff of the branch file list against that pass found **no uncovered change** — the 52 footer-edit action files need no surface beyond `gmail.md`, and item 1 is microcopy no doc quotes. Hub **DOC MAP: NOOP**; **SECURITY INVARIANTS: unchanged** (byte-compared).

**Superseded hub values.** Live `vfo-admin-api` **v764 → v766**. Action count **unchanged at 464**, re-derived. Route pages **33**, crons **15**, security-advisor baseline **unchanged**, the last re-confirmed after both migrations. `flows/partnership-fast-track.md`'s PFT template count **9 → 10** (now a query, not a number).

## 2026-08-20 — Growth Credits got an owner: every marketplace service now names the team member who fulfils it, reroutes its bell to them, and emails the member a confirmation with their scheduling link

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-e86ec3`, BOTH repos, one chat, no handoff blocks.** `vfo-admin-api` v762 → **v763** → **v764** (two deploys, both mid-session and explicitly approved; v764 exists only because the Remove/delete branch was added after v763 shipped). `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**; `draft-agreement-pdfs` still v1. Action count **unchanged at 464** — `router/dispatch.ts` and `index.ts` were never opened; three existing GC handlers changed shape instead. **One migration, `gc_service_allocation`.** At the time this entry was written the **frontend was NOT yet published**, which matters more than usual here — see the interim hazard below.

**The gap.** The GC marketplace could take a member's credits but had no idea who was supposed to *do* the work. Every redemption bell went to the member's assigned MSM regardless of what was redeemed, so a website build and a coaching hour both landed on the same person, who then had to forward it. Nothing told the member what happened next, and nothing gave them a way to book the meeting they had just paid for.

**Schema.** `gc_services` gained **`allocated_admin_email`** (validated against `allowed_admins`) and **`scheduling_link`**, both nullable — an unallocated service keeps the old behaviour exactly. Seeded **19 of 22** active services: Ian Welham (coaching, 2 rows, both with Calendly links), Lindsay Czajka (all 15 VFO Website + Virtual Marketing rows, 2 with HubSpot links), Tray Valdés-Dennis (Corporate Member Sponsorship), Tracy Miller (Business Advisory). **Ids 5, 7 and 8 were left NULL deliberately** — Jake chose not to allocate the two Tailored Tracks or the Advanced Coaching package.

**Routing (`actions/gc/redeem.ts`).** When a service has an allocated team member the `GC_credits_spent` bell goes to **them**; otherwise both historical fallbacks (assigned MSM, then the MSM team with the *"assign an MSM"* prompt) are preserved **byte-for-byte**. No new rule key — per **#411** the bell's title is the clear contract and the recipient is free, so the existing rule was re-addressed rather than duplicated. The `ASSIGNED_MSM` dynamic token name was deliberately KEPT even though it now often carries a non-MSM address, because `notification_rules.default_recipients` still names it; the row's `recipients` override was checked and is **null**, so the handler default is operative (**#324/#413** — read the handler, not the rule row).

**The confirmation email — new `utils/gc-redemption-email.ts`, modelled on `membership-confirmation.ts`.** Template **id 226**, pipeline `GROWTH_CREDITS`, name `GC_redemption_confirmation`, `active`, **`send_mode = false`** (draft — so **#325**'s "exactly ELEVEN `send_mode=true` rows" is still true). `to_list ["RECIPIENT"]`, `cc_list ["TEAM_MEMBER"]`. Fire-and-forget behind its own try/catch after the bell: the credits are already spent, so no failure in here may ever fail the redemption. Six tokens, two of which carry the design: **`[Credits Spent]`** renders *"1 Growth Credit"* / *"N Growth Credits"* / *"0 Growth Credits (free of charge)"*, and **`[MEETING_LINK_TEXT]`** emits the scheduling sentence + anchor only when the service has BOTH a link and an allocation. An **unallocated** service still emails — `[Team Member Name]` becomes *"Our team"* and the `TEAM_MEMBER` ctx is omitted, so the Cc token resolves to nothing and drops silently rather than to a stray address.

**Payload split (`actions/gc/load-services.ts`).** Was `select *` for everyone, which would have shipped internal staff emails to the member marketplace. Members now get the two new columns **stripped**; admins additionally get `allocated_admin_name` per service and a sorted `admins: [{name,email}]` list for the dropdown. The **#167/#385 gate check was run and deliberately came back NO-CHANGE**: `gc_load_services` is in no gate list, and the tab gate denies only actions it *maps*, so a `growth_credits`-only admin can already call it — adding it to `TAB_ACTIONS.growth_credits` would have **newly restricted** it and locked automation-only admins out of the service editor. Recorded because the reflex here is to widen.

**Frontend.** `GrowthCreditsPanel.jsx` (Automation & Config) grew per-row editing of name, description (resizable textarea), category (a dropdown built from the categories in use, with an `+ Add new category…` escape hatch that swaps in a text input and can be backed out of), team member, scheduling link and cost — all riding **one** Save; the Active pill became a sliding switch; and a **Remove** button with a confirm modal calls the new `mode:'delete'` branch. `GrowthCreditsRedemptionsPage.jsx` lost its sort pills and became two sub-tabs — **Redemptions** and a read-only **Menu** — using the pill strip copied verbatim from `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx:299-306` so it is format-identical to Accounting > Members. `EmailTemplatesPanel.jsx` + `templateMeta.js` gained the Growth Credits section.

**Delete is refused when history exists, on purpose.** `gc_redemptions.service_id` is `ON DELETE NO ACTION`, so the handler catches Postgres **`23503`** and returns a **400** *"This service has redemption history — set it Inactive instead."* Redemptions are never cascaded — the history has to keep resolving — and Inactive remains the way to retire a service anyone has used.

**Two bugs found in review, both pre-existing and both now fixed.** (1) `gc_manage_service` opened with `if (!name || !credit_cost)`, so **service 13 "Website Exploratory Meeting", which legitimately costs 0**, 400'd on *every* save — latent since the handler was written, reachable only once the new editor put that row in the click path (gotcha **#423**). (2) An Edit wrote a **raw NUL byte** into a sentinel string literal; the build stayed green while `git diff` reported *"Binary files differ"* and ripgrep **silently skipped the file** (gotcha **#422**).

**HOW IT WAS TESTED, and exactly where the coverage stops.** `deno check --no-lock` **0 errors**; `npm run build` **exit 0**, 33 route pages; action count re-derived at **464**; security advisor re-run after the DDL and **exactly baseline** (5 deny-all INFO + pg_net WARN). **Smoke gate 5/5 PASS against v764** — the shipping version, not v763. **Live click-through against v763/v764:** both bell routes (allocated → Ian; unallocated → the assigned-MSM Paul fallback), Remove on a throwaway service, the slider, name/description/category edits, a **zero-cost row save** (the #423 fix), the sub-tabs, the Email Templates section, and the member marketplace confirmed unchanged. All test data was wiped afterwards (redemptions, transactions and bells deleted, balance restored to 2). **THREE things were NOT verified and are now hub OWED lines.** (a) **No redemption email has been drafted since the template body was restored** — a user edit had introduced a stray `<br><br>`, the body was put back, and the two drafts that *were* inspected (the unallocated *"Our team"* no-Cc variant, and the allocated + meeting-link variant) both rendered the **PRE-restore** body; **the next real redemption draft is the spacing fix's first verification.** (b) The **zero-credit `[Credits Spent]` wording** — *"0 Growth Credits (free of charge)"* — has never rendered in an actual draft, only in code. (c) The **Menu sub-tab's single-grid alignment rebuild** was the last change of the session: build-green and reviewed, but **never eyeballed**.

**INTERIM HAZARD while the frontend is unpublished.** `gc_manage_service`'s UPDATE writes `allocated_admin_email` and `scheduling_link` on **every** save, and a body that omits them cleans to `null`. The **currently published** Growth Credits panel does not send them. So until `npm run deploy` runs, **any admin who saves a service from the live panel silently wipes that service's allocation and scheduling link** — the seeds would need re-running. The new panel always sends current values (patch semantics) so the hazard closes the moment the frontend ships; it is called out here because the backend went live first and the two halves are only safe together.

**Docs.** New gotchas **#422** and **#423**, both **registry-only** — a tooling trap and a validation trap, neither a money/auth/data-loss/cross-repo invariant, so neither earns hub always-loaded status. `flows/gift-credits.md` updated in the redemption-flow section only (the file predates the 2026-07 GC overhaul and was deliberately not rewritten wholesale) plus Flow D's `gc_manage_service` signature, which had claimed a `{mode, service}` envelope and an insert/update/**delete** it did not then have. `tables/marketplace-gc.md` gained the two columns. `architecture/05-api-action-catalog.md` rewrote all three GC action rows and took a dated count-unchanged entry. `flows/notifications.md`, `tables/notifications.md` and `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md` were **checked and are genuinely unaffected** — none of them names `GC_credits_spent`, and the audit's `| Growth Credits | 2 |` row is still true because the rule was re-addressed, not added. Hub **DOC MAP: NOOP** — the gift-credits row already exists and no new flow file was created.

**Superseded hub values.** Live `vfo-admin-api` **v762 → v764**. Action count **unchanged at 464**, re-derived. Route pages **33**, re-derived. Security-advisor baseline **unchanged**, re-confirmed after the DDL.

## 2026-08-19 (3rd) — The Payment Continuation page stopped understating what it is about to charge: `/connect-card` now quotes the past-due TOTAL, and the schedule email splits past-due from upcoming

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-673071`, BOTH repos, one chat, no handoff blocks — three files, all reviewed and approved in-session.** `vfo-admin-api` v761 → **v762** (one deploy, mid-session, freshness-gated at 0 behind `origin/main` in the same invocation and explicitly approved). `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**. **No schema changes, no DML, no migrations.** Action count **unchanged at 464** — two existing handlers changed shape; nothing was added, removed or renamed. At the time this entry was written the **frontend was NOT yet published** (`vfoportal.com` still served the live-155 build), so the interim state was deliberately verified as well.

**The bug, on a real client.** `/connect-card` is the public token page a migrated client uses to save a card or bank via Stripe `mode:'setup'`. For a MAP 1 **Quarterly** row it always rendered `net_invoice / 4` labelled *"per quarterly payment"* — which is correct only for a client who is current. **Deb Moerland** (client **267**, `pipeline_map1` **138**, net **5,400**) had `pay1` and `pay2` succeeded and **`pay3` (2026-03-15) + `pay4` (2026-06-15) unpaid and past due**. The nightly `contract-chargescheduled-sweep.ts` (03:00 UTC) charges **every** past-due unpaid installment on its next run, so the night after she saved a method she would be charged **$2,700** — while the page that took her payment method had just said **$1,350**. Nothing downstream corrects that: a Stripe `mode:'setup'` session has **no line items and shows no amount at all**, so the only dollar figures the client ever sees in this flow are the ones our page and our email print.

**Two decisions, both Jake's and both explicit.** (1) **The page shows the total due now**, not one installment — it is the surface that triggers the charge, so it must state the charge. (2) **The schedule email becomes past-due-aware too, for FUTURE sends** — no resend, no backfill, no reissued tokens; already-delivered emails are left alone.

**`actions/migration/connect-load.ts` — the page mirrors the sweep, line for line.** The MAP 1 Quarterly branch now selects `pay1_status` + `pay{2,3,4}_date/_status` and reproduces the sweep's candidate filter from the same file: `pay1_status === 'succeeded'`, `payment_plan === 'Quarterly'`, N in 2–4, `payN_date <= today` (UTC date-string compare), and `payN_status` **not** in `{succeeded, processing, pending, declined, auth_required}`. When any installment qualifies, `amount` becomes their **sum**, `amount_label` becomes *"total due now"*, and the response gains **`due_now_rows: [{date, amount}]` + `due_now_count`**. Those two fields are **spread in only when non-empty**, which is the deliberate part: the no-past-due, non-Quarterly and TAX responses stay **byte-identical** to v761, so nothing else on the page could regress and an un-deployed frontend keeps working off `amount_label` alone. `declined` / `auth_required` are in the skip set because the sweep treats them as terminal and never retries them — counting them would re-open exactly the over-promise this change exists to remove.

**`utils/migration-schedule.ts` — the email splits by DATE ONLY, and promises nothing.** The `[PAYMENT_SCHEDULE]` block of both continuation templates (**172** `setup_link`, **209** `setup_link_reminder`) now renders *"Past-due payments:"* — its own table, plus a bold *"Total due now: $X"* line when there is more than one row — above the existing *"Your upcoming payments:"* intro and table, which now holds future rows only. Signature unchanged; TAX branch byte-identical.

**The review correction, and the reason it is the point of this entry.** The past-due heading **originally promised collection** ("will be collected automatically", mirroring the page). That was wrong and was softened before deploy, because the email's split is by **date**, not by collectibility, and its date-only set legitimately contains rows the sweep will **never** auto-collect: an unpaid `pay1` (the sweep requires `pay1` succeeded before it touches a row), a `declined` / `auth_required` / `pending` installment, and every non-Quarterly row. So **the email's "Total due now" can exceed the page's on the same row at the same moment, and both are correct.** Only the page mirrors the sweep, therefore **only the page is allowed to promise collection** — and a future reader who spots the two totals disagreeing must not "fix" it by widening the page or by re-adding a promise to the email. This is recorded as new gotcha **#421**, with the filter divergence spelled out in both files' comments and headers.

**`src/pages/ConnectCardPage.jsx`.** When `due_now_rows` is present the breakdown becomes **one row per installment** (*"VFO Services payment (due March 15, 2026) — $1,350.00"*), the headline stays `data.amount` (the total), and the intro becomes *"Saving your payment method is free. Once it's saved, your N past-due payment(s) totaling $X will be collected automatically."* (singular/plural handled). A new `formatDate` helper uses the same UTC formatting as the email so the dates on the two surfaces match exactly. The no-past-due render and the TAX render (`amount === null`) are unchanged.

**HOW IT WAS TESTED, and exactly where the coverage stops.** `deno check --no-lock` clean (0) after the edges; `npm run build` exit 0, 33 route pages; action count re-derived at **464**; security advisor **not re-run and not owed** — no DB, policy or function changed. The **5-pipeline smoke gate ran 5/5 PASS against v762**, the shipping version, not an earlier one. **Live click-through against v762 on Deb's real token:** **$2,700** headline on both cards, **two dated breakdown rows**, **$0.00** processing fee, the new past-due sentence; the **old-FE + new-BE interim** view was checked too and degrades honestly to a single *"total due now"* $2,700 line; and the Stripe `mode:'setup'` pages were eyeballed for **both ACH and card** (no amount shown — by design). **Nothing was completed** — the token is still unused and `done:false`. **What was NOT exercised: the email.** The `[PAYMENT_SCHEDULE]` split was proved only by a scratch Deno render of five cases (Deb's two-past-due with the total line; one past + one upcoming; upcoming-only; all-paid → empty string; TAX sentence byte-identical), so **the first real `setup_link` or `setup_link_reminder` draft is its live verification** — recorded by name in the hub's OWED list, along with the two by-design divergences (non-Quarterly rows get a past-due section in the email but keep the page's old single-amount display, since `due_now_rows` is Quarterly-only; and `declined`/`auth_required`/`pending` rows count in the email's total but never in the page's).

**Docs.** New gotcha **#421**; **#352** given a forward pointer, since its "MAP 1 is deliberately untouched on both surfaces" line is read as current guidance and no longer is. `flows/payment-method-change.md` rewritten where it said *"MAP 1's page amount is unchanged"* (now false) plus two neighbouring corrections: Step 6 now says that for a row already behind, "the next off-session charge" means **that night and every past-due installment**, and failure-mode 7's *"no automatic re-charge on update"* is qualified so it cannot be read as contradicting the page — a **failed** (`declined`) installment is not retried, an unpaid **past-due** one is collected. `NOTIFICATION_AUDIT.md`'s setup-link-reminder row updated for the split. `architecture/05-api-action-catalog.md` gained a dated entry for the `migration_connect_load` response-shape change with the count held at 464. `07-server-chains.md` and `glossary.md` were checked and are genuinely unaffected (no chain semantics, no rule keys, no template rows, no new vocabulary).

**Superseded hub values.** Live `vfo-admin-api` stamp **v761 → v762** (`boldsign-webhook` still v40, `draft-agreement-pdfs` still v1, `verify_jwt=false` on both). Action count **unchanged at 464**, re-derived. Route pages **33**, re-derived. Also corrected while in the file: `flows/payment-method-change.md`'s deployment block claimed **"Backend live v483"** and **"All pipelines currently `sandbox_mode=true`"** — the first was two months and ~280 versions stale and the second has been false since every pipeline went LIVE, so both were replaced with a derive-it instruction (#402) rather than a fresh hard-coded number.

## 2026-08-19 (2nd) — The ROI deck says "VFO Tax Planning Process", and the planner's notes now ride into the speaker notes: template v5, the 22nd token, and the first one that has ever lived outside `ppt/slides/`

**Branch `claude/roi-titles-planner-notes`, BOTH repos — but the frontend has NO code change at all.** The Notes textarea this feature consumes already shipped on 2026-08-18 with v759; everything here is backend plus the template, so `vfo-react` carries **docs only** and no `gh-pages` publish is owed. `vfo-admin-api` v760 → **v761** (one deploy, mid-session, after the template was uploaded). `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**. **No schema changes, no DML.** Action count **unchanged at 464** — this changed an existing handler, it did not add one.

**The template reached its live content in THREE stages on one day, and only the first took the versioned path.** That sequence is the most useful thing in this entry, because it is the cleanest worked example of the two-path rule (#336/#342) the bucket has ever held.

**Stage 1 — `ROI-template-master-v5.pptx`, built by the new `scripts/roi-presentation/make_v5.py` from the v4 base, uploaded BEFORE the v761 deploy.** Two edits. (i) Slides **7–13**'s two-run title `TAX` + ` Proactive Planning ` became `VFO` + ` Tax Planning Process `. Only the two `<a:t>` bodies moved: the run structure and **both `rPr` blocks survive**, so the first word keeps its `accent2` colour and the rest stays inherited. **The script matches the whole run PAIR, never the bare word** — every one of those slides also carries `<a:t> TAX PLANNING STEPS</a:t>` and slides 8–13 carry `<a:t>Proactive Facilitator Establishes</a:t>`, both of which a naive `replace("TAX","VFO")` would wreck; it asserts they survive, asserts the pair matched exactly once per slide, and asserts the exact byte-length delta. (ii) A `{{PLANNER_NOTES}}` paragraph was appended to **`ppt/notesSlides/notesSlide23.xml`** — a verbatim clone of the closing script paragraph with only the text swapped, so the planner's notes render in the same italic Inter 12pt as the line above them. **Half (i) alone would have been a hot swap** (seven token-free slides, pure wording); **the new token SITE is the entire reason v5 needed a new name and a lockstep deploy.**

**Stages 2 and 3 — two same-name HOT SWAPS on that object, both rename-first.** Stage 2 (backup **`ROI-template-master-v5-pre-trim-2026-08-19.pptx`**) removed the six-line label list from slide 23's speaker notes (*"Total Taxes - No Planning"* … *"Total Net Tax Benefit"*) and moved the existing empty spacer paragraph from **before** to **after** the *"Let's break that down…"* line, so the rendered layout is script line → blank line → planner notes. Stage 3 (backup **`ROI-template-master-v5-pre-agenda-2026-08-19.pptx`**) retitled slide 3's agenda item *"Tax Proactive Planning Process"* → *"VFO Tax Planning Process"* — a single run on a token-free slide. The bucket now holds **NINE** ROI objects and each backup is precisely the rollback for the swap it names. **`make_v5.py` reproduces STAGE 1 ONLY:** live v5 = its output plus those two swaps, which is written into the script README and into #336 so nobody rebuilds from it and quietly reverts the trim.

**Stage 2 is the one worth carrying: a hot swap INSIDE a token-bearing part is legal, but only while the token site stays byte-intact.** `notesSlide23.xml` is now a part the handler opens, patches and sweeps, so the reflex reading of the rule ("it carries a token → versioned path") would have forced a v6. It did not, because the versioned path is keyed on **whether the code's contract with the file moves**, and that contract is exactly one literal — `<a:t>{{PLANNER_NOTES}}</a:t></a:r>` plus the `<a:r>` that opens it. Stage 2 deleted six sibling paragraphs and moved a seventh without touching a byte of that run. The test to apply is therefore not *"is this part in `TOKEN_PARTS`?"* but *"does this edit move, duplicate, restyle or delete the token's own run?"* — and because that is a far finer distinction than a filename, prove it by diffing the run out of both packages.

**The handler (`actions/tax/generate-presentation.ts`).** `TEMPLATE_OBJECT` → v5. Two new constants: **`NOTES_PART`** (`ppt/notesSlides/notesSlide23.xml`, pinned by `ppt/slides/_rels/slide23.xml.rels` rather than by display position, since a rebuild can renumber notes parts independently of slides) and **`TOKEN_PARTS` = `SLIDE_PARTS` + `NOTES_PART`**. **All three uses moved onto `TOKEN_PARTS` together** — the substitution loop, the missing-part 500, and the leftover-token guard — because a part that is patched but not guarded can ship a deck with a raw `{{TOKEN}}` visible on it. The notes part is dropped in **neither** deck mode: what single-year removes are the two appendix SLIDES, and the v2 clone step left those with no notes part at all.

**`substitutePlannerNotes()` — the one token that bypasses the generic loop, because its replacement is markup.** Twenty-one tokens go through `split(token).join(xmlEscape(value))`. `PLANNER_NOTES` cannot: the notes come from a textarea, and a bare `\n` inside `<a:t>` renders as **nothing** — DrawingML's soft break is the `<a:br/>` ELEMENT, a sibling of `<a:r>`. So a two-line note has to become run / break / run, which means emitting XML the generic loop would correctly escape into visible angle brackets. The dedicated substitution runs on the notes part **before** that loop, replacing the whole `<a:r>…</a:r>` with one run per line joined by `<a:br>`, `xmlEscape`ing each line exactly as every other value is escaped and **cloning the run's own `<a:rPr>` onto every rebuilt run and break**, so nothing about the notes styling is duplicated in code. **Empty is the ordinary path, not a branch:** `"".split(/\n/)` is `[""]`, one empty invisible run — no notes, no dangling *"TAX PLANNER NOTES:"* label.

**A real bug, caught in simulation, and it is why the run is located by INDEX WALK (new gotcha #420).** The obvious pattern — `<a:r>(<a:rPr…>[\s\S]*?</a:rPr>)?<a:t>\{\{PLANNER_NOTES\}\}…` — reads as "the run containing the token" and behaves perfectly on a hand-made fixture. On the real part it **silently deleted roughly seven kilobytes of speaker notes**, because regex is **leftmost-match, not shortest-match**: the engine starts at the FIRST `<a:r>` in the part, and with the `rPr` group optional and its body lazy, `[\s\S]*?` is free to expand across every intervening paragraph until it can reach the token — which it can. Laziness only minimises the match *at a given start position*; it does nothing about which start position wins. The fix is `indexOf` the exact tail (asserted to occur **exactly once**), then `lastIndexOf("<a:r>", tailAt)` — which by construction cannot start earlier than the nearest preceding run open and cannot match `<a:rPr` either, since the `>` is part of the needle — plus a shape check that everything between them is a plain `<a:rPr>`. **It never reached production because the change was simulated against the REAL template bytes and the output size was diffed**, which is the transferable half: an assertion passing is not the same as the artifact being intact.

**HOW IT WAS TESTED, and precisely against what.** Fixture **plan 148 (test client 62)**, a **single-year** submission carrying a **two-line** note, generated against **v761** and verified through Google's `/export/pptx` **after each of the three template stages**. Final state confirmed: **eight** slides reading *"VFO Tax Planning Process"* (the seven section slides plus slide 3's agenda item), **zero** occurrences of *"Proactive Planning"* anywhere in the package, speaker notes reading script line → blank line → *"TAX PLANNER NOTES: \<line 1\>"* / break / *"\<line 2\>"* with the six-line label list gone, **27 slides**, and **zero leftover tokens**. The pipeline smoke gate ran **5/5 PASS against v761** — the shipping version, not an earlier deploy.

**What is NOT covered, and is now hub OWED.** (a) The **EMPTY-notes live path** — simulated only; no deck has been generated for a plan with no notes, so the "no label" behaviour is code-reviewed rather than seen. (b) A **TWO-YEAR (29-slide) deck against v5** — also simulated only. v5 provably did not touch slides 24/28/29 or the drop logic, so the risk is low, but no two-year deck has been generated since the bump. Both are recorded by name in the hub.

**Docs.** #336 **amended in place** (template v5, 22 tokens, `TOKEN_PARTS`, the three-stage lineage, the `substitutePlannerNotes` contract, and the hot-swap-inside-a-token-part rule) and #374 amended for the nine-part guard. The long-standing "speaker notes are the cleanest hot-swap case" claim is now qualified rather than deleted: **26 of the 27 notes parts still are; `notesSlide23.xml` is the exception.** New gotcha **#420** (markup-valued tokens cannot ride an escaping loop; leftmost-match regex traps). Bucket inventories in `architecture/03-edge-functions.md` and `integrations/supabase.md` re-derived from a live `storage ls` rather than incremented.

**Superseded hub values.** Live `vfo-admin-api` stamp **v760 → v761** (`boldsign-webhook` still v40). Action count **unchanged at 464** — re-derived, not assumed. The client-62 fixture line was rewritten again: it said **0 plans / 4 notifications**, and the live answer is **plan 148 + 5 `client_tax_progress` rows + 5 notifications**, the fifth being **1361** *"Download the ROI presentation for Test Client"* (`dismissible:false`, unread) minted by this session's own assess-form save. The Drive-deck debt grew from **ten** to **at least thirteen** (one generation per template stage; every regenerate creates a new file). `ERT_Zoom_Background.png` was **confirmed still present** by a bucket listing, at the exact path `client-tax-returns/62/340ccd1c5f481b5c_ERT_Zoom_Background.png`.

## 2026-08-19 — Four bell changes: the Download button clears its own bell, "Reached out?" clears its step's, and a PF can finally see their own client's tax vault

**Branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-43e4ac`, BOTH repos, one chat (three Opus agents + a review pass), no handoff blocks — the whole change is this session.** `vfo-admin-api` v759 → **v760** (one deploy, freshness-gated and user-approved); frontend built and **published to `gh-pages`**. `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40** and deliberately never opened. **No schema changes** — DML only (listed at the end). Action count **463 → 464**.

**The thread running through all four items: a bell is a promise that something is owed, and every one of these was leaving a bell standing after the work behind it was done.**

**1. `tax_presentation_downloaded` — the Download button retires its own bell (+1 action).** The Tax 2 bell says *"Download the ROI presentation for \<client\>"*, and until now the only things that cleared it were **scheduling the send date** (v726) and the sweep stamping `presentation_email_sent_at`. So a PF could do exactly what the bell asked — download the deck — and watch it sit there. New handler `actions/tax/presentation-downloaded.ts` (ADMIN_ONLY, dispatch + role-gates) calls the existing `clearPresentationDownloadBells`; both older clear sites stay and are idempotent with it. It **writes nothing** — no column, no email, no status — because the FE fires it **fire-and-forget alongside a synchronous `window.open`** of `generated_presentation_url` and swallows every error: a bell must never cost the PF their download. **GENERATING deliberately does not clear** — building the deck is not taking it, and it is frequently built by someone else. Guards: no `tax_plan_id` → 400, `denyIfNotPlannerPlan`, unknown plan → 404, NULL `generated_presentation_at` → 400 (nothing could have been downloaded, so the bell is genuinely still owed). Not added to `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS`: the planner portal locks that whole step via `plannerMode`.

**2. The planner-vault-drop FYI now also reaches the client's assigned PF.** `utils/vault-planner-notify.ts` went to Tracy alone; Tracy owns the vault but the PF runs the engagement, and every drop was being relayed by hand. `assigned_pf` rides along on the `clients` name lookup the function already did — one row, one round-trip, **server-side, never from `body`** — and resolves through **`taxPfLoginEmail`** (the PORTAL LOGIN address, not the `pf-emails.ts` correspondence map). A null/unmapped PF leaves **Tracy alone**, i.e. exactly the old list, and never throws. `Set`-deduped, plus `dynamic: { ASSIGNED_PF }` so a rule-level override can actually resolve (#324/#413 — the token is dropped silently otherwise).

**3. Assigned-PF tax-vault access — VIEW-ONLY, via one shared predicate.** New async `canViewClientTaxVault(sb, email, clientId)` in `constants/tax-access.ts` = `isTaxAdmin` **OR** the admin who is *that one client's* assigned PF (case-insensitive, fails closed). **Both** `vault_tax_list`'s `can_view` and `vault_tax_download` call it, so the flag and the download cannot drift apart — the failure mode where a UI offers a button the handler refuses. **Upload / delete / share are untouched**, still the 4-person `isTaxAdmin` or an in-group planner, and `vault_tax_list` now returns that narrower answer as a **second flag `can_manage`** (literally the pre-carve-out `can_view` expression). `ClientVaultTab.jsx` splits `canManage`→View from `canWrite`→Add/Delete/Share on the ERT seam. **`can_manage` fails closed on a stale backend**, which turns an ordinary two-repo change into a hard **backend-before-frontend deploy order** — ship the FE first and the four tax admins silently lose Add/Delete/Share everywhere, with no error (new gotcha **#417**). This widens a read path behind a *named server-side predicate*; **no security invariant moves.**

**4. `automation_stall_ack` rewritten — ticking "Reached out?" clears the step's bells, and the sweeps stop fighting it.** The ack column was inert on both sides: nothing read it, so the nightly sweep re-minted straight over a ticked box, and the bell the admin had just acted on stayed unread. Now, on all seven pipelines, `ack !== false` marks read **every** unread bell of that step — **regardless of `dismissible`**, making this the first clearer that retires FYI and action-required rows alike. Title suffixes are **byte-copied from the insert sites**, plus `extraTitles` for the extra-meeting bells (MAP 1 `c14` always; advisor/accountant only when the row's `extra_meeting_stage` matches the stall being acked; TAX `tax_decision` clears the `(tax)` variant). Scoping: `pipeline + client_id` for client pipelines, **END-anchored** `link LIKE '%onboarding=<id>'` for advisor/accountant/specialist (those bells carry `client_id NULL`), with TAX further narrowed by `'%program=<program_id>'` and REGULAR by the priority name quoted in the message — one client can hold several plans or tracks minting identical titles. Fail-soft throughout; response gains `bells_cleared`; **unchecking is one-way** (nulls the column, restores nothing). The matching half: **all 7 sweeps** (`pipeline/contract-revshare-sweep`, `tax/revshare-sweep`, `advisor/sweep`, `accountant/sweep`, `onboarding/sweep`, `pft/sweep`, `regular/map4-followup-sweep`) gained `.is("<stall>_pf_ack_at", null)`, so the ack is a real satisfied-on-fire guard (#365) rather than a note.

**Why the two extra-meeting titles cannot share a pattern (new gotcha #418).** MAP 1 / advisor / accountant end in `requested extra meeting`; TAX ends in `requested extra meeting (tax)`. A naive `'%requested extra meeting%'` matches both, so a MAP 1 acknowledgement would retire a live tax bell for the same client. Each literal is listed separately and the un-suffixed one is END-anchored. **The suffix is the discriminator that keeps two same-client asks independently clearable** — the concrete instance of #407.

**Frontend, beyond the two contract changes.** `PFTEngagementTrack.jsx` gained the **missing discovery "Reached out?" checkbox** — `<stall>` ∈ discovery/ft/decision had been true of the backend whitelist since v734 while `DiscoveryViewer` rendered no escalation row at all, so the docs had been describing the intended set, not the built one. `RegularPrioritiesTab.jsx` got a `useEffect` re-sync its copy was missing (`useState` seeds once on mount, so the box kept a stale value after the parent reloaded tracks).

**HOW IT WAS TESTED — the before/after bell-flip method, and what it does NOT cover.** Live rows were read by SQL, exercised through the UI, then re-read: **bell 1251** (`Download the ROI presentation`) was confirmed unread, **Regenerate** was clicked and it stayed unread (proving generation does not clear), then **Download** cleared it. For the stall-ack, bells **708 + 824** (Emma Friend, MAP 1 `c14`) were deliberately flipped back to unread to re-arm the test: **unticking cleared nothing**, and a single retick **dual-cleared both** — including the month-old `dismissible:false` extra-meeting bell, which is the case the whole `extraTitles` mechanism exists for. The planner-drop widening minted **2 rows, Tracy + Jake**, as designed. **What that leaves untested is the majority of the surface**, and it is now hub OWED: **item 3 has never been seen on a real PF session** (code review + DB mapping only — Evan is owed an eyeball); **six of the seven stall pipelines were never clicked** — TAX (incl. the `(tax)` coupling and the `%program` narrow), advisor/accountant (stage-matched coupling + the onboarding link scope), specialist, and regular, which has **no live target rows at all**; and the **refire guards cannot be verified until the first cron run after 2026-08-19**.

**Flagged, not built.** `pft/meeting-email.ts:~90` still **nulls `discovery_pf_notified_at`** on a non-`reschedule` send — the new guard stops the re-mint over an ack, but the null-out erases the row the checkbox hangs on. `advisor/extra-meeting.ts` + `accountant/extra-meeting.ts` still match on an **un-anchored** `'%onboarding=<id>%'` link (5 matches 51) — pre-existing, deliberately left alone, so anchored and un-anchored matching now coexist in the same feature.

**DB side effects (DML only, no DDL).** Backfill marked read: notifications **1251**, **708**, **821**; **708/824** were re-flipped for the live test and ended **read**. Test drop bells **1359/1360** marked read. Fixture plan **147** created then **deleted**.

**Gate results, all against v760 (the deployed tree).** `deno check --no-lock` clean · action count **6 + 458 = 464** · `npm run build` exit 0, **33 route pages** · security advisor at the documented baseline (5× `rls_enabled_no_policy` INFO + the `pg_net` WARN, nothing else) — **no schema changes, so no invariant moved** · **pipeline smoke gate 5/5, run by the user against v760**.

**OWED discharged from the hub by this entry.** The 2026-08-18 Client Overview line carried *"the smoke gate's 5/5 was run against the FIRST of that session's three backend deploys, so no run exists against the shipping version — re-run it"* — **discharged**: 5/5 against v760 today. The client-62 fixture line's claim that the two permanently-stuck bells were gone was **re-verified by SQL** (no `%HLM%`, no `Complete Client decision 2%`, no `Download the ROI presentation%` row on client 62; plans = 0) and the line was rewritten, because the *other* half of it was wrong: the client is **not** at zero notifications. Four rows exist, and **1347/1348** (*"Test Client hasn't set up their payment method"*, both `2026-08-19 04:00Z`, one still unread) are **cron-minted after the wipe** — so "clean" on this fixture means *no plan rows*, never *no bells*. Still owed by hand: the ten Drive decks, and `ERT_Zoom_Background.png` in client 62's Sensitive vault (UI/Storage API only — #206 blocks SQL).

## 2026-08-18 (2nd) — The two-year ROI deck comes back, and the template that restored it has no content delta

**Branch `claude/roi-two-year-return`, BOTH repos, one chat, no prior handoff — the whole change is this session.** `vfo-admin-api` v758 → **v759** (one deploy, freshness-gated and user-approved). **Note the base: v758, not v751** — other sessions shipped in between, and the hub's version line was stale by seven revisions before this one re-derived it. `boldsign-webhook` **untouched at v40**; no migrations, no DML, no policy changes. Frontend built clean but **NOT deployed in this session**. Template **`ROI-template-master-v4.pptx`** uploaded to the `presentation-templates` bucket by the user **BEFORE** the v759 deploy — the versioned-object path, as the rule requires (#336/#342) — taking the bucket to **SIX objects** (v1, v2, v3, the two dated 2026-08-17 hot-swap backups, and v4).

**The problem it solves.** On 2026-08-17 the assess form collapsed to four flat totals and the ROI deck went *unconditionally* single-year — 27 slides, both year-appendix slides dropped on every generation, and slide 24's year header deleted from the master outright so the deck carried no year anywhere. That was right for a one-year engagement and wrong for the ones that actually run two years: a planner with a genuine two-year plan had nowhere to put year 2's numbers and no deck that showed them. This session gives the form an **optional Year 2** (and an optional **Notes** box) and lets the deck's shape follow the data instead of a constant.

**1. The stored shape gains an optional group — and a deliberate asymmetry.** `client_tax_plans.assess_form` is now `{ fee, taxes_without_plan, taxes_with_plan, cash_outlay, year2?: { taxes_without_plan, taxes_with_plan, cash_outlay }, notes?: string }`. **`year2` carries THREE fields, not four: there is no `year2.fee`.** The VFO Services Tax Planning Fee is a single **engagement-level** figure entered once and attributed entirely to year 1 — which is the deck's original design and the reason slide 29's One-Time Fee has always been the literal `$0` template text rather than a token. Both optional keys are written only when they have content, so clearing either drops it from storage.

**A per-year fee was designed, built, and REVERTED inside the same session, on user direction.** The first cut split the fee across years with `{{PLANNING_FEE_Y1}}` / `{{PLANNING_FEE_Y2}}` token sites; the user's ruling that the fee is one engagement-level number undid it. `scripts/roi-presentation/make_v4.py` now carries a **tripwire assert** that neither token exists anywhere in the master — the reverted design's permanent guard against coming back by accident.

**2. The deploy was WINDOWLESS, and that was designed rather than lucky.** The year-1 keys did not move: they stay flat and unchanged, `year2`/`notes` are purely additive. So every pre-existing four-key row is already a valid *current* single-year row needing no re-save and no backfill, **and the OLD deployed frontend's four-key payload still validates and still stores against the NEW handler**. Unlike the 2026-08-17 four-total ship, there was no interval in which either side rejected the other — which is also why the frontend not being deployed yet is safe. The corollary recorded in #306: this did **not** create a fourth historical shape. There are still three (current / strategy-list / legacy `question_1`), because **the flat four-key row IS the current single-year shape**.

**3. The deck is 27 or 29 slides again, and `year2`'s mere presence is the whole condition.** Absent → single-year, 27 slides, both appendix slides dropped. Present → two-year, 29 slides, nothing dropped, slide 24 reading *"Your investment: 2026 + 2027"*, the full fee plus its two `FEE_HALF` halves on the 2026 slide and a literal `$0` on the 2027 slide. The v3-era condition — a per-strategy `singleYear` test over year-2 amounts — is **not** what came back, and #374 now records why: a test computed from *amounts* can be fooled by offsetting entries that sum to zero, so the new test asks about the **presence of a group** instead. Combined figures are the **sums of the per-year figures**, computed from them so the two can never drift, and three identities hold by construction: `NET_Y1+NET_Y2 === NET_BENEFIT`, `GROSS_Y1+GROSS_Y2 === GROSS_BENEFIT`, `INVEST_Y1+INVEST_Y2 === CASH_OUTLAY`.

**4. The single-year layout INVERTED — from a static template edit to generation-time surgery.** Yesterday the master had the year header deleted and the twelve shapes below it shifted up; today template v4 **carries** the header (a two-year deck needs it) and the handler reproduces the old layout on the fly. `dropInvestYearsHeader()` deletes the one `<p:sp>` containing `{{INVEST_YEARS}}` and shifts every remaining `<p:sp>` with `x < 4800000` and `y >= 1773000` up by **539650 EMU**, asserting exactly **1** deletion and exactly **12** shifts. It runs on the raw XML **before** substitution, because the shape is found by the literal token substitution is about to erase. The constants were measured off v4 and **byte-verified to reproduce the old live master's `slide24.xml` exactly** — and they are **coupled to v4**, so a template rebuild must re-derive them. The whole block, appendix drops included, sits behind one `if (!twoYear)`.

**5. v4 is byte-identical to a file already in the bucket — and that is the interesting part.** `ROI-template-master-v4.pptx` **has no content delta at all**: it is `ROI-template-master-v3-pre-shift-2026-08-17.pptx` under a new key (SHA256 `319593587028fdad36429e3349819ddb132707462676a3722d8cfc54e8d1385b`, 27,614,869 bytes, same 570 entries / 29 slides / 27 notes parts / **21 tokens**). It got a new version anyway, because **the versioned-object rule is keyed on the delta against the object the LIVE FUNCTION READS, not against your build artifact.** The live `…-v3.pptx` had been hot-swapped to *delete* slide 24's `{{INVEST_YEARS}}` header, so restoring it is a token-**site addition** relative to what production was actually reading — the versioned path, upload-before-deploy, v3 retained as the rollback. The new committed `make_v4.py` is a **verifier, not an editor**: it checks the base's SHA256 before stamping a new name on unknown bytes, asserts the package shape and the token inventory, refuses a base cut from the post-shift object, and then `shutil.copyfile`s rather than repacking — deliberately, so the property that makes the version trivially auditable survives.

**6. Validation is ten messages in strict FE/BE lockstep, em dash and all.** In order: *"VFO Services Tax Planning Fee is required"* (validated first, **suffix-free** — the suffix it briefly carried under the per-year-fee design came back off when the fee went engagement-level), the three `— Year 1` required messages plus *"Total Tax with the Plan must be less than Total Tax without the Plan — Year 1"*, the identical four with `— Year 2` **only when some year-2 field is non-blank**, then *"Notes must be 5000 characters or fewer"*. **All three year-2 fields blank means the group is ABSENT, never invalid** — ticking "Add Year 2" and leaving it empty must not block a save, and both sides apply that test identically. The suffixes are U+2014 em dashes on both sides. Generator and FE gate additionally share *"Re-save the Assess form — it uses the old strategy format"* and the new *"Re-save the Assess form — the Year 2 totals are incomplete"*, the FE mirroring both failure modes in the generator's order so the button never fires a call that can only come back as an error.

**7. The form, and the toggle that doubles as the delete affordance.** Fee on top alone (no suffix) → a **Year 1** section with all three inputs on **one row** (3-column grid, labels given a fixed 28px min-height so boxes stay aligned when a label wraps) → an **"Add Year 2"** checkbox → the Year 2 section in the same 3-column layout → a Notes textarea (4 rows, `maxLength` 5000). Toggling Year 2 **off excludes the group from the payload**, and since the save handler rebuilds the whole jsonb rather than merging, **that is also how an existing year-2 group is removed** — no separate delete path was needed or added. Typed values survive in component state while the toggle is off, so a mis-click destroys nothing. The read-only view's branch 3 renders the fee, both groups, the summary and the notes; the two legacy branches are untouched. The summary line has two shapes — the old single-year string when there is no usable year-2 group, and a per-year-plus-combined string when there is, using the backend's own construction so it can never disagree with the deck.

**Tested against the shipping version (v759 + template v4), by the owner.** Smoke gate **5/5 vs v759**. A fresh **single-year** submission on fixture plan 146 (Test Client 62) stored the four flat keys only and produced a **27-slide** deck verified through `/export/pptx` — 100k/60k/15k/5k in, 40k gross / 20k net / 40% out, no year line anywhere. A **year-2 + notes** save stored the asymmetric shape (SQL-verified) and produced a **29-slide** deck — 180k/110k/70k/25k/5k in, 40k net / 39%, header *"Your investment: 2026 + 2027"*, the 2026 slide carrying the 5,000 fee and its two 2,500 halves, the 2027 slide a literal `$0`, and all three identities holding. **Toggling "Add Year 2" back OFF on that saved two-year row** dropped `year2` from storage entirely while `fee`, the year-1 keys and `notes` survived the re-save, and the regenerated deck came back at **27 slides** with no year line, no 2027 and correct single-year numbers. One year-2 required message was confirmed firing instantly client-side, and the 3-column layout was eyeballed by the owner. **Not tested:** the generator's 400 on a hand-corrupted `year2` group, and the notes 5000-character cap — both minor, both code-reviewed with their FE mirrors in place, both carried to the hub as OWED.

**Fixture debt reconciled rather than carried.** The hub's standing "Test Client 62" entry was stale: **plans 136 and 138 were deleted** during 2026-08-18 testing and that part is now **discharged**. What actually remains was re-queried this session — plan **145** (`stopped`, 4 progress rows, 1 `client_tax_specialists` row) and the new fixture plan **146** (`live`, 5 progress rows, assess form submitted and a deck generated), **64** TAX notifications on the client of which **3** are unread action-required (two permanently stuck on deleted plans; the third, *"Download the ROI presentation…"*, belongs to plan 146 and clears normally), and **TEN** test decks in the Drive *"ROI Presentations"* folder (7 dated 08-17, 3 dated 08-18) needing hand deletion.

**Superseded hub values moved here:** live `vfo-admin-api` **v758 → v759**; the bucket's **five objects → six**; the template the function reads, **`ROI-template-master-v3.pptx` → `ROI-template-master-v4.pptx`**; and the 2026-08-17 statements that the deck is *"27 slides, always"*, that *"no year appears anywhere on a generated deck"*, and that `INVEST_YEARS` is *"computed but dead / has no site"* — all three now describe the **single-year branch only** and are retained above as history.
