- **Chrome had been covering the admin's own search results with a Google-Wallet “Manage loyalty cards…” dropdown, and the fix everybody reaches for first — `autocomplete="off"` — DOES NOT WORK on wallet-backed autofill; what actually stopped it was reclassifying the boxes as SEARCH fields AND deleting the phrase “member number” from the placeholder copy. Alongside it, a long file name in any vault row stopped shoving the View/Share/Delete buttons out past the card border** (2026-08-07, the **FOURTH** session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-e083e9` — **react ONLY: 19 files under `src/` plus docs; the EDGE worktree carries a ZERO-file diff and `git status` there is empty**. **+0 actions (457)** — no backend file was opened, so `router/dispatch.ts`, `constants/role-gates.ts`, `index.ts`, `middleware/auth.ts` and `router/webhooks.ts` were never touched; parity re-counted anyway at audit (6 + 451). **NO DEPLOY OF ANY KIND this session** — `vfo-admin-api` stays **v713**, `boldsign-webhook` stays **v40**, both re-verified ACTIVE via MCP at audit. **ZERO DB CHANGES — no migration, no DDL, no DML**, so the security advisor was correctly **NOT** run. `deno check` **NOT re-run** (backend untouched — the carried-forward 0 is not a fresh verification). **`npx vite build` exit 0**, 556 modules. Gotcha **#343**, ALWAYS-APPLIES (Frontend). **`npm run deploy` is OWED for this session's 19 react files.** **MERGE-PENDING (react repo only).**)
  - **THE ATTRIBUTES ALONE DID NOT FIX IT, AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF #343.** Round 1 did the textbook thing — `type="search" name="search" autoComplete="off"` on every admin search box — shipped it, and the user retested: **the “Manage loyalty cards…” dropdown was still there.** Chrome's Google-Wallet loyalty-card autofill is not the generic autofill it looks like; it **ignores `autocomplete="off"`** (Chrome has long treated that attribute as advisory for its own wallet surfaces) and it classifies a field by **regex over the placeholder and label text**. The trigger sitting in this portal was the literal phrase **“member number”** — plus “member #” and “or member” — in placeholders written for humans years before anyone thought about Chrome. Round 2 rewrote that copy and the popup went away. **Keep BOTH halves: the attributes reclassify the field, the wording keeps it out of the heuristic's net, and dropping either one reopens the bug.**
  - **WHAT CHANGED, EXACTLY.** **19 inputs across 14 files** got the three attributes: `MembersPanel.jsx` (5), `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx` (2), and one each in `MemberOverviewPanel`, `ClientOverviewPanel`, `SpecialistsPanel`, `TaxPlannersPanel`, `SpecialistPaymentInput`, `MSMTracking`, `NewModelSaleModal`, `tax-planner/PlannerClientsList`, `shared/MemberCIQ`, `shared/MemberWebsitePlugin`, `member/MemberShowroom` and `pages/MemberPortal`. **7 placeholders were reworded** — “Search by name or member number…” → “…or number…” (`MembersPanel`, `MemberOverviewPanel`), “…ref, member #, or member name…” → “…ref, number, or name…” (`ClientOverviewPanel`), “Search name or member number…” → “…or number…” (`MembershipFeesPanel`), “…name or member type…” → “…name or type…” (`TaxPlannersPanel`), “…ref, or member…” → “…ref, or name…” (`PlannerClientsList`), and “Type a name or member # — leave blank for n/a” → “Type a name or number — …” (`NewModelSaleModal`). **`NewModelSaleModal` was found by the closing grep, not by the original sweep** — it had the strongest trigger in the codebase (“member #”) and had been missed entirely; the audit grep `placeholder="[^"]*[Mm]ember` is what caught it and is the check to re-run. **`src/index.css` gained a two-part reset** — `input[type="search"] { appearance: none }` on the element **plus** `::-webkit-search-cancel-button` / `::-webkit-search-decoration` → `appearance: none` on the pseudo-elements — so `type="search"` renders **byte-identically to `type="text"`** — without it every box would sprout a WebKit clear-X. **Search BEHAVIOUR is unchanged everywhere:** every one of these inputs is a controlled React field whose `value`/`onChange` were left exactly as they were.
  - **THE VAULT ROW BUG WAS `min-width: auto`, THE FLEXBOX DEFAULT NOBODY REMEMBERS.** A document row is a flex line — icon, file name, size, then View / Share / Delete. The name span carried `flex: 1` but **no `minWidth: 0`**, and a flex item's default `min-width: auto` means an unbreakable string **refuses to shrink below its own content width**, so a long file name grew the row and pushed the buttons straight out past the card border. Fixed in **5 row markups across 4 files** — `admin/ClientVaultTab.jsx` (the one markup all three sections render through), `shared/VaultSections.jsx`, `admin/SpecialistOnboarding.jsx` (2 rows) and `pages/SpecialistDdcPage.jsx` — by giving the name `minWidth: 0` + `overflow:hidden` + `textOverflow:ellipsis` + `whiteSpace:nowrap` and a **`title={f.name}` tooltip** so the full name is still reachable on hover, and pinning every trailing control with **`flexShrink: 0`**. Two of them were not the expected shape and were brought INTO it deliberately: **`SpecialistOnboarding`'s two file lists were plain block `div`s**, not flex rows, so they were converted (`display:flex`) — and the size separator moved from a text-node `‘ · ’` to a real `gap`, because a leading space collapses inside a flex container. **`SpecialistDdcPage`'s `fileChip` was already 90% right** (ellipsis on the span, `flexShrink:0` on the shared `removeBtn` const) and only needed `flex:1` + `minWidth:0` + the tooltip; its shared style constants were left alone.

Root cause: **client 119 is DUAL-ENROLLED** — program 4 (VFO Tax Planning, plan 90) and program 1 (VFO Holistic Planning, plan 99) — and `automation_TAX_readyfortax3` was clicked **once from each program view** (20:42 and 20:45 UTC). The handler is **per-plan and has no cross-plan awareness**, so two legitimate clicks on two legitimate plans produced two legitimate drafts. The user was shown the options and **chose Option 1: accept it and delete the extra draft by hand.** No dedupe, no cross-plan guard, no code change — recorded here so the next person who sees double drafts recognises it instead of re-diagnosing it. Note the general shape, which keeps recurring in the tax track: **on a dual-enrolled client, any per-plan action is a per-plan action** (same family as #340's dual-candidate stamping and #339's per-program mirrors).

  - **WHAT THE DECK NOW SAYS, SLIDE BY SLIDE.** **Slide 24 is unchanged in its numbers and changed in its claims:** the header becomes `Your investment – {{YEAR}} + {{YEAR2}}` (box widened to **4.70in** with `wrap="none"` so it can never wrap onto a second line), and the year was **REMOVED** from the "Estimated Tax Savings" / "Net Tax Savings" / "Plan Investment" labels, because every value on that slide is and always was the **COMBINED** two-year figure — the old single-year labels were simply lying about what sat next to them. **The two new slides are the breakout.** The **year-1** slide shows Σ `gross_y1`, the same fee block as slide 24, `{{YEAR}}` Plan Investment = Σ `invest_y1`, and Net = `gross_y1 − invest_y1 − the FULL fee`. The **year-2** slide shows Σ `gross_y2`, a One-Time Fee of literal **"$0"** (**template text, NOT a token** — do not go hunting for a `PLANNING_FEE_Y2`), Σ `invest_y2`, and Net = `gross_y2 − invest_y2` with no fee at all. Neither year slide carries the percentage-reduced box; that stays a combined-view claim.
  - **THE FEE ATTRIBUTION IS THE ARITHMETIC OF RECORD, AND IT IS A CHECKABLE IDENTITY.** The one-time planning fee is charged **entirely to year 1**, which is what makes the three slides agree: **`NET_Y1 + NET_Y2 === NET_BENEFIT`**, and likewise `GROSS_Y1 + GROSS_Y2 === GROSS_BENEFIT` and `INVEST_Y1 + INVEST_Y2 === CASH_OUTLAY`. The handler now **DERIVES** the combined `GROSS_BENEFIT` / `CASH_OUTLAY` **from the per-year sums** rather than reading them independently — deliberately, so the two views cannot drift apart no matter what the strategy rows contain. A real consequence to expect rather than treat as a bug: **`NET_Y1` can go NEGATIVE** on a year-1-light plan that still carries the whole fee, which is why the TS `money()` renders negatives accounting-style as `(12,345)`.
  - **THE VERSIONED BUCKET OBJECT IS A DEPLOY-SAFETY MECHANISM, NOT A NAMING PREFERENCE.** `TEMPLATE_OBJECT` became **`"ROI-template-master-v2.pptx"`** and `SLIDE_PARTS` became `[1, 20, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29]`, with **7 new tokens** (`YEAR2`, `GROSS_Y1/Y2`, `INVEST_Y1/Y2`, `NET_Y1/Y2`) taking the deck to **20**, every one whole-dollar — **`FEE_HALF` remains the ONLY cents-tolerant token**. Because the object was given a NEW NAME instead of being overwritten, there was a **zero-breakage window**: the still-live v1 function kept reading `ROI-template-master.pptx` right up to the moment v713 went live, and that v1 object is **deliberately retained in the bucket as the rollback**. Overwriting in place would have broken every generation between the upload and the deploy.
  - **THE APPENDIX SLIDES' FILENAMES ARE NOT THEIR POSITIONS, AND THIS IS THE TRAP A FUTURE READER WILL FALL INTO.** The new parts are `ppt/slides/slide28.xml` and `slide29.xml`, but they **DISPLAY at positions 25 and 26** — `<p:sldIdLst>` orders them `1–24, 28, 29, 25, 26, 27`, which pushes the old "Choose Who You Pay" / Double-Guarantee / Congratulations slides out to display **27/28/29**. The edge function addresses parts **by filename**, so `SLIDE_PARTS` is correct as written and must **NOT** be "fixed" to the display numbers. Anyone touching `sldIdLst` or `SLIDE_PARTS` has to hold both numbering systems in their head at once (see #336).
  - **THE RESTYLE ROUNDS SHIPPED WITH NO DEPLOY AND NO CODE — AND THAT IS THE REUSABLE PROPERTY, NOT A SHORTCUT.** After v713 the session did several rounds of pure appearance work on **token-free** slides: slide 2 (Disclaimer) restyled to the deck's standard 37pt `125ECC` Inter title over one rounded `EFF8FF` panel of 18pt centred text; slide 3 (Overview) restyled **twice**, ending as **six evenly spaced bullet items with NO tinted chips** (the chips were an intermediate that the second round removed); and **ONE canonical blue bullet spec** (`buClr 125ECC`, `buSzPct 80000`, Inter, `U+25CF`) applied **byte-identically** across display slides **3, 4 and 28** (files `slide3` / `slide4` / **`slide26`** — the same filename-vs-display trap again). Because none of those slides carries a token and neither the slide count nor any part filename moved, every round shipped by **REPLACING THE SAME BUCKET OBJECT** — no code change, no deploy, no version bump, picked up on the very next generation. **The rule that comes out of it:** token-free slide changes hot-swap the same object; any change to a token, the slide count, a part filename or `sldIdLst` requires a **NEW versioned object name plus a lockstep backend deploy**. One incidental finding of record: **slide 4's bullets had been BLACK at 150%**, not blue as everyone believed — the canonical spec was applied anyway, deliberately, as the chosen end state.
  - **THE TEMPLATE LINEAGE IS NOW FOUR SCRIPTS AND IT IS WRITTEN DOWN.** `scripts/roi-presentation/` in the edge repo gained **`restyle_23.py`** and **`restyle_bullets.py`**, extending the chain to `roi-template.pptx → build_master.py → v1 → clone step → edit_v2.py → revise_v2.py → v2 → restyle_23.py → restyle_bullets.py → the current bucket object`. Its README carries the HOT-SWAP RULE table and a **mandatory** restyle step in the maintenance cycle — a fresh Google Slides export carries the OLD styling, so a rebuild that skips the restyle scripts silently reverts the look while still generating perfectly correct numbers. Both scripts assert word-identity per slide and die loudly on any moved index; none of them is production code.

  - **WHAT THE BUTTON ACTUALLY DOES, END TO END.** `tax_generate_presentation` (`actions/tax/generate-presentation.ts`) reads the plan, its `assess_form` and the plan-level risk grade, pulls the tokenized master **`ROI-template-master.pptx`** out of the new private **`presentation-templates`** bucket, substitutes **13 `{{TOKENS}}`** across slides **1 / 20 / 23 / 24 / 25 / 27** (every value XML-escaped before it goes near the slide XML), **repositions the slide-20 `upArrow`** to the client’s risk band off a hardcoded EMU table (1→801612, 2→2566499, 3→4349395, 4→6126289, 5→7900180 — the numbers came from measuring the chevron strip PNG, they are not guesses), then uploads the result to **Google Drive multipart with metadata `mimeType='application/vnd.google-apps.presentation'`**, which is what makes Drive **convert it server-side into a real Google Slides file** rather than parking a .pptx. It lands in an **“ROI Presentations”** folder under `GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID`, gets sharing **role=writer type=anyone**, and the handler stamps `client_tax_plans.generated_presentation_{drive_id,url,at,by}` and returns `{success, url, generated_at}`. **The formulas are fixed and worth having written down:** `gross = Σ(gross_y1+gross_y2)`; `invest = Σ(invest_y1+invest_y2)`; `taxes_with = taxes_without − gross`; `net = gross − invest − fee`; `outlay_plus_fee = invest + fee`; `fee_half = fee/2`; `pct = round(gross/taxes_without × 100)`; `year` = the **current calendar year at generation time**. Money renders whole-dollar with commas (`fee_half` drops to 2 dp only when it is genuinely fractional) and negatives use accounting parentheses. The risk grade is the **plan-level** `client_tax_progress` row (`tax_specialist_id IS NULL`) for the task “Client risk profile complete”, parsed `/Risk\s*([1-5])/`.
  - **THE ZIP WORK IS THE PERFORMANCE STORY, AND IT INTRODUCED THE FIRST ZIP LIBRARY THIS CODEBASE HAS EVER HAD.** A .pptx is a zip, and this one is **27.6 MB — almost entirely PNGs**. The handler uses **fflate** (`https://esm.sh/fflate@0.8.2`), and the pattern that makes it viable is: **re-store every untouched entry at level 0 and deflate ONLY the 6 edited slide XMLs**. Recompressing the whole archive would burn most of a minute on image data that did not change. That is also why `src/lib/api.js` gained a **`LONG_TIMEOUT_ACTIONS` map** giving this one action **90s** instead of the default — generation runs ~30–60s in practice. **The #30 rule was left completely intact: writes still never retry**; only the timeout is per-action.
  - **`taxes_without_plan` IS A NEW REQUIRED FIELD, VALIDATED IN LOCKSTEP IN TWO PLACES, AND IT REWRITES THE STORED SHAPE.** `client_tax_plans.assess_form` jsonb is now `{ fee, taxes_without_plan, strategies:[…] }` — and because `tax_save_assess_form` **REBUILDS the whole jsonb on every submit** (it never merged, #306/#314), a re-save is what upgrades an old row. The requirement is enforced by `actions/tax/save-assess-form.ts` **and** by `AssessTaxForm` inside `TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx` with the **identical message** — *“Total Taxes without a Tax Plan is required”* — so the pair must move together or the two halves disagree. The generator adds two of its own 400s on top: **≤ 0** → *“Total Taxes without a Tax Plan must be greater than zero”* (it is a divisor), and a **legacy submission that predates the field** → *“Re-save the Assess form — it was submitted before the Total Taxes field existed”*, which tells the admin exactly what to do rather than failing opaquely.
  - **THE STEP’S DONE-STATE IS A COLUMN, NOT A PROGRESS ROW — THAT IS DELIBERATE AND IT IS THE THING A FUTURE READER WILL GET WRONG.** New `program_client_tasks` rows **173** (program 1 Holistic) / **174** (program 4 VFO Tax Planning), both named **“Generate and download presentation”**, `task_order=2` in **“Tax 2 - Deeper Dive”**, sentinel `status_options='tax_generate_presentation'`; ids **90/124** were renumbered to `task_order=3` and **168/169** to **4** to make room. Anything that later counts “completed steps” from progress rows alone will under-count this one.
  - **DESIGN DECISIONS OF RECORD — all made explicitly, several after being argued.** (1) **Sharing is anyone-with-link WRITER**, chosen over view-only *after* a security review surfaced the tradeoff, and approved by the user — it is a decision, not an oversight, and reversing it is a product call rather than a bug fix. (4) **Download opens the Slides URL** — there is no local file hand-off. (5) **Regenerate creates a NEW Drive file every time** and the plan row points at the newest; old files are not deleted. (6) **`year` is generation-time**, so regenerating in January changes it. Gotchas **#332** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, money) **+ #333** (ALWAYS-APPLIES) **+ #334**. **All three features were live-tested end to end by the user against v700/v702; the pipeline smoke gate was run by the user vs v700 — 5/5 PASS.** **The FRONTEND IS NOT DEPLOYED — `npm run deploy` is owed.** **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **THE HONEST FINDING CAME BEFORE THE FEATURE: MEMBERSHIP RENEWAL WAS COMPLETELY SILENT.** The research half of this session established that nothing anywhere warned a member that their membership was about to renew. The sweep rolled the plan into its next year the moment `renewal_date` arrived — new ledger, next-year terms applied, charging resumed — and `auto_renew` is `true` by default on every plan. **A member's first signal that they had been committed to another year was the charge on their statement.** That is what pass 0 closes, and it is worth recording that the gap was nine months old and had never been framed as one.
  - **THE IDEMPOTENCY STAMP IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART OF THE NOTICE PASS, AND ITS ORDERING IS DELIBERATE (#333).** `sweep.ts` gained a **pass 0** that runs BEFORE the renewal pass, so a plan is always warned before it is rolled over. Window: `status='active'` + `auto_renew` + `renewal_date` in `(today, today+30]` — **strictly future**, so a plan that actually reaches its 15th is renewed by pass 1 rather than noticed. The "already noticed" test is `renewal_notice_for <> renewal_date` and is evaluated **in JS**, because PostgREST cannot compare two columns and NULL has to read as not-noticed. The new `member_payment_plans.renewal_notice_for` is written **ONLY after the Gmail draft actually succeeds** — a missing template, a token refresh failure or a member with no email simply leaves it alone and retries tomorrow. Stamping first would have turned every transient Gmail hiccup into a permanently skipped notice. Because the predicate is an inequality, the pass also **re-arms automatically whenever the renewal date moves** — including after a pause. The durable `renewal_meeting_token` (partial-unique) is minted once per plan, reused by every subsequent notice, and **persisted BEFORE the email is drafted** so a link that goes out always resolves. `summary.noticed` joins the sweep's counters.
  - **`[Renewal Terms]` IS THE RENEWAL PASS'S OWN ARITHMETIC WRITTEN A SECOND TIME, AND A MISMATCH WAS CAUGHT IN REVIEW.** The notice quotes `(next_year_amount ?? annual_amount) − (next_year_credit_note ?? 0)` — **exactly** what pass 1 will bill. An earlier draft computed it differently; that was found during adversarial review of the money path and fixed before the deploy. **Quoting a member a renewal price the system then does not charge is the worst failure this feature has available to it**, so the two copies are now explicitly noted as having to move together.
  - **THE MEETING REQUEST IS A ONE-BIT PUBLIC ENDPOINT AND THE BELL HAS EXACTLY ONE EXIT.** NEW `actions/membership/renewal-meeting-request.ts` (`membership_renewal_meeting_request`, **PUBLIC**, in `PUBLIC_HANDLERS` with a comment) is credentialed **entirely** by `renewal_meeting_token` and returns a **bare `{ success }` that must never be widened** — the same reasoning as #331, stated in a file comment. It is **idempotent per `(plan_id, renewal_date_for)` open row**, so a double-click or a re-opened email renders the "already received" state instead of queueing a second meeting. It inserts a `membership_renewal_meetings` row and fires `notifyByRule('MEMBERSHIP_renewal_meeting_requested')` — **action-required (`dismissible:false`)**, default recipient `rhopson@elitert.com`, linked straight to the member's Membership Fees card. NEW `actions/membership/renewal-meeting-outcome.ts` stamps `completed_at` / `outcome` / `recorded_by`; **`cancel` also flips `auto_renew=false` and drafts `MEMBERSHIP_cancel_confirmation` inside a `try/catch`** (a Gmail failure must not lose an outcome that is already recorded); **both outcomes clear the bell**, and nothing else does.
  - **THE GATE MOVED ON PURPOSE AND MONEY DID NOT MOVE WITH IT (#333).** `membership_plans_load` **lost its in-handler superadmin check** — it is a read-only loader, and `TAB_ACTIONS.accounting` is now its whole gate, exactly like `accounting_outstanding_links_load`. `membership_renewal_meeting_outcome` was **never given one**. Both exceptions are commented at their sites in `role-gates.ts` and in `plans-load.ts` specifically so a future reader of #309 does not "restore" a check that was removed deliberately. The reason is a person: **Rachael Hopson runs the renewal meetings and is not a superadmin.** Correspondingly the two Membership Fees mounts in `AdminPortal.jsx` relaxed from `session.is_superadmin` to `canSeeTab('accounting')`, and `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx` now takes an `isSuperadmin` prop behind which **every money control** sits — create/setup, links, auto-renew, next-year terms, Pause, Terminate, cancel, resend/reminder. An accounting-tab admin sees read-only cards, the schedule and the Renewal meeting section, and nothing that spends money.
  - **A PAUSE IS A SCHEDULE SHAPE, NOT A STATUS — AND THAT CHOICE IS THE WHOLE DESIGN (#332).** `membership_pause` (AUTH, superadmin in-handler like `terminate`; `{plan_id, months 1-12, preview}`) makes a pause mean exactly three things: **the member skips N months, every remaining payment moves N months later, the membership year ends N months later.** The plan **stays `status='active'`**, so the charge pass, the notice pass, the waive pass, terminate/cancel eligibility, the Payments page and every future reader of `plan.status` are all untouched. Four mechanics carry invariants: the shift runs **DESCENDING by `due_date`** so the partial unique `(plan_id, due_date) WHERE kind='membership'` never sees a transient collision (#315); `period_label` regenerates **only** when it still equals `periodLabel(old due)`, preserving annotated catch-up and annual labels verbatim; `year_end` extends +N across the whole `year_start` group while **`year_start` is never touched** (#280); and `renewal_date` advances +N pinned to the 15th, which is precisely what keeps **#235** true after the shift. `renewal_notice_for` is **deliberately left stale** so the member is warned again for the new date. `preview: true` runs the identical computation and **writes nothing** — the panel auto-calls it, so preview and commit cannot drift.
  - **THE `kind='pause'` MARKERS ARE SAFE FOR ONE REASON, AND IT IS A REASON A FUTURE READER CAN REVOKE BY ACCIDENT.** The vacated slots get zero-dollar `waived` marker rows so the ledger visibly shows the skipped months. **They are invisible to every money consumer ONLY because all of them filter `kind='membership'`** — that was verified reader-by-reader before shipping: invoice/receipt (4 sites), all five sweep passes, terminate and cancel voids, `send-reminder`, `all-payments-load`, the Stripe webhook blocks and the confirmation email. **So the standing rule is that any NEW reader of `member_payment_schedule` must filter `kind` or consciously decide what `'pause'` means to it.** A forgetful "total collected this year" query would not crash; it would silently count a $0 row as a payment. On the react side the ledger renders a Paused pill (amber `#b45309`), `bucketByYear` was **rewritten to group by `year_start`** (legacy 12-month windows only as a NULL fallback) because a paused year no longer fits a fixed 12-month bucket, and an amber **"Payments paused"** header pill was added — **distinct from the pre-existing `members.paused` pill**, and the two can appear together.

It is react-only, needs no backend, and rides the same owed deploy. Click-tested by the user.

  - **THE DUPLICATE WAS REAL, IT WAS TRACED TO ITS CAUSE, AND THE CAUSE IS NOT WHERE ANYONE WOULD LOOK FIRST (#327).** Henry Mennig (client **132**, `59380-001`, MAP 1 continuation payment **3**, **$1,050**) received **two identical receipt drafts carrying the SAME receipt number `REC-59380-001-0001`**. The DB timestamps settle it: the `payment_intent.succeeded` chain — invoice/receipt PDF → Drive upload → Gmail draft — ran **longer than Stripe's ~30s delivery timeout**, so Stripe marked the delivery failed and **redelivered the identical event**. `router/webhooks.ts` has **no event-id dedupe**, and the MAP 1 P2-4 branch had **no idempotency guard**, so `automation_CONTRACT_invoicereceipt` simply ran a second time. **Only ONE charge was taken** — the sweep's Stripe idempotency key held — and, decisively, **only ONE revshare draft** was produced, because `contract-revshare.ts` carries an `isResolved` guard and the receipt path carried none. **That asymmetry is the proof.** **v696 was investigated and ruled out** — it changed email *recipients*, not the receipt path.

- **Setting up a member who transfers in MID-YEAR stops being an arithmetic puzzle — the admin enters ONE number (payments already made) and the server derives the rest: how many charges are left, how much the setup link collects, and whether that link has to carry a catch-up so the year still finishes on the unchanged renewal date. Gotchas **#315** + **#316** (both ALWAYS-APPLIES, money). **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **WHY THE OLD FORM WAS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** A mid-year transfer keeps its existing renewal 15th, and the schedule used to be derived purely from that date: bill every charge date before renewal, one pull at the link, done. That is only correct for a member who is exactly on schedule. A member who came in with **free weeks** (paid ahead on the old platform) got billed for months they had already covered; a member who was **behind** got billed fewer than 12 times in the year and simply never caught up, because the renewal date is fixed and there are only so many charge dates before it. The admin had no way to say which of the two was happening, and the form's numbers and the emails' numbers were derived independently, so they could disagree.
  - **ONE INPUT, EVERYTHING ELSE DERIVED — and the derivation lives in exactly one function.** `prior_payments_made` (0–11) is now **REQUIRED** on monthly transfers (`plan-save.ts` 400s with *"Enter how many payments they already made this year (0-11)"*; still optional on annual transfers, which pay nothing at the link). The NEW column `member_payment_plans.remaining_payments` is **DERIVED SERVER-SIDE as `12 − prior`** and is written **unconditionally** — any value a client sends is ignored, and editing a plan away from monthly/transfer clears it back to NULL rather than leaving a stale number behind. NEW exported **`transferLinkPulls(plan, basisDate)`** in `actions/membership/shared.ts` returns `{remaining, slots, pullsAtLink}` and is the **single source** consumed by all four surfaces that used to compute their own answer: `setup-load.ts` (what the `/membership-pay` page shows), `setup-checkout.ts` (what Stripe actually charges), `activate.ts` (what the ledger records) and `send-setup-link.ts` (what the email quotes). `slots = 1 + subsequentChargeDates(basis, {untilExclusive: renewal}).length`; `remaining` falls back to `slots` when the column is NULL, which reproduces the **exact** legacy behaviour for any pending plan saved before the column existed; `pullsAtLink = 1 + max(0, remaining − slots)`.
  - **BEHIND PAYS CATCH-UP AT THE LINK; AHEAD JUST STOPS EARLY; THE RENEWAL DATE NEVER MOVES.** That is the whole model in one line. A member owing more than the calendar has room for pays the shortfall **in the first payment** — `mode=payment` charges `pullsAtLink × base` (the New Model card gross-up wraps the **total**, not the base), the memo appends *" (includes N-month catch-up)"*, and the period label reads *"August 2026 (includes 1-month catch-up)"*. A member with free weeks simply gets fewer scheduled rows and nothing at all in the months already covered. Because the year still ends on the same 15th, renewal, next-year terms and the sweep's renewal guard (#235) are all untouched.
  - **THE CATCH-UP MUST BE ONE ROW, AND WE LEARNED THAT THE EXPENSIVE WAY (#315).** The first implementation wrote the catch-up as **k separate rows all dated the pay date**. `member_payment_schedule` carries a deliberate **UNIQUE `(plan_id, due_date) WHERE kind='membership'`** index — the duplicate-charge guard — so in the sandbox test **Stripe collected the money first** and the year-1 ledger insert then bounced on `23505`: plan stuck `setup_pending`, member paid, no ledger, only an alert bell. It now folds into **ONE** row at `perPull × pulls` with `credit_applied` scaled the same way. That is safe because **the invoice/receipt engine totals by PaymentIntent, not by row** — a combined charge already stamps one PI (and one `card_processing_fee`, #281) across every row it covers. Two adjacent traps were closed in the same rewrite: a follow-up remainder of **0 must short-circuit** (`count: 0` is falsy inside `subsequentChargeDates` and reads as UNLIMITED), and `untilExclusive: renewalDate` is now passed on **every** transfer branch including the counted one, so no scheduled row can ever land on or after the renewal date.
  - **COUNTS SPEAK IN MONTHS NOW, NOT ROWS (#316).** The moment a row could span several months, `rowsThisYear.length` stopped meaning "payments remaining" — the invoice said **6** where the setup email said **7**, and the schedule ended the year at **"Payment 11"** of 12. NEW **`monthsCoveredByRow(row, grossMonthly)`** = `max(1, round((amount_due + credit_applied) / grossMonthly))` derives a row's span from the row's **own money**, which is what makes it survive a credit spread: net alone is short by the credit, but **net + credit = one gross month**. `invoice-receipt.ts` now routes every count through it — the invoice's payments-remaining, each schedule-line ordinal (multi-month rows label as **ranges**, *"Payments 6-7"*, so the year reaches 12), the receipt's `paymentLabel`, and the `[Remaining Payments]` / `[X]` / `[Y]` tokens. `utils/membership-confirmation.ts` counts the transfer ordinal's denominator the same way. **An ordinary row always evaluates to 1, so every non-catch-up document is byte-identical to before** — that is the regression proof, not an assertion.
  - **THE SETUP EMAIL NOW QUOTES THE REAL NUMBER.** `send-setup-link.ts` sources `[Remaining Payments]` from `transferLinkPulls` (it used to re-derive it from the renewal date) and gained **`[Setup Amount]`** — the actual link total — and **`[Setup Note]`**, which expands to *" — this covers N months (your regular month plus N-1 catch-up month(s)) so you're fully caught up by your renewal"* and is **empty when there is only one pull**, so a normal transfer's email is unchanged. Template id 191 was edited to consume both.
  - **ONE PRE-EXISTING WEBHOOK BUG RODE ALONG, AND ONE ALERT WAS TOLD THE TRUTH.** In the **MEMBER MEMBERSHIP FEES setup-link block only**, `router/webhooks.ts` now reads the session's `pull_count` metadata (stamped on **both** the session and `payment_intent_data`, clamped `>= 1`) and multiplies the **card-fee base** and the **ACH confirmation amount** by it. Without that, a multi-pull payment would have stamped the entire extra pull as `card_processing_fee` — and the invoice/receipt engine deliberately **prefers the stamped fee** over any re-derivation (#281), so the wrong number would have printed on a real document. `pipeRow` and every other webhook block are untouched. Separately, the activation-failure alert was **reworded**: the title is now *"Membership payment received but NOT recorded — <name>"* (payment path) / *"Membership setup saved but plan NOT activated"* (save-only) and the message opens *"The member's first payment WENT THROUGH at Stripe — the money landed — but it is not recorded on the ledger"*. The old *"Membership activation FAILED"* was read as a failed charge by the user during live testing — exactly the wrong instinct at exactly the wrong moment.
  - **THE FRONTEND FORM LOST INPUTS ON PURPOSE.** `MembershipFeesPanel.jsx`'s monthly-transfer setup is now **one required field** — *"Payments already made this year"* (0–11, blocks save when blank or invalid) — with everything else mirrored from the backend (`remaining = 12 − prior`, `pullsAtLink = 1 + max(0, remaining − slots)`, `perPull = max(0, roundDollar(annual/12 − credit/remaining))`) and rendered as a plain-English preview: *"Paid 5 of 12 — 7 × $667.00 left: $1,334.00 at the link (includes 1-month catch-up), then 5 monthly until renewal Jan 15, 2027"*. An earlier build in this same session had a *"Charges remaining (optional)"* override plus **two** warnings (a 13-payments mismatch and a renewal-cap warning); **all three were DELETED before shipping** when the user simplified the design — they never reached live, and the warnings became unreachable anyway once the count is derived rather than entered.
  - **NEW 4th PILL — "Outstanding Payment Links".** `OutstandingLinksSection` / `OutstandingLinkRow` list every `setup_pending` plan whose setup link has actually been emailed: expandable cards with Setup link / Transferred / Sandbox badges, the amount due at the link (or *"Save-only"*), the plan details, and **Resend payment setup link** + **Edit plan** buttons. **A deliberate difference from the tax and holistic tabs:** sandbox rows are **SHOWN**, flagged with an orange Sandbox badge, rather than hidden — this panel is precisely where sandbox test runs are watched, so hiding them would defeat the pill's purpose. Anyone unifying the "outstanding" pills across tabs must keep this exception.
  - **Verification.** `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every edge edit and again at the audit; action parity **449** (443 `(c) =>` + 6 logins, **+0**) re-run at the audit; `npm run build` exit 0 with 31 route pages; **security advisor GREEN** after the DDL and re-confirmed at the audit (only the five standing deny-all INFO rows + the standing `pg_net` WARN). **CURRENT STATE entry archived verbatim from SESSION_REFERENCE (the assess-form Edit + retainer-paid Tray bell session, aged out at this audit):**
- **A submitted "Assess tax planning opportunities" form stops being permanently frozen — it gains an Edit button that reopens the real form without disturbing the step's completion date — and paying the tax retainer now raises ONE bell to Tray asking her to schedule the Detailed tax plan meeting** (2026-07-31, the THIRD session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-af97ed` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **2 modified code files + 1 new migration file**, react = **1 code file** + docs. **+0 actions (449)** — no new handler, no dispatch or role-gate change. `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every edge edit. `npm run build` exit 0, 31 route pages. **Backend DEPLOYED → live `vfo-admin-api` v687** (TWO deploys, v686 then v687, both user-approved; verified via `supabase functions list`). `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **NO DDL — DML ONLY** (one `notification_rules` insert, 107 `email_templates` `cc_list` updates, a 4-row typo-Cc removal, and a test-fixture wipe at close), **so the Supabase security advisor was correctly NOT run** — it is the gate for DDL, not for data. Gotchas **#313** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, Notifications) **+ #314** (ALWAYS-APPLIES, tax track). **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **WHY THE ASSESS FORM WAS FROZEN, AND WHY THAT WAS NEVER A RULE.** The "Assess tax planning opportunities (and enter presentation details)" step (ids 89/123, sentinel `assess_form`, #306) went permanently read-only the moment it was submitted. Investigating it turned up the important fact: **the backend never had a guard.** `tax_save_assess_form` has always accepted a re-save and overwrites the whole `assess_form` object. The lock was one line of frontend state — `isViewMode = !!existingData` in `AssessTaxForm` — i.e. an accident of how the submitted view was built, not a policy anyone decided. Fees and strategy numbers change between the assessment and the presentation, and the only recourse was asking an engineer to edit jsonb by hand.
  - **THE REMOUNT KEY IS LOAD-BEARING — this is the trap (#314).** `AssessTaxForm` now takes `editing = false` + `existingCompletedDate = null`, and `isViewMode = !!existingData && !editing`. The submitted branch renders an **Edit** button (`e.stopPropagation()` so it does not toggle the chevron; sets the expand key **and** a new `assessedit_${task.id}` key) and the call site passes **`key={isEditing ? 'edit' : 'view'}`**. That key is not cosmetic: the view branch's Summary table renders from **component state** (`rows = assessComputeRows(strategies)`), not from the plan prop, so without the remount React would keep the edit-mode state alive when `editing` flipped back to false — **Edit → change numbers → Cancel would display the abandoned draft as if it were saved, and a second Edit would resume it.** That bug existed in the first implementation and was caught in review before it shipped.
  - **AN EDIT MUST NOT MOVE THE COMPLETION DATE.** `handleSubmit` passes `existingCompletedDate` (read from `localProgress[task.id]?.completed_date`) into `saveTask`, so re-saving a submitted form re-writes the same `completed_date` rather than stamping today — the client overview's last-action reading stays truthful about when the step was actually completed. A first submit still passes `null` and gets today's date. **`assess_form_submitted_at` / `_by` DO still move on every save** (the backend owns them and stamps unconditionally) — accepted deliberately: those two fields mean "who last touched this form", which is exactly what they now report. The Submit button reads **"Save changes"** while editing.
  - **LEGACY `{question_1}` ROWS ARE EDITABLE, AND SAVING REPLACES THEM FOR GOOD.** This was the user's explicit decision. Edit mode on a legacy row shows the old free-text answer in a dimmed, read-only box labelled **"Previous answer — will be replaced when you save"** above a blank structured form; saving writes the structured `{fee, strategies}` shape and the legacy text is gone (the backend overwrites the whole `assess_form` object — there is no merge). The legacy read-only *view* is unchanged for anyone who does not press Edit, so #306's "legacy rows must keep rendering" invariant holds.
  - **WHO GETS THE EDIT BUTTON — and no role changed to make it so.** The **member portal is unaffected**: its `readOnly` early-return fires before the submitted branch, so members still see the pill only. The **tax planner portal gets Edit automatically** and correctly — the step is already on **both** `PLANNER_EDITABLE_TASK_NAMES` whitelists (#262) and `tax_save_assess_form` is already in `TAX_PLANNER_ALLOWED_ACTIONS` with its `denyIfNotPlannerPlan` guard. **No `role-gates.ts`, no whitelist and no handler was touched.** #306's other invariants are intact: derived values are still computed at render and never stored, and FE/BE validation is untouched.
  - **THE RETAINER BELL — ONE BELL, ONE EVENT, DELIBERATELY NOT WAITING FOR ACH.** `actions/tax/confirmation-email.ts` fires `insertTaxNotifications(…, "TAX_retainer_paid_schedule_meeting", ["tvaldes@elitert.com"], …)` — title `"<Client First Last> has decided to move forward with tax planning"`, message `"Please schedule the Detailed tax plan meeting."`, link `/admin/client/<id>?tab=tax&program=<program_id||1>`, `dismissible:true`, `dedupe:"unread"`, wrapped in try/catch so a notification failure can never fail the payment handler. **Placement is the design:** inside the retainer-only (`!isImpl`) block, **after** the `retainer_confirmation_status` write and the existing PF "retainer paid" bell, **before** the ERT agreement copy. That puts it among the unconditional retainer side effects — the `cardReceiptOnly` gate above it only skips the CLIENT email (#287) — so it fires for **BOTH card and ACH at `checkout.session.completed`**, at submit time rather than at ACH settlement, because Tray should start booking the meeting the moment the client commits. Check payers reach the same point via the `automation_TAX_checkcleared` chain, which is intended. The handler's terminal-status early-return (`'Sent'` / `'Skipped - Card (Receipt Only)'`) makes a replayed webhook a no-op, so the bell is exactly-once without any extra guard.
  - **THE KEY COLLISION THAT WOULD HAVE FAILED SILENTLY (#313).** The obvious rule key `TAX_retainer_paid` was **already taken** — by the assigned-PF "Retainer paid" FYI seeded in `20260702120000` and fired from **this same handler, ten lines above**. Reusing it would have done two bad things at once: the seed migration would have been a **silent no-op** (`ON CONFLICT (key) DO NOTHING` — the file would look applied and change nothing), and the two bells would have shared one Notification Editor row, so disabling or retargeting the PF FYI would have silently done the same to Tray's. **CURRENT STATE entry archived verbatim from SESSION_REFERENCE (the member Introductions-vs-Connections session, aged out at this audit):**
- **"Connected Member" splits into TWO different relationships that were never the same thing — an INTRODUCTION is one-way and carries the tier the INTRODUCER earns, a CONNECTION is mutual, untyped and unlimited — and both now render on BOTH members' profiles with clickable names, while the old single-pointer column retires to corporate-parent duty** (2026-07-31, the SECOND session that day, branch `claude/vfo-session-setup-b5c9b3` in **BOTH** repos — edge = **4 modified + 2 new action files + 2 new migration files**, react = **2 code files** + docs. **+2 actions (449)** — `member_connection_add` + `member_connection_remove`. `deno check --no-lock` **0** after every edge edit. `npm run build` exit 0, 31 route pages. **Backend DEPLOYED → live `vfo-admin-api` v685** (TWO deploys, v684 then v685, both user-approved; verified via `list_edge_functions`). `boldsign-webhook` UNTOUCHED at **v40**. **TWO DDL migrations**, written as files AND applied live **by the user** in Studio SQL (the Claude-side MCP was permission-blocked — #196 still satisfied because the files are committed) → security advisor **GREEN** + anon probe `*/0`. Gotcha **#312** (ALWAYS-APPLIES). **MERGE-PENDING both repos.**)
  - **WHY.** There was exactly ONE member-to-member link in the system: `members.connected_member_number`, a single self-referencing pointer, optionally tiered by `members.connection_type`. That one slot was carrying three unrelated meanings — a revenue-sharing introduction, an ordinary peer relationship, and the corporate-parent pointer — and because it was one-way and single-valued it failed at all three: the *other* member's profile showed nothing, a second relationship overwrote the first, and nobody could tell from the data which meaning a given row had. The two real concepts now have two separate stores with two different shapes, and the old column keeps only the third meaning.
  - **AN INTRODUCTION IS DIRECTIONAL, AND THE TIER IS THE INTRODUCER'S MONEY (#312).** NEW column `members.introduced_by_member_number` (text, FK → `members.member_number` `ON DELETE SET NULL`) answers "who introduced THIS member" — **one introducer per member**. The tier stays in the EXISTING `members.connection_type` (`'5% - Regular Advisor'` / `'10% - Accredited Introducer'` / `'10% - Accredited Mentor'` / `'20% - Accredited Introducer + Mentor'`), relabelled **"Introducer Benefit"**, because it describes what the person named in `introduced_by_member_number` earns: **read it off the introduced member's row, pay it to the introducer.** It is now shown for **every** member category — accountants included, where the dropdown used to be hidden. Migration `20260731120000_introduced_by_member_number.sql` also MOVED the three rows that already carried a tier (Marjorie Wang 59470 ← Jason Bright 59119, Violetta Terpeluk 59515 ← Deb Snyder 59414, Todd Veillon 58088-FC6 ← Jack Branch 58088) — a typed old-style link WAS an introduction, which is exactly why `connection_type` could be reused untouched. **No new action was needed for this half**: `member_profile_save` is a whole-row spread upsert of the `profile` payload, so the column persists through the ordinary Save button.
  - **A CONNECTION IS A CANONICAL PAIR, AND THE CHECK IS THE DESIGN.** NEW table `public.member_connections` (`id` identity PK, `member_a`/`member_b` text FK → `members` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, `created_at`, **CHECK `member_a < member_b`**, **UNIQUE `(member_a, member_b)`**, deny-all RLS in the same migration per #141). Storing the lexicographically smaller number first means the same link can never exist twice in opposite orders and "are these two connected" is ONE symmetric lookup. **Every writer normalizes before touching the table.** NEW `member_connection_add` / `member_connection_remove` (`actions/members/connection-add.ts` / `connection-remove.ts`, AUTH, both in `ADMIN_ONLY_ACTIONS` on the line below `member_profile_save`, both registered in `AUTH_HANDLERS` right after it) accept `{member_a, member_b}` in either order, sort them, and are **idempotent on purpose** — add treats a `23505` unique violation as success (double-clicks, retries), remove treats a missing row as success (the end state is reached either way). Add validates non-empty / not-equal / both-exist with an error-destructured lookup (#187) so a DB failure can never masquerade as "member not found".
  - **`connected_member_number` IS NOW LEGACY, AND THE VALUES ARE GONE.** Migration `20260731130000_member_connections.sql` backfilled all **240** one-way links as pairs and then **CLEARED the column on every non-corporate row** — zero live rows carry a value. It survives for exactly one writer: the Add Advisor **corporate** flow (`add_member_full`, behind the "Connected Member \*" picker that only appears for a Corporate member type), which uses it as the parent pointer; corporate members were deliberately excluded from both the backfill and the clear. `load_data` still returns it for that purpose. **Anything else reading it for connection meaning is now a bug, not a style question — the data is empty.** The PFT auto-link in `actions/accountant/create-member.ts` was converted accordingly: it no longer writes `connected_member_number` on the members insert and instead inserts a normalized pair **after** the members row exists (both sides are FKs), best-effort inside try/catch with `23505` swallowed, so a connection failure can never block accountant creation.
  - **THE PAYLOAD GAINED A TOP-LEVEL KEY, NOT A PER-MEMBER ONE.** `actions/data/load-data.ts` adds `introduced_by_member_number` to the per-member roster merge (beside `connected_member_number`/`connection_type` — a new `members` column is invisible to the portal until it is whitelisted there, #207) **and a NEW top-level `member_connections` array** of raw `{member_a, member_b}` rows, fetched by one extra query inside the existing `Promise.all`. Pairs are top-level rather than folded into each member because they are symmetric — attaching them per-member would duplicate every row twice and invite one side to drift.
  - **TWO CARDS ON DETAILS, AND THE DIRECTION IS SPELLED OUT.** The profile details view renders an **"Introductions"** card with two labelled sub-sections — *Introduced By* (this member's introducer, 40px avatar, tier chip **inline next to the name**) and *Introducer Of* (everyone whose `introduced_by_member_number` points back at this member, 30px rows, each chipped with **their own** `connection_type`) — plus a separate **"Connections"** card of mutual partners as plain rows with **no chips**, because a connection has no tier and inventing one would imply money that does not exist. Corporate-type members are excluded from both; they stay in the unchanged Corporate Members card.
  - **THE EDIT TAB HAS TWO ADJACENT CARDS WITH TWO DIFFERENT COMMIT MODELS — this is the trap (#312).** The **Introductions** card is ordinary buffered profile state (typeahead → `introduced_by_member_number`, select → `connection_type`, "Remove Introduction" clears both) and commits on **Save**, like every other card on the tab. The **Connections** card **cannot** — its data lives in another table — so each per-row **Remove** and each "Add Connection (search member)" pick fires `member_connection_remove` / `member_connection_add` **immediately** and then calls `onDataChange()` (`AdminPortal.loadAllData`) to re-read. **Leaving the tab without pressing Save does NOT undo a connection change.** The add typeahead also filters out existing partners and self, so the idempotent-add path is a safety net rather than a routine occurrence.
  - **EVERY NAME IS A LINK, AND THE SAME-CATEGORY JUMP NEEDED A NEW ADOPT BRANCH.** `AdminPortal.openMemberProfile` — the same callback the Member Overview list uses — is threaded down as `onOpenMember` through `MembersPanel` → `AccountantsPanel`/`AdvisorsPanel`/`StrategicMembersPanel` → `MemberDirectoryView` → `MemberProfile` (alongside `memberConnections`; #193 — a prop used only inside a nested component must reach it), so an advisor's card can open an accountant's profile. A **cross-category** jump remounts `MemberDirectoryView` and its `useState` initializer picks the seeded `sessionStorage` selection up; a **same-category** jump does not remount, so the `navClickCount` effect was extended to **ADOPT** a seeded selection (look it up in `allMembers`, select it, restore the feature tab, scroll to top) instead of only clearing when the key is absent. Ordinary tab navigation still wipes the key first and therefore still clears the selection.

Eight such rows existed and were backed up and deleted (see the DB cell). **Every consumer of Tax 6 done-ness must iterate `client_tax_specialists`** — there are four, and they were all changed together: the FE `getPhaseState` branch, the FE hero counts, the FE card pill, and the BE overview branch. **Phase done additionally requires at least one allocated specialist** — a plan with none shows "No specialists allocated yet." and can never read Done, which is correct (nothing has been implemented) and is a deliberate change from the old vacuous-truth behavior.
  - **THE OVERVIEW SHARES TAX 5's SCOPE ON PURPOSE.** `overview-tax.ts` emits one step per specialist labelled `<task name> — <specialist name>` with `applicable: implReach`, and crucially tags it with the **SAME `spec-<id>` scope string the Tax 5 branch uses**. That makes one specialist's Tax 5 steps and their Tax 6 steps a single ordered sequence for the skipped-step scanner, so "step 3 answered but step 2 blank" warns within a specialist and never across two different specialists. Giving Tax 6 its own scope would have produced false warnings on every multi-specialist plan.
  - **CHIP PRECEDENCE IS Stopped > Done > In progress > Not started.** Per specialist box: ANY of the four steps answered `Stopped` → red **Stopped** (a stop is the headline, even if the other three are done); else all four answered → green **Done**; else some answered → blue **In progress · n/4**; else grey **Not started**. **"Answered" means any non-empty status** — `Completed`, `Stopped` and `N/A` all count, because the question has been decided either way. The box default-expands until all four are answered (expand key `tax6_spec_<id>`), matching the phase-collapse convention (#275). The card pill counts **specialists × 4**, not 4.
  - **THE HERO COUNT WAS THE EASY DOUBLE-COUNT TO GET WRONG.** Tax 6 is the only phase in `phasesAfterSpec`, and it used to be summed by the plan-level `reduce` over `[...phasesBeforeSpec, ...phasesAfterSpec]`. It is now **removed from BOTH reduces** and added once as its own per-specialist term (`taxSpecialists.length × tax6SpecTasks.length`), mirroring how `tax5aSpecTasks` is already handled. Leaving it in the reduce **and** adding the per-spec term would have counted it twice; removing it without adding the term would have dropped it from the hero entirely.
  - **THE REMOVE BUG THE USER HIT.** Removing a specialist left the card on screen until a page reload. `removeSpecialist` cleared the progress keys and the expand keys but relied on `loadSpecialists()` — whose `catch` is silent — to drop the row itself, so any hiccup in the re-fetch left a deleted specialist rendered. It now does an **optimistic `setTaxSpecialists(p => p.filter(...))` immediately after backend success**, with the re-fetch demoted to reconciliation. It also clears the new `tax6_spec_<id>` expand key alongside the Tax 5 `spec_<id>` one — a new per-specialist expand key must be cleared here or it leaks across specialist ids.
  - **CUSTOM NAMING: THE SERVER OWNS THE PREFIX.** The picker's trailing option is relabelled **"Custom"** (the sentinel `OTHER_SPEC_VALUE = '__other__'` is UNCHANGED) and selecting it reveals a name input (80-char `maxLength`) with **Add disabled until it is non-empty**. The body gains `custom_name`; `add-specialist.ts` runs `sanitizeCustomName` (collapse whitespace → trim → strip a leading case-insensitive "custom -" → 80-char cap) and inserts **`Custom - <name>`**, building the prefix itself from the `CUSTOM_PREFIX` constant so a client that sends "Custom - Bob" still stores `Custom - Bob` rather than doubling it. **An empty or absent `custom_name` falls back to the legacy `Other #N (See notes)` numbering** — kept deliberately for API back-compat and for rows already in the wild, not as a UI path (the FE can no longer reach it). **`expert_id` stays NULL on both paths**, so the showroom/widget-leak guarantee of #305 is untouched, and **neither path dedupes** (several customs on one plan are legitimate, exactly as several "Other"s were).
  - **WORDING.** The greyed-out Tax 5 steps under a `Client decision 2 = 'Move to Implementation'` plan now read **"(Due Diligence Skipped - Moved to Implementation)"** (was "(Moved to implementation)"). This is the `greyNote` display string ONLY — **the two load-bearing status strings `'Continue DD'` / `'Move to Implementation'` of gotcha #274 are UNCHANGED**, and so is the BE `byName("Client decision 2")` resolution.
  - **DB — DML ONLY, and the user re-entered the data by hand.** A pre-change report found exactly two clients with Tax 6 progress: **Marc Ehrhardt** (client 129, plan 89) and **Henry Mennig** (client 132, plan 92), all four tasks `Completed` 2026-07-30, all plan-level.   - **THE MONEY BUG — found by a fresh-eyes review, confirmed, and defused before it ever fired.** `actions/pipeline/contract-revshare.ts` and `actions/tax/revshare.ts` both opened with `let revPaidValue = "N/A — No Share Due"` — a **TERMINAL** status — and ran the Stripe transfer only inside `if (!isMoneyMapping && shareAmount > 0 && member.stripe_account_id)`. A share that WAS due but whose member had **no Connect account** (or a run where the `STRIPE_KEY` lookup failed) fell straight past that block and wrote the terminal value: **no transfer, no bell, and a row both sweeps treat as resolved**, indistinguishable from a genuine zero-share row. Replaced with an **exhaustive branch chain** — `isMoneyMapping` → `shareAmount <= 0` → `!stripe_account_id` (NEW non-terminal `AWAITING_CONNECT` = `"Awaiting Connect Setup"` + an action-required bell) → `!STRIPE_KEY` (`Failed` + the existing FAILURE bell) → transfer.   - **THE HARD BLOCKER THE FIX ITSELF CREATED — and why the tax sweep had to move with it.** `actions/tax/revshare-sweep.ts` gated its retry on `isRetry = revShare === "Pending" || revPaid === "Failed"`, and the handler writes `rev_share='Completed - Revenue Share'` **even when held** — so a held tax leg would have matched NEITHER predicate and been dropped **forever**, a worse outcome than the bug. Widened with `|| revPaid === AWAITING_CONNECT` (reason label `awaiting-connect`). **The MAP 1 sweep needed NO change** — it has no `isRetry` gate. Alongside it: `*_rev_completed_at` is now stamped **only on a terminal outcome** (a held leg no longer reads as finished), `actions/tax/refund.ts` **settles** a held leg after a successful refund (else the widened sweep would pay a share out of refunded money), `actions/payments/normalize.ts` shows **"Awaiting payout setup"** instead of the misleading "Pending", and `actions/msm/pip-revshare.ts` got its missing-`STRIPE_KEY` hole closed (**PIP was the only pipeline already handling the missing-account case** — it still has no retry sweep, so its bell honestly says "manual re-fire").
  - **THE PAYOUT MATH + THE DEAD CONTRIBUTION CODE (#304).** The MAP 1 member leg computed `(member_share / gross_fee) × thisPayment`, so a member contribution making `net < gross` **silently shrank the entered share**. Now the entered share pays **IN FULL**, split by cumulative difference — **numerically identical for every existing row** (all have `gross == net` or a blank gross); the strategic leg's proration is untouched. **USER-CONFIRMED SEMANTICS:** `member_contribution` is a discount the member funds (client pays `gross − contribution`) and **Member Share is typed already net of it**, so both handlers' contribution-deduction blocks were **deleted** — they were dead (nothing has ever written `member_contrib_status='Pending'`) **and** a latent overpay-on-retry bug (they flipped the status to `Applied` **before** the transfer, so a retry recomputed without the deduction). `client_tax_plans` has no `member_contribution` column at all.

A NULL expert means **no `experts` row exists**, so an "Other" can never leak into a showroom or the public widget. ONE picker (`TaxPrioritiesTab.jsx`) serves **both** programs, so both got it at once.

  - **THE SURFACES.** Three pill-tabs, all labeled **"Outstanding Payment Links"**, added to the existing `AccountingCombinedPanel` containers: **Accounting > VFO Services > Holistic Planning**, **> Tax Planning**, and **Accounting > Specialists > VFO Specialist Revenue**. ONE new component `src/components/admin/OutstandingLinksPanel.jsx` serves all three off a `kind` prop (`map1` | `tax` | `specrev`) plus the standard `embedded` prop; `AdminPortal.jsx` gains 1 import + 3 appended tab objects (keys `holistic_outstanding_links` / `tax_outstanding_links` / `specialist_outstanding_links`). **PILL-ONLY and deliberately not deep-linkable** — no sidebar entries and no `accountingSection` guard changes, so there is no `?section=` that lands here; the pills are reached from their parent Accounting surface.
  - **WHAT COUNTS AS OUTSTANDING (the loader's five sections).** `accounting_outstanding_links_load` returns `{ map1: {first_links, continuation}, tax: {first_links, implementation_links, continuation}, specrev: {recurring, requests} }`. **first_links** = the original payment email sent and never paid — MAP 1 `pay1_email_sent_at` set with `pay1_status` NULL, TAX `payment_email_sent_at` set with `retainer_status` NULL. **tax.implementation_links** = `retainer_status='succeeded'` with `implementation_charge_status` in (`declined`, `auth_required`, `manual_required`), **deduped against the continuation rows** so a client mid-continuation is not listed twice. **continuation** = the newest UNUSED `migration_setup_tokens` row per `(pipeline, row_id)` — **the EXACT same reduction `sweepMigrationSetupLinks` uses**, so what the tab shows is what the sweep will act on tonight, with per-token history, expiry state, and auto-resend lineage. - **Specialist $99/mo license invoice/receipt + Stage 4→5 automation fix** (2026-07-07, branch `claude/specialist-lic-invoice-fix` — backend only, `vfo-edge-functions`; **backend DEPLOYED v545→v550 across 6 approved deploys**, save-point tag **`backend-good-2026-07-07-v551`**; **DB applied live via MCP; advisor GREEN**; no frontend change). *(Moved from SESSION_REFERENCE CURRENT STATE 2026-07-08. Independently reviewed + hardened 2026-07-08 → v561; the claim RPC's migration file `20260708130000_claim_specialist_license_invoice_rpc.sql` was committed then — gotcha #196.)*
  - **Symptom.** Jake reported: specialist pays the $99/mo license via subscription checkout, gets the confirmation email, but the invoice/receipt email never drafts and the record never advances Stage 4→5 — a flow that had "worked ~30 times before." Stripe showed the webhook returning 200; nothing in the DB moved.
  - **Bug 1 — Stripe API version fragility (real, but not the root cause).** The `invoice.paid`/`invoice.payment_succeeded` handler hard-gated on the invoice's subscription ref (`invoice.subscription || invoice.parent?.subscription_details?.subscription`); the account's newer API version (`2025-08-27.basil`) can omit both, so the guard silently skipped the whole block. Fixed: never gate on the event's subscription ref — fall back to the row's stored `lic_subscription_id`. ALSO made the first invoice/receipt + Stage advance fire inline from `checkout.session.completed` (card path) by expanding the subscription's `latest_invoice` at checkout time, so the card-payment case no longer depends on a separate invoice event arriving/parsing correctly at all (ACH still waits for the later event, since funds aren't confirmed yet at checkout time).
  - **Bug 2 — THE actual root cause: a PostgREST schema-cache anomaly + a silently-swallowed error.** Direct REST calls (curl GET/PATCH) against `specialist_onboarding` resolved `lic_last_invoice_id` (added 2026-06-05) fine; the SAME write issued by the deployed edge function via `supabase-js` reliably threw `42703 column does not exist` — before AND after a `NOTIFY pgrst, 'reload schema'`. The ORIGINAL code destructured only `{ data }` from the claim UPDATE, so this real DB error was invisible — the handler just silently returned, looking identical to "nothing to do." This is almost certainly why it's been failing quietly for a while, not "just started" — the visible signal (confirmation email, a DIFFERENT code path) kept firing. **Fix:** every `supabase.from(...)` call in the license-invoice path now checks `error` and logs explicitly (gotcha #187); the specific troublesome write was moved into a new `SECURITY DEFINER` RPC `claim_specialist_license_invoice(p_onboarding_id, p_invoice_id, p_paid_at)` called via `supabase.rpc(...)` — RPC only needs PostgREST to resolve the function name (a coarser, stable cache entry), so the write now runs as native SQL with full column visibility, sidestepping the anomaly entirely (gotcha #188).
  - **Verification.** End-to-end on a fresh test specialist with a real sandbox card payment (`4242…`): invoice/receipt drafted (`INV-SPECLIC-…`/`REC-SPECLIC-…`), Stage 4→5 advanced automatically, claimed exactly once (idempotency intact — the `.or(is.null,neq)` dedup pattern, gotcha #28, is preserved inside the new RPC). Two rounds of Stripe-event resend testing plus one full fresh-specialist real-payment test were used to isolate the two bugs from each other. deno check 0; action count 373 (unchanged); advisor GREEN; pipeline smoke **5/5 PASS**.
  - **Cleanup.** A temporary diagnostic table (`_webhook_debug_trace`) + matching trace-log calls were added mid-session to see past the log-visibility gap, then fully removed once the fix was confirmed — zero trace remains. Two test `specialist_onboarding` rows (created for verification) were fully deleted along with their progress/ledger/notification/document-number rows. *(2026-07-08 note: one orphan `specialist_license_payments` row for that test survived this cleanup and was removed the next day.)*
  - **New gotchas #187–#188.** No config remaining — this was a pure bugfix, fully verified live.

- **VFO Specialist Revenue — shared house-account "record expected payment → mark received" model** (2026-07-07, branch `claude/specrev-house-account` BOTH repos; **backend DEPLOYED v554→v555**; frontend **SHIPPED `live-44-specialist-revenue-house-account`** (react #102 / edge #75); **DB applied live via MCP; advisor GREEN**). Replaced the rotating per-request "Bank transfer" option (built the day before, `live-40`) with a single permanent receiving account. *(Moved from SESSION_REFERENCE CURRENT STATE 2026-07-08.)*
  - **A. The model.** ONE shared VFO Stripe "house" customer PER MODE (sandbox/live), reused forever, giving a permanent ACH account/routing via Stripe `funding_instructions` handed to every specialist to push to. Stored in NEW table `specialist_revenue_house_account` (sandbox boolean PK; deny-all RLS). An earlier per-specialist `specialist_revenue_accounts` table was created then dropped same-session (no residue; migration file keeps that name but creates the house table).
  - **B. Flow.** Admin picks "Bank transfer — record expected payment" → `send-request.ts` (`payment_method:'pending'`) calls NEW `ensureHouseAccount` (`house-account.ts`), inserts request `payment_status='pending'` + lines, sends **NO email**, returns the house account details. Later admin clicks "Mark payment received" → NEW action `specialist_revenue_confirm_received` (`confirm-received.ts`, self-gates `auth.isSuperadmin`): trust-the-click, creates+confirms a `customer_balance` PaymentIntent to draw the amount from the pooled house cash balance.
  - **C. The critical guard.** If the draw doesn't immediately succeed the PI is **CANCELED** and the action returns `{ok:false,not_funded:true,message}` — otherwise the open PI sits and silently swallows a later transfer into the pool. On success the request flips to `received` + chains `specialist_revenue_invoicereceipt` + `specialist_revenue_payout` via service-role. The confirm PI carries **NO `metadata.pipeline`** (only `request_id` + `payment_kind=specialist_revenue_house`) so `router/webhooks.ts` ignores it — **webhooks.ts NOT touched this session**.
  - **D. Received-only surfaces (latent over-count fix).** `SpecialistReconciliationPanel.jsx` now counts only `payment_status='received'` requests; `SpecialistRevenuePanel.jsx` viewer money totals + By-member rollup are RECEIVED-ONLY (`receivedFiltered`) — pending/requested is expected money, not reconciled revenue. By-specialist list still shows all.

  - **A. Per-request payment-method pick.** New Payment (`SpecialistPaymentInput.jsx`) offered a radio-card selector: **ACH-debit payment link** (existing default — unchanged) OR **Bank transfer** (new). Bank transfer: `actions/specialist-revenue/send-request.ts` created a confirmed Stripe `customer_balance` PaymentIntent (`funding_type=bank_transfer`, `us_bank_transfer`, metadata `pipeline=VFO_SPECIALIST_REVENUE` + `request_id` + `payment_kind=specialist_revenue`); Stripe issued per-customer **virtual bank details** (account/routing/bank name/reference/hosted URL) persisted on the request row (6 `bank_transfer_*` columns) and emailed to the specialist via a pay-link-free template (`SPECREV_payment_request_banktransfer`). Status design — deliberately NO 'processing' stage.** The request stayed `payment_status='requested'` through funding so the payout-sweep 48h/96h reminder ladder (keyed on `'requested'`) kept running; `payout-sweep.ts` gained per-method 48h reminder branches (bank-transfer rows used `SPECREV_payment_reminder_banktransfer`, restating the stored bank details). When funds FULLY arrived, `payment_intent.succeeded` (webhook guard widened to accept `requested` + bank_transfer) flipped it straight to **`received`** and chained invoice/receipt + member payout exactly like ACH (`invoice-receipt.ts` + `utils/specialist-revenue-invoice.ts` gained bank-transfer label branches — invoice "Bank Transfer", receipt "Via Bank Transfer" no last4, "[PROCESSING_TIME]" → "Your bank transfer has been received.").

`Completed`/`Signed`(Anton) → `agreement_signed_by_ceo_at` + chain `automation_SPECIALIST_licstripecustomer` → reuses `bg_stripe_customer_id`, mints `lic_checkout_token`, chains `licpaymentemail` (`/specialist-pay?token=&kind=license`) → `licloadpayment` / `liccheckout` (Stripe Checkout **mode=subscription**, inline monthly $99 `price_data`, card grossed-up 2.9%+$0.30 / ACH flat, `subscription_data[metadata]` + session `metadata` `pipeline=SPECIALIST_ONBOARDING`/`payment_kind=license`/`payment_method_type`). **Webhook (`router/webhooks.ts`, 3 new additive blocks):** `checkout.session.completed` (mode=subscription + license) records subscription/method + marks `payment_made` + chains `licconfirmation`; **`invoice.paid`/`invoice.payment_succeeded`** (routed by `lic_stripe_customer_id`) → captures the payment method **if not already set** (race-proof — either event can land first), sets `lic_last_invoice_id` (per-invoice idempotency), first invoice (`billing_reason=subscription_create`) → `licconfirmation` + `licinvoicereceipt` (INV/REC-`SPECLIC` PDFs to the same Drive folder) + advance **Stage 4→5**, recurring → monthly invoice/receipt; **`invoice.payment_failed`** → Tracy dunning FYI + `lic_payment_status='failed'`. 20 new `specialist_onboarding` columns (`lic_*` + `agreement_*` + `rev_share_agreement_text` + 6 Stage-4 reminder guards — see [tables/specialists.md](specialists.md)). **Reminder sweep now 7 stalls** (removed the dead per-meeting rev-share stall #2 + `revButtons` + `SPECIALIST_revshare_reminder` template; added **DD-checklist / final-rev-share / agreement-signature / license-payment**, each 48h reminder + 96h Tracy FYI; the signature reminder fetches a fresh BoldSign embedded link). **Stage-2 reviewer notes reworked**: order is now **rev-share proposal → reviewer notes → vote**, notes are **always-visible** (shared `ReviewerNotesSection` so Stage 2 and Stage 4 mirror), **Tim shown unless tax=No** (labeled "if applicable"); `save-progress.ts` reviewer-notes notification idempotency now matches **title + unread** (multiple non-dismissible notifs can share a link), and skips a reviewer who already filled their notes; Tracy gets a non-dismissible **"submit the revenue share proposal"** action (fired by `stage2-email.ts` when all Stage-2 items are complete, cleared on submit). 10 new email templates (91–100; see Templates). `pipeline_sandbox_config` SPECIALIST_ONBOARDING still `sandbox_mode=true`. See [docs/flows/specialist-onboarding.md](specialist-onboarding.md).
- **Partnership Fast Track (PFT) automation** (this session, branch `claude/objective-hopper-26d8a3`, backend live **v415**; ⚠️ **frontend NOT deployed** — PFT track UI, `/pft-ft-decide` + `/pft-discovery` pages, the onboarding deep-link + "Accountant Type" changes live only on the dev server until `npm run deploy`. **NOTHING committed in either repo.**). Makes the previously-inert PFT engagement track ("PFT Engagement Process" tab on a Partnership-Fast-Track client; `components/admin/pft/PFTEngagementTrack.jsx`) actually send emails + drive the flow. Pipeline label `PARTNERSHIP_FAST_TRACK`; per-accountant state in NEW table `pft_engagement` (client_id uniq + `discovery_token`/`_data`/`_submitted_at`/`_email_sent_at`/`_reminder_sent_at`/`_pf_notified_at` + `ft_response_token`/`_email_sent_at`/`_response`/`_response_at`/`_reminder_sent_at`/`_pf_notified_at` + `accountant_onboarding_id`). Track structure is DB-driven (`program_client_phases`/`program_client_tasks`, `track_type='partnership_fast_track'`) — this session stripped "Phase N -" from phase names, renamed task51→"Meeting 1 confirmation email", deleted the date-only Meeting 2/3 tasks, added a "Does the Accountant need a third meeting?" Yes/No gate (both green) + a no-third-meeting decision task, and blanked both Phase 6 task lists (rendered dynamically). **Meeting confirmation** (Meeting 1/2/3) = one warm `PFT_meeting_confirm` template (placeholders `[PRIOR_MEETING]`/`[NEXT_MEETING]`/`[NEXT_MEETING_TITLE]`/`[FORM_SECTION]`/`[CLOSING]`; discovery-form button only on Meeting 2) via a 3-button decision (with date / date-not-confirmed / declined → `automation_PFT_meetingemail`, Gmail draft). **Decision step** (VFO FT / VFO Associate / No → `automation_PFT_decisionemail`): all three draft an email; FT + Associate **immediately create an `accountant_onboarding` handoff** (FT: `selected_vfo_ft`+`accountant_type='VFO FT'`; Associate: `selected_pft`+`accountant_type='VFO Associate'`); No drafts decline + sets client `status='lost'`. The **VFO FT email carries two recipient buttons** ("I Don't Need Another Meeting - Confirm Onboarding" / "I'd Like Another Meeting" → `/pft-ft-decide?token=&decision=confirm|another_meeting` → `automation_PFT_ftresponse`); confirm auto-checks the Accountant Onboarding Preliminary Meeting step as **"Request no meeting"**. **Discovery form** = public `/pft-discovery?token=` (`PftDiscoveryPage.jsx`, SIF-style, all required except "How long have you owned your firm?") → `automation_PFT_loaddiscovery`/`_submitdiscovery`; admin sees a "View discovery form" dropdown under the Meeting 2 step. **Notifications:** discovery completed / 4-day-not-done → assigned PF; FT response (either button) + VFO Associate pick → **assigned PF + Rachael** (`rhopson@elitert.com`); FT 4-day no-response → PF only. PF routing via name→email map (Evan `eanderson@`, Bridger `bsilvester@`, Ian `iwelham@`); falls back to all-admins if no Assigned PF set. **Reminders** (cron `pft-sweep-daily` 08:00 UTC): discovery 2-day reminder email to accountant + 4-day PF notice; FT 2-day reminder email (`PFT_decision_vfo_ft_reminder`) + 4-day PF notice. **Accountant Onboarding** gained an **Accountant Type** field on "+ New Onboarding" (VFO FT / VFO Associate) — associates **skip Stages 1 & 2** (no agreement/payment), go straight to Stage 3 (the `create-member` `invoice_sent_at` gate is bypassed for `accountant_type='VFO Associate'`); new `accountant_onboarding.accountant_type` column + `prelim_meeting_status` value "Request no meeting". **Onboarding notifications now deep-link** to the specific record via `?onboarding=<id>` (AccountantOnboarding + AdvisorOnboarding now read it; Specialist already did) — applied to PFT, ceo-countersign, sweep, and client-decision links for accountant + advisor. "Stage N -" prefix removed from the 3 stage titles + list-row pills in Accountant + Advisor onboarding. New skeleton `PFTTrackSkeleton`. `pipeline_sandbox_config` has a `PARTNERSHIP_FAST_TRACK` row (`sandbox_mode=true`, sandbox_email `jlatham@elitert.com`). 8 email templates (pipeline `PARTNERSHIP_FAST_TRACK`) + listed in the Email Templates tab. New routes `/pft-ft-decide`, `/pft-discovery`. See [docs/flows/partnership-fast-track.md](partnership-fast-track.md).
